allMergedFindings.title: ~21 debug visualization branches compiled into the production globe fragment shader (not pragma-stripped)
allMergedFindings.observation: fragmentMain (GlobeTerrain.wgsl:2576-3756) contains ~21 debug branches gated on `tile.time > X.5e9` (e.g. lines 2647, 2663, 2677, 2693, 2708, 2723, 3116, 3122) that sample textures, compute derivatives, and force mip levels. In production, `tile.time` is the ocean-wave clock `secs % 1e6` (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:569, always < 1e6); the debug sentinels (>1e9) are only written when `getActiveDebugSentinel()` returns non-null. But `getActiveDebugSentinel()` (WebGPUGlobeFragmentDebug.ts:184) is a plain function that returns null in production — it is NOT inside a `//>>includeStart('debug')` pragma block, so the call site at WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:580 is also live, and the WGSL branches are NOT wrapped in any `//>>ifdef` directive. Result: all 21 branches are emitted into the compiled production WGSL of the single hottest shader in the engine. They are never taken at runtime, but they cost shader compile time, increase module size, and add register/uniform pressure (every `tile.layers[i]` / `useWebMercatorTLayer[]` they reference must stay live).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's GlobeFS debug visualizations (wireframe, LOD, etc.) are behind `#ifdef` defines and stripped from the compiled shader in production. The fork already has the `//>>ifdef`/`WebGPUShaderPreprocessor` machinery (used for GEODETIC_NORMAL, LOG_DEPTH, MATERIAL_APPLY in this very file) to do the same.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Wrap the 21 `tile.time > *e9` debug blocks in a `//>>ifdef GLOBE_FRAGMENT_DEBUG` preprocessor region (add the bit to ShaderDefine, add-only) and only set the define when a debug mode is active, OR at minimum hoist them behind a single `if (tile.time > 1e9) { ... }` outer guard so the compiler can prove the whole region dead in the common case. Also wrap `getActiveDebugSentinel()`'s call site in WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:580 in `//>>includeStart('debug')` per the project's logging-pragma rule.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Two of the finding's load-bearing claims are factually wrong, and the remaining true claim describes a deliberately-documented design, not a defect. (1) FALSE call-site claim: the finding asserts the getActiveDebugSentinel() call at WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:580 is 'NOT inside a //>>includeStart(debug) pragma block, so the call site is also live.' I read lines 572-584: the call IS wrapped in //>>includeStart('debug', pragmas.debug) ... //>>includeEnd('debug'). The writer IS stripped from production. (2) The factual core — ~21 `tile.time > N.5e9` branches exist in WGSL with no //>>ifdef guard — is TRUE (verified 21 guards via grep at lines 2619-3740). But DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md:586 documents this EXACT design as intentional: 'The JS write should be inside //>>includeStart(debug,...) so the writer is stripped — the branch itself stays in the shader but is dead code in production (cost: one comparison per pixel).' The branch guard is `tile.time > 1e9` and production `tile.time = secs % 1e6` (verified WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:569), so every branch is provably never taken — the GPU shader compiler folds the constant-false comparisons, and modern WGSL→SPIR-V/MSL/HLSL compilers DCE the unreachable bodies, so the 'register/uniform pressure' claim is largely unfounded (the referenced uniforms are already live for the production composite). The finding's recommendation (wrap in //>>ifdef GLOBE_FRAGMENT_DEBUG) directly contradicts the documented rationale (keep branch, strip writer) and would break the runtime-toggleable CesiumDebug.globeFragmentDebug() debugging workflow that DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md:710-794 and 6+ probes depend on — switching to a compile-time define means rebuilding the shader to change modes. Severity drops to low: a defensible micro-optimization suggestion (single outer `if (tile.time > 1e9)` guard) exists but the framing as a high-severity unaddressed code-quality defect with a false pragma claim is not accurate.

allMergedFindings.title: Eager dual upload + reproject for every Mercator imagery tile vs WebGL's lazy, conditional reproject
allMergedFindings.observation: ImageryLayer.js:631-655 runs `fr.uploadAndReproject(...)` for ANY Mercator-provider tile that has an image, `regardless of whether geographic projection is currently requested`. `uploadAndReprojectMercatorImage` (WebGPUImageryReprojection.ts:365-439) always allocates a full-mip Mercator GPUTexture AND runs a render pass to produce a second full-mip reprojected GPUTexture. So every Mercator imagery tile costs 2 textures (≈2× VRAM) + a reproject render pass + 2 mipmap-generation passes — even for the overwhelmingly common case where the tile is mid-latitude (useWebMercatorT=true) and the geographic variant is never bound. IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:85 acknowledges this is intentional (so bind-group + tile-UB see a consistent dual-texture state from frame 1), but the cost is real and unbounded by tile count.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL (ImageryLayer.js:658-693) only queues the reproject ComputeCommand when `needGeographicProjection && isMercatorProvider` — i.e. lazily, only when a geographic-binding (polar/wide) tile actually demands it. The Mercator source texture is the default; the geographic reprojection is the exception. WebGPU inverts this to eager-always.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Gate the geographic reproject half on demand: upload the Mercator texture eagerly (needed for the common path + consistency), but defer `reprojectWebMercatorWebGPU` until a tile with `useWebMercatorT===false` for this imagery first requests the geographic variant (the `getOrCreateImageryTexture` geographic branch can trigger it on miss). This restores WebGL's lazy semantics and halves steady-state imagery VRAM for typical mid-latitude views without reintroducing the frame-1 inconsistency (the Mercator texture is still eager).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The code behavior is CONFIRMED exactly as described. ImageryLayer.js:631-655 runs fr.uploadAndReproject() for any Mercator-provider tile with an image regardless of needGeographicProjection; uploadAndReprojectMercatorImage (WebGPUImageryReprojection.ts:365-439) always creates the full-mip Mercator texture (397-424) AND runs reprojectWebMercatorWebGPU (429) to produce a second full-mip geographic texture. The WebGL comparison is also accurate: ImageryLayer.js:658-661 gates needsReprojection on `needGeographicProjection && isMercatorProvider`. So the eager-vs-lazy divergence and the ~2x VRAM cost are REAL. However, this is not an undiscovered defect — it is the documented, deliberate Batch 65 architecture. IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:85 and the in-code comment ImageryLayer.js:603-627 both spell out the rationale: the bind-group setup and tile-UB packer iterate passLayers independently inside the renderer and must see a consistent dual-texture state from frame 1 (the lazy single-texture model produced the Batch 56 mercator-data-keyed-as-geographic bug). The finding's own observation acknowledges IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:85. It belongs in this bucket because the cost/tradeoff is already tracked; the proposed lazy-geographic-half optimization is a legitimate FUTURE refinement but reintroduces exactly the frame-1 inconsistency risk the doc was written to eliminate, so it is non-trivial, not a clean win. Severity reduced from high to medium: the VRAM doubling is real but bounded by the imagery tile cache (which has its own eviction), only affects Mercator providers, and the geographic half is reused the moment any polar/wide tile needs it.

allMergedFindings.title: Per-tile, per-pass bind groups recreated every frame with no caching
allMergedFindings.observation: In the per-tile command build (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:877-905) every visible tile, every pass calls `device.createBindGroup` for group0 (camera+tile UB), `_createTextureBindGroup` (group1, 16 textures + sampler), and `_createWaterOceanBindGroup` (group2) — all freshly allocated. `_createTextureBindGroup` (1302-1369) additionally allocates a `textureViews` scratch array per call. A grep of the renderer shows no bind-group cache (`_bindGroupCache`/`getBindGroup`/`reuseBindGroup` all absent). For a globe with hundreds of visible tiles this is 3-4 bind-group object allocations × tiles × passes × frames, plus the GC churn of the scratch arrays. The UB content changes each frame (camera) so group0 must be rebuilt, but group1 (imagery texture views) is stable as long as the tile's ready imagery set is unchanged, and group2 (water/ocean) is near-static.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no bind-group concept; uniform/texture binding is per-draw state-setting with no per-tile heap allocation, so this is a port-introduced allocation pattern with no WebGL analog. WebGPU best practice (and the fork's own bind-group-cache infra elsewhere) is to key bind groups by their resource set and reuse.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Cache group1/group2 bind groups keyed by (tile id, imagery-set revision) / (waterMaskTexture id) on the TileGPUResources entry; invalidate when the imagery set or water mask changes. Only group0 (camera UB) needs per-frame rebuild, and even that can use the ring allocator's stable buffer with a per-frame offset (already partly done via writeUniformSlice).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified directly. WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:877-905 allocates bindGroup0 (device.createBindGroup, camera+tile UB), bindGroup1 (_createTextureBindGroup at :899), and bindGroup2 (_createWaterOceanBindGroup at :901) fresh per visible tile per pass. Grepping the file for _bindGroupCache|getBindGroup|reuseBindGroup|WebGPUBindGroupCache|BindGroupCache returns ZERO matches — the globe surface renderer does NOT use the fork's WebGPUBindGroupCache. I checked whether the 2026-04-30 ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE audit already covers this: line 131 says 'globe terrain hot paths deduplicated' but cross-referencing line 94 shows that refers specifically to WebGPUEffectsBindGroup (group3, the effects/shadow/clipping bind group), which DID get an effectsBgCache in Batch 55. Groups 0/1/2 in WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer are NOT covered by that fix and are not separately called out in the audit. So this is a real, currently-undocumented allocation hot path: ~3 createBindGroup + a textureViews scratch array (_createTextureBindGroup at 1302-1369) per tile per pass per frame. group0 legitimately must rebuild per frame (camera UB content changes), but group1 (stable while the tile's ready imagery set is unchanged) and group2 (near-static water/ocean) are cacheable by resource identity, matching the established Batch 55 pattern. The WebGL 'no analog' framing is correct — this is a port-introduced GC/driver-allocation pattern. Severity medium is appropriate: hundreds of tiles x passes x 60Hz of avoidable allocations, but it is steady-state churn (perf, not correctness) and the effects-bind-group precedent makes the fix mechanical.

allMergedFindings.title: GlobeDepth depth-copy uses a hand-rolled RGBA pack divergent from the canonical csm_packDepth
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUGlobeDepth.ts:62-66 (and the MSAA variant at 113) pack float depth as `r=floor(d*255)/255; g=floor((d-r)*65025)/255; b=floor((d-r-g/255)*16581375)/255; a=1` — a bespoke 3-channel floor-based scheme. The repo already ships the canonical `csm_packDepth.wgsl` (`fract(depth * vec4(1,255,65025,16581375))`, 4-channel) which is the exact WGSL mirror of GLSL `czm_packDepth`/`czm_unpackDepth`. Any consumer that unpacks this texture with `csm_unpackDepth` (dot with vec4(1, 1/255, 1/65025, 1/16581375)) will mis-decode the GlobeDepth copy because the encodings differ (floor vs fract, missing the channel-0 `1.0*depth` term, /255 vs raw). Two depth-pack conventions coexisting in one renderer is a latent correctness + maintenance hazard.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL GlobeDepth packs/unpacks with the single canonical `czm_packDepth`/`czm_unpackDepth` pair so any depth consumer (terrain clamping, pickPosition, 3D Tiles classification) decodes consistently.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Replace the inline pack in DEPTH_COPY_WGSL / DEPTH_COPY_MSAA_WGSL with the shared `csm_packDepth` chunk so the WebGPU GlobeDepth color copy is byte-compatible with `csm_unpackDepth` and the WebGL convention. If nothing currently unpacks this copy (WebGPU samples texture_depth_2d directly per the file docstring), confirm and consider whether the packed-copy target is needed at all; if retained for cross-backend consumers, it MUST match the canonical format.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The finding's central correctness claim is mathematically WRONG. It asserts: 'Any consumer that unpacks this texture with csm_unpackDepth (dot with vec4(1, 1/255, 1/65025, 1/16581375)) will mis-decode the GlobeDepth copy because the encodings differ.' I traced the actual producer/consumer pair and numerically verified the round-trip. Producer (WebGPUGlobeDepth.ts:63-66): r=floor(d*255)/255, g=floor((d-r)*65025)/255, b=floor((d-r-g/255)*16581375)/255, a=1. Consumer: I followed the packed output — globeDepthTexture (WebGPUGlobeDepth.ts:198) is published as context._globeDepthTexture/_globeDepthView (WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:366-376) and is actually sampled+unpacked by WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js:1101-1102 and WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js:571 via unpackDepth() at GroundPrimitiveRenderer:873, which is EXACTLY the canonical dot(packed, vec4(1, 1/255, 1/65025, 1/16581375)) == czm_unpackDepth. I ran a node round-trip over 1,000,001 depth values: max abs error of canonical-unpack(producer-pack(d)) vs d is 6.03e-8 — i.e. ONE part in 16.5 million, entirely from the benign a=1 constant term (1/16581375 = 6.03e-8). The producer's floor-based 3-channel split and the canonical fract-based csm_packDepth are two algebraically-equivalent factorizations of the same byte-split; the floor pack telescopes back through the canonical dot product correctly. So the GlobeDepth copy is NOT mis-decoded by csm_unpackDepth — the real consumers decode it correctly, confirming the format is compatible, not divergent. The only true residue is a code-quality/DRY nit (an inline pack instead of importing the csm_packDepth chunk, and a stale producer-format comment at GroundPrimitiveRenderer:870 that describes the canonical pack rather than the floor pack while still being numerically equivalent). The finding's claimed correctness/parity hazard does not exist.

allMergedFindings.title: WGSL ocean shader ships unrequested visual enhancements that diverge from WebGL behavior

Under the parity contract WebGPU should mirror WebGL behavior; these are gratuitous algorithm divergences (not backend-forced).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either (a) back-match the WGSL to WebGL's 2-octave + czm_getSpecular + no-foam so the two backends render identically (preferred for the parity contract), or (b) if the enhancements are desired, port them to WebGL too so both backends stay in lockstep. The unused `computeSubsurfaceScattering` is confirmed scaffolding (item 7) — leave it. Low severity because it's gated on `showWaterEffect` (default false) so default scenes are unaffected.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Confirmed and explicitly documented in-code. GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3217-3234 enumerates exactly the four divergences the finding lists: item 4 (3-octave WGSL waves vs WebGL 2-octave czm_getWaterNoise), item 5 (GGX distributionGGX vs WebGL czm_getSpecular Phong), item 6 (computeFoam whitecaps, WGSL-only), item 7 (computeSubsurfaceScattering defined-but-unused — flagged as scaffolding). allMergedFindings.title: uploadImageSource swallows all errors and returns null, masking real upload failures
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts:378-380 wraps the entire createTexture + copyExternalImageToTexture + mipmap-generate body in `catch (e) { return null; }` with no logging at all — not even a pragma-stripped diagnostic. A genuine failure (device lost mid-upload, format/size validation error, mipmap generator throwing) is indistinguishable from a benign cache-miss-retry, and the caller (_createTextureBindGroup) silently substitutes the placeholder view, so the tile renders blank with zero console signal. CLAUDE.md's logging rules require real errors (device lost, pipeline/copy failures) to reach the console unwrapped.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's texImage2D/generateMipmap failures surface as GL errors / console warnings via the Context error path; a silent texture upload failure that blanks a tile with no log is a port regression in observability.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Distinguish expected transient failures (undecoded HTMLImageElement — already handled by the early `return null` at line 304) from unexpected ones. In the catch, emit a non-pragma `console.error` with the cacheKey + error for the unexpected case (it indicates broken output), or re-throw device-lost. At minimum add a pragma-stripped `console.warn` so debug builds see the cause.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified directly at WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts:378-380: the entire createTexture + copyExternalImageToTexture + generateMipmaps body (322-377) is wrapped in `} catch (e) { return null; }` with no logging at all — not even a pragma-stripped diagnostic. The caller getOrCreateImageryTexture treats null as a benign cache miss (line 214: `if (!uploaded) return null;`) and the tile then renders with the placeholder, so a genuine device-lost / format-validation / mipmap-generator failure is indistinguishable from the expected transient case and produces zero console signal — a blank tile. This violates the CLAUDE.md logging rule that real errors producing broken output (device lost, copy/pipeline failures) must reach the console unwrapped. The finding correctly notes the legitimate transient case (undecoded HTMLImageElement) is already handled separately by the early `return null` at line 304, so the catch can safely distinguish unexpected failures. The WebGL observability comparison is fair: GL upload failures surface via the context error path. This is a real, actionable observability regression. Severity medium is appropriate — it does not by itself break rendering, but it blinds diagnosis of a class of real failures. Recommended minimal fix matches the codebase convention: a non-pragma console.error (or re-throw on device-lost) in the catch for the unexpected case.

allMergedFindings.title: Precision-stable ray-sphere intersection is a clean back-port candidate for WebGL2
allMergedFindings.observation: GlobeTerrain.wgsl:837-853 reformulates ray-sphere intersection by scaling the origin by 1/radius before the dot products, keeping all intermediates in [-10,10] where f32 precision is ~1e-6, instead of the naive `c = dot(origin,origin) - radius*radius` which loses ~10m at Cesium camera scale (1.6e7² = 2.56e14, past f32's 24-bit mantissa). The author's own comment (lines 820-833) notes WebGL's `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval` has the identical imprecision and only survives because it switches to per-fragment math at orbit.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval` (Builtin/Functions) uses the naive un-scaled formulation and carries the same precision loss. The WGSL fix is algorithmically backend-neutral and trivially translatable to GLSL.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Port the 1/radius-scaled formulation into `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval.glsl`. It's a ~5-line change, costs one extra divide + multiply, is a strict precision improvement, and benefits sky-atmosphere LUT, volumetric clouds, and any other ray-sphere consumer on WebGL. Feasibility: high — pure math, no API surface change, covered by existing atmosphere visual-regression probes.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified as an accurate, actionable backport candidate. GlobeTerrain.wgsl:837-853 implements raySphereIntersectionInterval by scaling origin by 1/radius (invR at 842, originScaled at 843) so c = dot(originScaled,originScaled) - 1.0 (845) keeps intermediates in [-10,10] instead of the naive dot(origin,origin) - radius*radius which at 1.6e7 m loses ~10m past f32's 24-bit mantissa. The author's own comment (820-833) AND IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:94 both confirm WebGL's czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval carries the identical imprecision and only survives via the per-fragment ground-atmosphere switch at orbit. The math is genuinely backend-neutral (pure algebra, one extra divide+multiply, no API change) and would benefit sky-atmosphere LUT, volumetric clouds, and other GLSL ray-sphere consumers. This is correctly scoped as a low-severity opportunity (improvement, not a bug — WebGL renders correctly today), and the existing atmosphere visual-regression probes provide coverage. Note: this is documented as a WGSL fix in IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:94 but the GLSL back-port itself is NOT tracked anywhere I found, so flagging it as the next work item is appropriate per CLAUDE.md Principle 9. Severity low confirmed.

allMergedFindings.title: useWebMercatorT graceful-downgrade fallbacks can bind a texture that mismatches the cached translation/scale space
allMergedFindings.observation: getOrCreateImageryTexture (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts:120-220) has race-window fallbacks: 'want geographic, only have merc → bind merc and flip isMercator=true' (177-187) and 'want merc, no merc, have reprojected → bind reprojected' (153-160). It returns `isMercator` so the caller can track the binding. BUT the tile-UB packer (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:157-161) independently computes `effectiveUseWebMercatorT = tileImagery.useWebMercatorT && hasMercatorTexture` from the imagery object — it does NOT consult the `isMercator` value the texture cache actually returned. The texture bind group (group1) and the `useWebMercatorTLayer` flag (group0 tile UB) are produced by two separate code paths (`_createTextureBindGroup` vs `createTileUniformBuffer`) that can disagree in the race window: e.g. want-geographic + only-merc-present → cache binds merc (isMercator=true) but the UB sees `useWebMercatorT===false` so writes flag=0, telling the shader to sample geographic-V on a Mercator texture. The cached translationAndScale is geographic-space, compounding the mismatch. The doc (IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:86) explicitly says the flag MUST track the binding decision, but the two paths derive it independently.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL (GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1492-1515) selects the texture and the matching `useWebMercatorT` uniform from the same `tileImagery.useWebMercatorT` value in one place, so binding and flag cannot diverge.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Make the tile-UB flag follow the cache's actual `isMercator` return rather than recomputing it. Easiest: have `_createTextureBindGroup` record the per-layer `isMercator` results and pass them into `createTileUniformBuffer` (or fold both into one pass over passLayers) so group0 and group1 are guaranteed consistent. The eager-dual-upload (Finding 2) makes this race rare in practice, but the two-source-of-truth structure is fragile and will resurface if the eager upload is ever made lazy.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the two-source-of-truth structure is real. getOrCreateImageryTexture (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts:120-220) returns {view, isMercator} and has the exact race fallbacks described: want-geographic but only mercator present → binds mercator and returns isMercator:true (lines 177-187), and want-mercator-none-have-reprojected → binds reprojected isMercator:false (153-160 fall-through). The tile-UB packer (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts:157-161) INDEPENDENTLY computes effectiveUseWebMercatorT = tileImagery.useWebMercatorT && hasMercatorTexture — it does NOT consult the isMercator value the cache returned. In the want-geographic+only-merc fallback, useWebMercatorT===false so the UB writes flag=0 (geographic-V sampling) while the cache actually bound the Mercator texture (isMercator:true), and the cached translationAndScale is geographic-space — a genuine binding/flag/UV-space three-way mismatch. The doc proves the bug: IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:87 states the formula as `useWebMercatorTLayer[i] = (tileImagery.useWebMercatorT && !!imagery._webgpuMercatorTexture)` and CLAIMS it 'Tracks what the cache will actually bind' — but that claim is only true on the happy path; it is wrong precisely in the cache's own documented fallback branches. So the doc describes the intended invariant (flag must track binding, IMAGERY_PROJECTION.md:86) but the code derives it from a second source that diverges in the race window — this is a confirmed latent correctness bug, not merely documented. The finding correctly notes the eager-dual-upload (Finding 2) makes the race rare in practice (both textures usually exist by bind time), which is why severity medium (not high) is right. The fix — thread the cache's isMercator back into the UB flag — is sound and matches the doc's stated invariant.

allMergedFindings.title: computeModifiedModelView allocates two Float64Array(16) per tile per frame
allMergedFindings.observation: computeModifiedModelView (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:803-819) does `new Float64Array(view)` on the no-center path (809) and `new Float64Array(16)` on the center path (811), returning a fresh array every call. It is invoked once per tile per frame from createCameraUniformBuffer:214 (and again for wireframe). For a few-hundred-tile globe that's hundreds of 128-byte Float64Array allocations per frame purely as transient scratch, feeding straight into `m4Values`/the UB pack. The module already uses module-level scratch (swCarto, projectedTileRect, etc.) for the 2D path, so the pattern for fixing this is established right there.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's equivalent (GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js modifiedModelView scratch) reuses a module-level Matrix4 scratch — no per-tile allocation.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add a module-level `_modifiedViewScratch = new Float64Array(16)` and write into it instead of allocating, matching the existing scratch convention in this file. The result is consumed synchronously by `m4Values` before the next call, so a single shared scratch is safe (the packer is single-threaded per frame, as the file's own comment at line 60 notes).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. computeModifiedModelView (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:803-819) returns `new Float64Array(view)` on the no-center path (809) and `new Float64Array(16)` on the center path (811) — a fresh 128-byte array every call. It is invoked from createCameraUniformBuffer at line 214 (the main per-tile camera UB build) and createCameraUniformBuffer is called per-tile from WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:856 (main tile loop) plus :1626 (wireframe), confirming per-tile-per-frame invocation. The result is consumed synchronously by m4Values(modifiedView) at line 215 before the next call, so a single module-level scratch is safe — and the file already establishes that convention (host._cameraMvpScratch is used two lines later at 222, and the module uses swCarto/projectedTileRect scratches per the finding). The WebGL comparison (reused module-level Matrix4 scratch) is accurate. This is a real, low-cost-to-fix port-introduced allocation. I confirmed it is NOT tracked as a perf item in DEFERRED_WORK or the 2026-04-30 audit (the only computeModifiedModelView doc hits are about the center-offset/morph-splay correctness bugs, DP-M8 and the morph fix, not allocation). Severity low is correct — it is GC churn, not correctness, and dwarfed by the bind-group allocations in Finding 3, but it is a clean trivial fix matching the file's own scratch pattern.

allMergedFindings.title: Gaussian splats render in buffer order — CPU back-to-front sort (primitive._indexes) is silently dropped
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1037-1057, 281-291, 412-455; GaussianSplatPrimitive.js:1183-1192, 2071-2102
allMergedFindings.observation: The WebGPU splat renderer builds its draw command with `instanceCount: cache.splatCount` (WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1043) and reads splat instance data directly from the loader buffer in storage order (cache.splatBuffer, vertex layout SPLAT_VERTEX_BUFFERS at :412). It never reads `primitive._indexes`. The WebGL GaussianSplatPrimitive computes a per-frame, camera-driven back-to-front sort via GaussianSplatSorter and a full re-sort state machine (GaussianSplatPrimitive.js:64-181, 725), then draws with `instanceCount = primitive._indexes.length` using the *sorted* index array as an instance attribute (`idxAttr.typedArray = primitive._indexes`, :2098; `renderResources.instanceCount = primitive._indexes.length`, :2071-2074). GaussianSplatPrimitive.update() routes to the WebGPU feature renderer and `return`s at :1191 — BEFORE the entire sort state machine runs — so on WebGPU no sort ever executes. The renderer's own comment admits it (WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:286-291: 'there is NO per-frame sort/compaction at this layer'). Because splats use premultiplied over-blending (srcFactor 'one' / dstFactor 'one-minus-src-alpha', :518), unsorted draw order produces incorrect color where splats overlap in depth — visible as wrong tinting/haloing that changes with camera angle.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: see above
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Consume `primitive._indexes` in the WebGPU renderer: either (a) upload the sorted index array as a per-instance attribute / storage buffer and index splat reads through it (mirror the WebGL instance-attribute approach), or (b) implement the GPU radix sort that FEATURE_INVENTORY line 1001 already earmarks and feed its output buffer into a drawIndirect. Until then, at minimum let the CPU sort run (don't early-return before it) and re-upload `_splatData` in sorted order on each re-sort. Also fix DEFERRED_WORK line 637 which incorrectly implies sorting is in place on WebGPU.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified in code. WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1043 draws with instanceCount: cache.splatCount and reads splat instance data directly from cache.splatBuffer in storage order (built from _splatData at :900-913, SPLAT_VERTEX_BUFFERS at :412 is a plain instance-stride layout). It never consumes primitive._indexes. The renderer's own comment (:286-291) confirms 'there is NO per-frame sort/compaction at this layer.' GaussianSplatPrimitive.update() returns at JS line 1191 after routing to the feature renderer, BEFORE the WebGL sort state machine. The WebGL path uses the sorted _indexes array as a per-instance attribute (_SPLAT_INDEXES, instanceDivisor=1, instanceCount = _indexes.length; GaussianSplatPrimitive.js:2071-2102). The blend is genuinely order-dependent premultiplied over-blend (srcFactor 'one' / dstFactor 'one-minus-src-alpha', :518-519, depthWriteEnabled:false :526), so unsorted draw order yields incorrect compositing where splats overlap. The missing GPU radix sort is tracked as FUTURE (FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:1001, BACKLOG-§11), but the resulting visual parity drift is NOT documented as a known artifact, and DEFERRED_WORK.md:637 actively misstates 'Per-splat prev-position follows current sort permutation' (implies a sort exists). One caveat narrowing impact: an OIT (weighted-sum, order-independent) pipeline variant exists (cache.oitPipeline) and is attached when available; if the splat pass runs through OIT, order-dependence is mitigated — but the default color pipeline is the order-dependent over-blend, so the drift is real in the common path. Finding's evidence lines all check out.

allMergedFindings.title: PointCloudLOD.wgsl computeMain: slot-255 offset broadcast clobbers a compacted index when a workgroup is fully visible
allMergedFindings.evidence: PointCloudLOD.wgsl:130-164 (esp. :150-156), :257-271
allMergedFindings.observation: After per-workgroup compaction, `sharedVisible[localSlot]` holds compacted point indices in slots [0..localCount). Lane 0 then writes the global offset into the SAME shared array at slot 255 to broadcast it (`sharedVisible[255u] = globalOffset;` :152), with the comment 'safe because localCount < 256'. But localCount can equal 256 — every one of the 256 threads in a workgroup can be visible (LOD 0 keeps all points, frustum fully inside). When localCount == 256, the compacted index for the point at slot 255 is overwritten by globalOffset; then the writeback `visibleIndices[baseOffset + 255] = sharedVisible[255]` writes the offset value (a small integer) as if it were a point index. Result: one wrong/duplicate point index per fully-visible workgroup, and one genuine visible point dropped. The subgroup variant (:261) has the identical pattern.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL point clouds have no per-point GPU compaction (tile-level LOD only), so there is no analogous code; this is a NEW WebGPU compute path, but the bug makes its output diverge from a correct compaction.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Use a dedicated workgroup scalar (a separate `var<workgroup> wgOffset: u32;`) for the broadcast instead of reusing sharedVisible[255], or size sharedVisible to 257 and broadcast via slot 256. The off-by-one is invisible in sparse/decimated frames (localCount<256) which is why baselines miss it — it only triggers on dense LOD-0 workgroups.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. sharedVisible is array<u32, 256> (:51), workgroup_size is 256 (:84). At LOD 0, shouldKeepAtLOD returns true for ALL points (:78), so if all 256 threads in a workgroup pass frustumTest at LOD-0 distance, localCount == 256 and the compacted indices fill slots 0..255 (atomicAdd compaction :130-133). Lane 0 then writes sharedVisible[255u] = globalOffset (:152) with the comment 'safe because localCount < 256' — but localCount CAN equal 256, in which case slot 255 still holds a real compacted point index that gets clobbered. The writeback loop (:158-163) executes for lid.x < localCount (i.e. lid.x up to 255), reading sharedVisible[lid.x]; at lid.x==255 it now reads globalOffset (a small integer) and writes it as a point index. Net: one duplicated/wrong index and one genuine visible point dropped per fully-visible LOD-0 workgroup. The subgroup variant has the identical pattern (:261, :265-269). The bug only triggers on dense LOD-0 workgroups (localCount==256), which is why sparse/decimated baselines miss it. The recommended fixes (dedicated var<workgroup> wgOffset, or size to 257) are correct. Not documented anywhere. NOTE: this matters only when the GPU LOD path is actually exercised (opt-in / gated), so live exposure depends on wiring, but the off-by-one is a genuine correctness defect in the compute path.

allMergedFindings.title: DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl relies on inter-workgroup forward progress + device-scope visibility that WebGPU does not guarantee
allMergedFindings.evidence: DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl:155-179; WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts:138-153, 644-688
allMergedFindings.observation: The scan's lane-0 lookback spins on `partitions[lookback]` until its flag != EMPTY (:161-170), using `storageBarrier()` inside the spin loop. WebGPU's memory model provides NO forward-progress guarantee between workgroups and no device-scoped barrier — `storageBarrier()` only orders memory for the *calling* workgroup, it does not make another workgroup's `atomicStore` visible nor force it to be scheduled. If the predecessor workgroup is not co-resident (common when grid size exceeds the GPU's occupancy), the spin can livelock/deadlock or read stale state. This is the well-documented reason single-pass decoupled-lookback is considered unsafe in portable WebGPU. The processor wires this as the `useDecoupledScan` opt-in path for 'deterministic ordering' (WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts:138-153) used by GPU-driven picking / multi-view selection.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL equivalent (transform-feedback compaction isn't used here). The default atomic-add path (useDecoupledScan:false) is correct; only the opt-in deterministic path is fragile.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either gate this path behind a documented device-capability/occupancy check, or replace it with a safe two-pass (reduce + downsweep) scan that needs no inter-workgroup spin — the docstring at the top of the shader even notes the two-pass approach is what this replaces. The ~20-30% asymptotic win does not justify a potential GPU hang. At minimum add a permanent watchdog/iteration cap in the spin loop and surface a console.error sentinel (CLAUDE.md logging rule) if it trips.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. The lane-0 lookback spins on partitions[lookback] in a loop{} until partitionFlag != FLAG_EMPTY (:161-170), using storageBarrier() inside the spin. This is the textbook decoupled-lookback pattern (docstring credits Merrill & Garland 2016 / Vello), which requires inter-workgroup forward-progress and device-scope atomic visibility. WebGPU's memory model guarantees NEITHER: storageBarrier() only orders memory for the calling workgroup and does not force another workgroup to be scheduled or make its atomicStore globally visible. If the predecessor workgroup is not co-resident (grid > occupancy), the spin can livelock. There is NO iteration cap / watchdog / console.error sentinel in the loop, violating the CLAUDE.md infinite-loop-guard rule. Confirmed it is opt-in: WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor defaults useDecoupledScan to false (:245), and WebGPUContext wires it from useDeterministicPointCloudLOD ?? false (:4702-4703). So the default atomic-add path is safe and only the opt-in 'deterministic' path is fragile, justifying medium not high. The forward-progress hazard itself is NOT documented (docs only track FEAT-SURVEY-06 consumer-wiring status, not the livelock risk). Recommendation (gate behind capability check, or switch to safe two-pass scan, or add iteration-cap watchdog + sentinel) is sound.

allMergedFindings.title: GPU LOD point-cloud path creates its own command encoder and queue.submit per primitive per frame, and hardcodes Pass.OPAQUE
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts:1677-1702 (encoder+submit), :1725 (Pass.OPAQUE)
allMergedFindings.observation: Two issues in `_runGPULODPath`: (1) It allocates a fresh `device.createCommandEncoder()` and does a standalone `device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()])` (:1678, :1702) for the LOD compute dispatch + visibleCount->indirect copy, for EACH point cloud, EVERY frame. This forces a separate submit that serializes against the main scene encoder and adds per-primitive CPU+driver overhead; the dispatch should be recorded into the frame's shared compute/scene encoder instead. (2) The resulting color command is pinned to `pass: Pass.OPAQUE` (:1725) regardless of the point cloud's translucency. Translucent point clouds (per-point alpha, common for colored LiDAR) would be drawn in the opaque pass with wrong blend/depth-write semantics on the LOD fast path.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL PointCloud selects its pass from the primitive's translucency (TRANSLUCENT vs OPAQUE) and records into the shared command stream — no per-primitive submit.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Record the LOD compute pass + buffer copy into the frame's existing command encoder (the one the scene renderer submits once) rather than a private encoder+submit. Derive the draw command's Pass from the point cloud's translucency (match the default non-LOD path's pass selection) instead of hardcoding OPAQUE.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Two sub-claims; verdict split. (1) CONFIRMED: _runGPULODPath creates a fresh device.createCommandEncoder() (:1678) and does a standalone device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]) (:1702) for the LOD compute dispatch + visibleCount->indirect copy, per point cloud per frame. This is genuinely LOD-path-specific (the default color path at :1359-1367 pushes a WebGPUDrawCommand into the shared command list, no private submit) and is a real per-primitive CPU/driver overhead + serialization concern. Not documented. (2) FALSE PREMISE: the finding claims the LOD path 'hardcodes Pass.OPAQUE ... regardless of translucency' and recommends matching 'the default non-LOD path's pass selection.' But the default WebGPU PointCloud path ALSO hardcodes pass: Pass.OPAQUE (:1366), as does the velocity command (:1533, :1919). So the Pass.OPAQUE pinning is a pre-existing renderer-wide property, NOT a LOD-vs-default divergence — there is no per-translucency pass selection on the WebGPU side to match. The webglComparison (WebGL selects pass from translucency) may hold for WebGL, but the recommendation as written is based on a non-existent WebGPU default behavior. Severity adjusted to medium because only the encoder/submit half is actionable as described; the translucency-pass half is mis-framed (it's a separate, broader gap if it matters at all).

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher allocates two Uint32Arrays sized to capacity on every sort() call
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher.ts:78-89, 291-313
allMergedFindings.observation: `_uploadInputs` allocates `new Uint32Array(r.capacity)` twice (keys + indices) per sort (:300-301) and rebuilds the sortable-uint keys + identity indices in JS each call. For a power-of-two-padded million-point cloud that is two ~4MB allocations every sort, plus a per-element JS DataView round-trip in `floatToSortableUint` (:78-89, allocates a 4-byte ArrayBuffer+DataView PER element). The class otherwise carefully reuses `_paramsScratch` to avoid GC (:132). Note: this dispatcher does not appear to be consumed by WebGPUPointCloudRenderer (no reference found), so live impact may be nil today — but if/when it is wired, this is a hot-path GC and CPU hazard.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — GPU sort is WebGPU-specific infrastructure; the WebGL/WASM fallback (WasmPointCloudBridge.sortByDistance) does the equivalent natively.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Hoist the keys/indices scratch arrays to instance fields grown with capacity (like the LOD processor's _ensurePositionBuffers). Replace the per-element DataView in floatToSortableUint with a single reused Float32Array/Uint32Array aliasing view. Also confirm whether this dispatcher is still reachable or is dead scaffolding (cross-ref the backlog before removing).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. _uploadInputs allocates new Uint32Array(r.capacity) twice (keys + indices, :300-301) and rebuilds keys/identity-indices in JS every call. floatToSortableUint allocates a new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4)) PER element (:80) — a per-point heap allocation in the hot key-build loop. The class otherwise carefully reuses _paramsScratch (:132, written in-place :321-324) to avoid GC, making these two allocation sites an inconsistent hot-path hazard. The finding's own caveat is accurate and important: this dispatcher is NOT consumed by WebGPUPointCloudRenderer directly. It IS instantiated and .sort()-called via the POINT_CLOUD_SORT feature-renderer registry in WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts:382-397, but that path is gated by WasmPointCloudBridge.useGPUSort (default false, per the :380-382 comment), so live impact is effectively nil today. Real GC/CPU hazard only if/when the GPU-sort path is enabled. Recommendation (hoist scratch arrays to instance fields, replace per-element DataView with a single reused aliasing view) is correct. Severity low is right given the current inert state.

allMergedFindings.title: LOD distance bands and screen-space density inputs are coarse/unused vs WebGL's geometric-error SSE
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts:1667-1691; PointCloudLOD.wgsl:34-37 (declared) vs :84-165 (never read)
allMergedFindings.observation: The LOD bands are hardcoded fractions of the camera far plane (lod0=far*0.1, lod1=far*0.25, lod2=far*0.5, lod3=far; WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts:1672-1675), and `screenSpaceRadius` is passed as a constant 1.0 (:1690). The shader carries `screenSpaceRadius` and `geometricError` in LODParams but neither is actually used in the visibility decision (PointCloudLOD.wgsl reads only distance bands; screenSpaceRadius/geometricError are declared but never referenced in computeMain). So the 'screen-space density decimation' the module docstring advertises is not implemented, and LOD selection ignores the tile's geometric error that WebGL's getScreenSpaceError centers its decision on. This is a NEW within-tile enhancement (not a strict port), but the unused params are misleading and the far-fraction heuristic will over- or under-decimate depending on FOV/viewport.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL uses per-tile geometricError + screen-space-error against the viewport to drive tile-level LOD; this within-tile pass approximates with fixed far-distance fractions and no SSE.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either implement the screen-space spacing term in the shader (project point spacing to pixels using viewport + projection and decimate to screenSpaceRadius) and feed geometricError into the band thresholds, or remove the unused LODParams fields and downgrade the docstring claim. Don't ship struct fields the shader silently ignores — it invites the next reader to assume they work.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. LOD bands are hardcoded far-plane fractions (lod0=far*0.1, lod1=far*0.25, lod2=far*0.5, lod3=far; WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts:1672-1675) and screenSpaceRadius is passed as constant 1.0 (:1690). In the shader, screenSpaceRadius and geometricError appear ONLY in the LODParams struct declaration (PointCloudLOD.wgsl:36-37) and are NEVER referenced in any function body (grep confirms zero other occurrences) — computeMain reads only the distance bands. So the 'Screen-space point spacing -> density decimation' that the module docstring advertises as step 2 (:3-8) is not implemented; only distance-band + index-modulo decimation exists. The two struct fields are dead inputs that mislead the next reader, and the far-fraction heuristic ignores FOV/viewport and per-tile geometric error (which is what WebGL's getScreenSpaceError centers on). This is a NEW within-tile enhancement, not a strict port, so it's a functionality-gap/misleading-fields issue rather than a regression. Severity low is appropriate. Recommendation (implement the SSE term or remove the unused fields + downgrade the docstring) is sound and matches the project's anti-dead-scaffolding posture.

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts is a 2168-LOC undecomposed file with extensive embedded WGSL and per-frame inline cast chains
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts (file length 2168); cast sites :1604-1608, :1877-1882
allMergedFindings.observation: At 2168 lines the file exceeds the project's ~1000-line decomposition guideline. It bundles: the color/pick/velocity WGSL string, the LOD fast path, the velocity (motion-vector) path, frustum-plane extraction, instance-buffer building, and pipeline resolution. It also repeatedly reaches through `context as unknown as { webgpuPipelineCache?: ... }` and `context as unknown as { pointCloudLOD?: ... }` (e.g. :1604-1608, :1877-1882) — backend-internal fields accessed via inline structural casts rather than a typed context surface, which is brittle if those field names change.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — organizational.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Split into WGSL source module(s), a PointCloudLODPath helper, and a PointCloudVelocityPath helper (mirrors how GaussianSplat keeps velocity in a separate function but here it's larger). Introduce a typed accessor (e.g. context.webgpuPipelineCache getter on the WebGPU context's own interface) instead of per-call `as unknown as {...}` casts.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. File is 2168 lines (wc -l), well over the CLAUDE.md ~1000-line decomposition guideline. It bundles the embedded color/pick/velocity WGSL string, the LOD fast path (_runGPULODPath), the velocity/motion-vector path, frustum-plane extraction, instance-buffer building, and pipeline resolution. It reaches through context via inline structural casts: 'context as unknown as { webgpuPipelineCache?: ... }' at :1604-1608 confirmed verbatim, and there are 10 'as unknown as' sites total (grep -c). This is brittle if field names change and bypasses a typed context surface. This is purely organizational (the file is not a perf-critical math class or pure-data/enum, so the CLAUDE.md decomposition exemption does not apply). Severity low is appropriate. Recommendation (split WGSL into a source module + extract LOD/velocity path helpers + introduce a typed accessor instead of per-call casts) aligns with the project's file-size and TS-cast guidance.

allMergedFindings.title: Voxel ray-marcher uses single-precision model-coordinate camera (no RTE) — precision risk if it ever renders real planetary voxel data
allMergedFindings.evidence: VoxelRayMarch.wgsl:6-15, 25-55; FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:514
allMergedFindings.observation: VoxelRayMarch.wgsl carries `cameraPositionMC: vec3<f32>` and an f32 modelViewProjection (:6-15) — a single-precision world/model position with no encodedCameraHigh/Low RTE pair, contrary to the mandatory RTE rule. Ray origin and sample positions are therefore f32 world coordinates. This is currently masked because the voxel renderer is a KNOWN placeholder gradient ray-marcher (FEATURE_INVENTORY line 514, tagged SCAFFOLDED; no provider/megatexture/octree wired). I am NOT flagging the missing octree/megatexture (correctly tracked), only noting that when real voxel rendering lands, this shader's precision model must be upgraded to RTE high/low or planetary-scale voxel volumes will jitter/snap. The renderer file itself imports EncodedCartesian3 but the shader uniform struct does not expose the high/low pair.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL VoxelFS/Megatexture path operates in a precision-managed shape-local space; the WebGPU placeholder collapses to a single f32 MC camera.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: When the voxel data path is implemented, add encodedCameraHigh/Low to VoxelRayMarchUniforms and compute the ray origin via RTE subtraction (the EncodedCartesian3 import is already present in the renderer, so the JS side is half-done). Track as a prerequisite of the real voxel-rendering work item, not a standalone bug.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:514 (WebGPUVoxelRenderer SCAFFOLDED placeholder) + :819 (WGF-4-EXPAND, Voxel camera packer RTE assertions pending)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Code claim verified: VoxelRayMarchUniforms carries cameraPositionMC: vec3<f32> and an f32 modelViewProjection (VoxelRayMarch.wgsl:6-15) with no encodedCameraHigh/Low RTE pair; ray origin + sample positions are f32 model-space (:42). This technically violates the mandatory RTE rule. HOWEVER, as the finding itself states, it is masked because WebGPUVoxelRenderer is a KNOWN placeholder gradient ray-marcher — FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:514 tags it 'SCAFFOLDED — not real voxel data' and notes VoxelPrimitive.update returns early so no traversal/megatexture/octree is wired. There is no real planetary voxel volume for the precision to corrupt today, so it is not an active bug. The forward-looking RTE-upgrade prerequisite is also partly tracked: WGF-4-EXPAND (FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:819) lists 'Voxel' among the camera packers pending RTE assertions, and the LOD-processor-style 'pass cameraHigh+cameraLow, ~20 LOC spike' fix is the standard remedy. The placeholder status (documented) plus the partially-tracked RTE-expand item means this is best classified as already-documented; no actionable standalone bug exists until real voxel rendering lands. Severity none — zero current runtime impact.

allMergedFindings.title: GPU LOD path could be back-ported as a within-tile decimation for WebGL2 point clouds (transform-feedback or instanced index draw)
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts:10-46
allMergedFindings.observation: The within-tile distance+frustum decimation the LOD processor performs (cull millions of points to a visible subset before draw) is a genuine perf win that WebGL2 currently lacks — WebGL2 point clouds draw every loaded point in a tile in full (the processor's own docstring notes this, WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts:10-17). WebGL2 can approximate the same effect with a transform-feedback compaction pass or a precomputed LOD-stride index buffer selected per distance band.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL2: no per-point culling within a tile; draws all loaded points.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Feasible but moderate effort: WebGL2 transform feedback can emit a compacted index stream (the GPU equivalent of the atomic-add path), then an instanced/indexed draw renders only survivors. Lower-effort alternative: precompute Morton-strided index buffers per LOD band on load and bind by distance. Worth tracking as a NEW-* perf item if large monolithic LAS loads are a target use case.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: This is a backport-candidate suggestion, not a defect. Its factual premise is correct and verified against the processor docstring (WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts:12-17): Cesium's WebGL path does tile-level LOD only and draws every loaded point in a tile in full — there is no per-point culling within a tile. The proposed WebGL2 approaches (transform-feedback compaction emitting a compacted index stream, or precomputed Morton-strided per-LOD-band index buffers selected by distance) are technically feasible and a genuine perf win for large monolithic LAS loads. It is discretionary forward-looking work, not an actionable bug, and is not currently tracked as a NEW-* item. Marking confirmed-real in the sense that the opportunity and its premise are accurate; severity low because it is optional enhancement scope, not a correctness or parity regression. Worth filing as a NEW-* perf backlog item only if large non-tiled point-cloud loads are a target use case.

allMergedFindings.title: Specular IBL uses analytic Fresnel approximation instead of WebGL's split-sum BRDF-LUT + multi-scatter; BRDF LUT is generated but never consumed by the model path
allMergedFindings.observation: The forward model FS computes specular IBL as `kS_ibl = fresnelSchlickRoughness(NdotV, F0, roughness); specularIBL = radiance * kS_ibl * iblSpecularFactor` (ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2640, 2698-2702) and diffuse IBL as `irradiance * diffuseColor * iblDiffuseFactor` (2652). There is no BRDF-LUT term and no energy-conservation/multi-scatter term. WebGPUBrdfLutGenerator.ts builds a 256×256 rg32float LUT via a compute pass on every device init (lines 247-323), and WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:177-180 invokes brdfLutGenerator.update each frame, but a grep of ModelPBRComplete.wgsl and WebGPUModelPipelineCache.js shows the LUT is never declared as a binding nor sampled in the model path — it is dead GPU work for models (the only WGSL consumer found is the deferred-lighting path's brdfLutTex). The generator docstring (WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:16-17) explicitly claims 'Specular IBL always uses a prefiltered radiance cubemap combined with the BRDF LUT for the split-sum approximation' — which is false for the forward model path.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl:30-33 and 48-99 sample `texture(czm_brdfLut, vec2(NdotV, roughness)).rg` and apply the full Fdez-Aguera single+multi-scatter model: FssEss = specularWeight*(F*brdfLut.x + brdfLut.y), plus FmsEms multi-scatter energy compensation and dielectricScattering for the diffuse term. WebGPU drops all of this, so metals/rough dielectrics will read brighter/dimmer and lose energy conservation versus WebGL.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Bind the generated BRDF LUT into the model material bind group (a free slot in group 1) and replace the analytic specular-IBL term with the WebGL split-sum: `specular = radiance * (F * brdfLut.x + brdfLut.y) * specularFactor`, and port the FmsEms/dielectricScattering diffuse terms. The LUT and prefiltered cubemap already exist — this is wiring, not new infrastructure. If the LUT is genuinely unwanted for models, delete the generator call from the model IBL update and fix the docstring.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified at the code level. ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2640,2702 computes specularIBL = radiance * fresnelSchlickRoughness(NdotV,F0,roughness) * iblSpecularFactor and diffuseIBL = irradiance*diffuseColor (2652) — no BRDF-LUT term, no FmsEms multi-scatter, no dielectricScattering. WebGL ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl:48-99 samples czm_brdfLut (line 62) and applies the full Fdez-Aguera single+multi-scatter model (FssEss, FmsEms, dielectricScattering). I grepped all WGSL: brdfLut is referenced ONLY in DeferredLighting.wgsl and BrdfLutGenerate.wgsl — never the model path. buildModelIBLEntries (WebGPUModelRenderer.js:1499-1502) returns exactly 4 bindings (33 diffuse, 34 specular, 35 sampler, 36 SH) with NO LUT slot, so the model material bind group cannot sample it. The WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:15-16 docstring falsely claims model split-sum uses the LUT. This is a genuine, actionable parity regression: metals/rough dielectrics will be brighter/dimmer and lose energy conservation vs WebGL. NOTE: DEFERRED_WORK.md:669-680 claims 'cubemap split-sum work shipped end-to-end Batch 130' but that entry only verifies the SH/cubemap DIFFUSE path — it does not verify LUT consumption and is itself overstated, so this is NOT properly tracked as a gap. The 'analytic Fresnel for IBL' is a deliberate, valid alternative formulation, not forced by WebGPU.

allMergedFindings.title: Direct-light geometry/visibility term diverges from WebGL (Schlick-GGX k=(r+1)²/8 vs height-correlated Smith-joint)
allMergedFindings.observation: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:852-859 uses `geometrySchlickGGX` with `k=(r+1)²/8` and `geometrySmith` returning G as a raw masking term, then divides by `4*NdotV*NdotL` separately (2241). It also uses `fresnelSchlick` with an implicit f90=1.0 (862-866). This is the LearnOpenGL/legacy formulation.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: pbrLighting.glsl:56-69 uses the height-correlated Smith-joint visibility `smithVisibilityGGX(alphaRoughness, NdotL, NdotV)` (Heitz 2014) which returns 0.5/(GGXV+GGXL) and already folds in the 1/(4 NdotL NdotV) denominator, and uses `f90 = clamp(reflectance*25, 0, 1)` (line 134) rather than a constant 1.0. The two geometry models produce visibly different specular falloff at grazing angles and for low-reflectance dielectrics; this is an algorithmic divergence not forced by WebGPU.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Port `smithVisibilityGGX` (height-correlated) and the `f90 = clamp(czm_maximumComponent(F0)*25, 0, 1)` Fresnel from pbrLighting.glsl into the WGSL so the direct BRDF matches WebGL bit-for-bit (modulo float ordering). Reuse the same alphaRoughness = roughness² mapping already present.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:852-859 defines geometrySchlickGGX with k=(r+1)*(r+1)/8 and geometrySmith as the product of two masking terms, then divides by 4*NdotV*NdotL separately (line 2241). fresnelSchlick (862-866) uses implicit f90=1.0. WebGL pbrLighting.glsl:56-69 uses smithVisibilityGGX (height-correlated Heitz-2014, returns 0.5/(GGXV+GGXL) folding in the 1/(4 NdotL NdotV) denominator) and f90 = clamp(reflectance*25,0,1) at line 134. These are genuinely different geometry/visibility models producing different grazing-angle specular falloff and different low-reflectance dielectric behavior. Not forced by WebGPU — both are pure WGSL math. Not found in any audit (no smithVisibility/f90/geometrySmith hits in the 2026-04-30 audits or DEFERRED_WORK). Real undocumented algorithmic divergence. Severity medium is fair: visible but subtle, affects shading correctness not crashes.

allMergedFindings.title: IBL diffuse/specular cubemaps sampled in raw eye space with no reference-frame matrix — reflections rotate with the camera
allMergedFindings.observation: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl samples the diffuse irradiance cubemap with eye-space N (`textureSampleLevel(iblDiffuseTexture, iblSampler, N, 0.0)`, line 2650) and the specular radiance cubemap with eye-space `R = reflect(-V, N)` (2659/2699). There is no transform into a stable world/ENU reference frame. If the radiance/irradiance cubemaps are generated from a world-aligned environment (procedural sky from environmentMapManager, or user specularEnvironmentMaps which are world-oriented), eye-space sampling means the reflection direction rotates as the camera orbits, so the reflected environment 'swims' across the surface — a hallmark IBL frame bug.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl:66 (`normalMC = normalize(model_iblReferenceFrameMatrix * normalEC)`) and :92 (`reflectMC = normalize(model_iblReferenceFrameMatrix * reflectEC)`) explicitly rotate eye-space N and reflection into the IBL reference frame before sampling, keeping reflections world-stable. WebGPU omits this matrix entirely.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Pass the IBL reference-frame matrix (eye→IBL/ENU) into the camera or material UBO and apply it to N and R before the cubemap sample, mirroring model_iblReferenceFrameMatrix. Confirm the frame the WebGPU radiance/irradiance cubemaps are baked in (WebGPUIBLPipeline) and choose the transform to match. If the cubemaps are already baked in eye space this finding is moot — but that itself would be non-durable since the bake happens once and the camera moves.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. ModelPBRComplete.wgsl samples iblDiffuseTexture with eye-space N (line 2650) and iblSpecularTexture with eye-space R = reflect(-V,N) (2659/2699) — no transform into a stable world/ENU frame. WebGL ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl:66 and :92 explicitly apply model_iblReferenceFrameMatrix to normalEC and reflectEC before sampling. I checked the cubemap provenance: WebGPUModelRenderer.js:1469-1485 sources the cubemaps from user specularEnvironmentMaps OR the environmentMapManager procedural sky (world-aligned), prefiltered via generateIBLMaps — these are world-oriented, baked once. So the finding's escape hatch ('moot if baked in eye space') does NOT apply: eye-space sampling means the reflected environment swims as the camera orbits. Genuine frame bug, not forced by WebGPU. Not documented in audits or DEFERRED_WORK (no reference-frame-matrix hits for the model IBL path). Severity medium is reasonable — a hallmark IBL artifact but only visible when a real environment map / procedural sky is configured.

allMergedFindings.title: Merged material / instance / IBL bind groups rebuilt via createBindGroup every frame for every primitive (no memoization)
allMergedFindings.observation: In the per-primitive draw loop, `buildModelIBLEntries` (2855), `buildMergedMaterialBindGroup` (2856), and `buildMergedInstanceBindGroup` (2866) all call `device.createBindGroup(...)` unconditionally every frame (definitions at 1413-1433 and 1517+). For batch-table (3D Tiles) primitives an additional `mergedMaterialBGTranslucent` is also built every frame (3318). The results are stored in local consts (`mergedMaterialBG`/`mergedInstanceBG`), never cached on `primCache`. For a static glTF model the underlying buffers and texture views are identical frame-to-frame; for a 3D Tileset with thousands of primitives this is thousands of bind-group allocations per frame plus GC pressure.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Cesium's WebGL path caches DrawCommands and only recreates GPU state when render resources go dirty; bind-group-equivalent state (uniform maps, textures) is not reallocated per frame. The WebGPU port regressed this by rebuilding descriptor-heavy bind groups every frame.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Memoize the merged bind groups on primCache/nodeCache, invalidating only when a constituent changes: material buffer identity, texture entries (deferred-texture refresh), feature-id entries, IBL views (cache.sourceVersion / env-map version), or the per-variant materialDefines. A simple dirty flag + stored bind-group reference eliminates the steady-state allocation entirely.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the mechanism: the per-primitive draw loop calls buildMergedMaterialBindGroup (2856) and buildMergedInstanceBindGroup (2866) unconditionally every frame, each invoking device.createBindGroup (1423), storing results in local consts not on primCache; the translucent BG is also rebuilt at 3318. This is real per-frame allocation. HOWEVER two things temper it: (1) the expensive sub-parts ARE cached — textureViews and textureEntries are memoized on primCache (1270-1313), and the comment there explicitly states 'The full merged group 1 bind group is built per-frame at the draw command emission site; this is just the cached texture portion' — so this is an ACKNOWLEDGED deliberate trade-off, not an oversight, and createBindGroup over already-built entry arrays is cheaper than the finding implies. (2) The identical anti-pattern IS documented in the ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE audit for post-process (:176) and SSR (:205) with the recommended fix (cache by tuple), and FORK_FEATURE_INVENTORY:104 lists Model perf items — but the Model-renderer-specific bind-group rebuild is NOT individually tracked. Downgrading severity from high to medium: real steady-state allocation + GC pressure under heavy tileset load, but partially mitigated and a known class of issue with an obvious memoize-by-dirty-flag fix.

allMergedFindings.title: Vertex shader runs full previous-frame morph + skin + instance deformation unconditionally even when TAA/motion is disabled
allMergedFindings.observation: vertexMain computes `prevPositionMC` by re-running the entire morph loop (773-789), the prev joint-matrix weighted blend (790-798), and the prev instance transform (799-802), then two extra mat4 multiplies for previousClipPos/currentClipPosForVelocity (808-814) — all with NO `if (motionFlags.x > 0.5)` guard. The FS gates motion-vector OUTPUT on motionFlags.x (computeMotionVectorScreenSpace:1102), but the VS work is always executed. For skinned/morphed characters this roughly doubles per-vertex morph+skin cost on every frame even when TAA is off, which is the default.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL Cesium does not emit per-vertex motion vectors at all in the standard model pipeline (TAA velocity for models is a fork addition), so there is no equivalent always-on cost. The unconditional execution is a port-introduced overhead.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Gate the prev-pose recomputation on a uniform (e.g. material.motionFlags.x > 0.5, the same flag the FS uses) so the second deformation pass and the extra matmuls are skipped when motion output is disabled. Since the flag is a uniform, the branch is uniform and cheap.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. vertexMain recomputes prevPositionMC via the full prev morph loop (772-789), prev joint-matrix blend (790-798), prev instance transform (799-802), plus two extra mat4 multiplies for previousClipPos/currentClipPosForVelocity (808-814) — with NO motion-flag guard. The FS gates motion OUTPUT on material.motionFlags.x < 0.5 (computeMotionVectorScreenSpace:1102), confirming the same uniform exists and could gate the VS work. So for skinned/morphed rigs this roughly doubles per-vertex deformation cost every frame even when TAA is off (the default). Real port-introduced overhead, not forced by WebGPU; the fix (uniform branch on motionFlags.x) is cheap and exact. Not documented. Severity medium is fair — a per-vertex cost on animated assets, not a correctness bug; impact scales with skin/morph complexity.

allMergedFindings.title: KHR_materials_anisotropy direct-light lobe is a heuristic GGX-roughness stretch, not the spec anisotropic BRDF WebGL implements
allMergedFindings.observation: The direct-light anisotropy block (ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2270-2316) approximates anisotropy by computing `aniRough = mix(roughness, 1.0, abs(TdotH)*aniStrength)` and feeding it to the isotropic distributionGGX, then adding the delta. The IBL-side bent-normal (2671-2696) IS a faithful port of WebGL's anisotropic IBL. The code comments acknowledge the direct path is an approximation.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: pbrLighting.glsl:142-152 implements the true anisotropic GGX: GGX_anisotropic + smithVisibilityGGX_anisotropic over a TBN-transformed light/view/halfway with separate tangential/bitangential roughness (tangentialRoughness = mix(alphaRoughness,1,strength²)). The WebGPU heuristic will not match brushed-metal highlight shape.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Port GGX_anisotropic + smithVisibilityGGX_anisotropic from pbrLighting.glsl; the authored tangent frame is already available in FragmentInput (tangentEC/bitangentEC). This closes the last KHR_materials_anisotropy gap. Likely already tracked under NEW-KHR-ANISO-TANGENT — confirm and surface as next work if so.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the code: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2310-2315 computes aniRough = mix(roughness,1.0,abs(TdotH)*aniStrength), feeds isotropic distributionGGX, adds the delta — a heuristic, not the spec GGX_anisotropic + smithVisibilityGGX_anisotropic that WebGL pbrLighting.glsl:142-152 implements. The finding's technical claim is accurate, AND the finding itself flags 'likely already tracked under NEW-KHR-ANISO-TANGENT — confirm.' I confirmed it IS tracked: DEFERRED_WORK.md:151 lists 'KHR_materials_anisotropy | Approximated | GGX D-term stretched ... Full per-tangent BRDF deferred', and FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:922 tracks FEAT-SURVEY-04 'KHR_materials_anisotropy full per-tangent BRDF (gated on Phase 8a).' (Note: the IBL bent-normal half WAS completed per NEW-KHR-ANISO-TANGENT Batch 210, and the direct-light path DOES now use the authored tangentEC per AUDIT B.5 — but the per-tangent anisotropic BRDF lobe itself remains the documented-deferred piece.) Documented; low severity confirmed.

allMergedFindings.title: BRDF LUT compute pass executes every device init but its product is unused by the forward model IBL path (wasted GPU/CPU work + misleading docstring)
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUImageBasedLighting.update calls `frameState.brdfLutGenerator.update(frameState)` (177-180), which dispatches the 256×256 integrateBRDF compute pass (1024 samples/texel) once per device. As established in finding #1, the forward model FS never samples this LUT. Per CLAUDE.md Principle 7 I checked the docstrings: the generator claims it feeds 'all PBR rendering' and IBL's docstring claims model split-sum uses it — but only the deferred-lighting WGSL declares a brdfLutTex binding. So for any viewer using forward model rendering (the default), this is a one-time wasted compute dispatch and the docstrings overstate consumption. (Not flagged as dead-code-to-remove since the deferred path may legitimately use it.)
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's czm_brdfLut is actually sampled by the model IBL stage, so the equivalent generation is load-bearing there. The WebGPU port generates it but, for models, leaves it disconnected.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either wire the LUT into the forward model path (finding #1, preferred) or, if only the deferred path consumes it, move the generator invocation behind the deferred-lighting enablement and correct both docstrings so future readers don't assume the model path is split-sum-correct.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified with one correction to the framing. WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:178-180 calls brdfLutGenerator.update each non-duplicate frame, but WebGPUBrdfLutGenerator.ts:242-245 early-outs with `if (cache.generated) return;` — so the compute dispatch (256x256, 1024 samples/texel) runs exactly ONCE per device, NOT per frame. The per-frame call is a cheap boolean early-out, so the 'wasted CPU/GPU work' is a one-time cost, not recurring (the title's 'every device init' is accurate; any implication of per-frame waste is not). The substantive claim stands: the LUT is never sampled by the forward model path (only DeferredLighting.wgsl declares brdfLutTex; buildModelIBLEntries binds no LUT), and the docstrings (WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts:15-16 'Specular IBL always uses ... the BRDF LUT for the split-sum approximation') overstate consumption for models. Real code-quality issue: misleading docstring + a generated-but-model-unused resource. Low severity is correct given it's a one-time dispatch. Tied to finding #1 (the real fix is to wire the LUT in).

allMergedFindings.title: Clearcoat base-layer dimming and Fresnel basis differ from WebGL (VdotH on `direct` only vs NdotV on the whole base color)
allMergedFindings.observation: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2357-2362 computes clearcoat Fresnel with VdotH (`F_cc = fresnelSchlick(VdotH, vec3(0.04)) * ccFactor`) and dims only the direct contribution (`direct = direct * (1 - F_cc) + ccBRDF...`). The ambient/IBL term is not attenuated by the coat.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: LightingStageFS.glsl:26-49 explicitly computes clearcoat Fresnel with NdotV (commented: 'clearcoat Fresnel computed with dot(n,v) instead of dot(v,h) ... to make it energy conserving with a simple layering function') and dims the ENTIRE accumulated base color including IBL: `return baseLayerColor * (1.0 - clearcoatFactor * F) + clearcoatColor`. WebGPU's VdotH basis and direct-only dimming under-attenuate the base layer under the coat, especially the ambient term.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Switch clearcoat Fresnel to NdotV per the WebGL energy-conservation note, and apply the `(1 - clearcoatFactor * F)` dimming to the full base color (direct + ambient + emissive base) rather than only `direct`, matching addClearcoatReflection. Also fold clearcoat IBL (computeSpecularIBL with the coat normal) which WebGPU currently omits.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WGSL ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2357 computes F_cc = fresnelSchlick(VdotH, vec3(0.04))*ccFactor (VdotH basis) and line 2361 dims ONLY direct: direct = direct*(1-F_cc) + ccBRDF...; the ambient/IBL term is never attenuated, and there is no clearcoat IBL lobe. WebGL LightingStageFS.glsl:28-29 computes clearcoat Fresnel with NdotV (with an explicit energy-conservation comment at :26-27), dims the ENTIRE accumulated base color at :49 (baseLayerColor*(1.0 - clearcoatFactor*F) + clearcoatColor, where baseLayerColor already includes direct + IBL + emissive), and adds clearcoat specular IBL at :38-43. All three divergences (Fresnel basis, dimming scope, missing coat IBL) are real and not forced by WebGPU. NOTE: DEFERRED_WORK.md:149 / FEATURE_INVENTORY claim KHR_materials_clearcoat is 'Full BRDF' — that doc claim is overstated relative to these divergences, so this specific divergence is NOT tracked. Low severity confirmed: a subtle energy-conservation/shading difference on coated materials, visible mainly on the ambient term under a coat.

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer produces an unbound buffer every frame — dead path, real logic lives in WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB
allMergedFindings.observation: Globe.js:1177-1178 calls the GROUND_ATMOSPHERE feature renderer's update() every frame. updateWebGPUGroundAtmosphere (WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts:97-153) packs 16 floats, dirty-compares, uploads to a GPUBuffer, and assigns globe._webgpuAtmosphereBuffer / _webgpuAtmosphereEnabled. But a repo-wide grep shows _webgpuAtmosphereBuffer is ONLY ever written (renderer + cesium-js-types.d.ts) and cleared (Globe.js:1256) — NO pipeline binds it. The shader GroundAtmosphere.wgsl's computeGroundAtmosphere() is never imported by GlobeTerrain.wgsl. The ACTUAL ground-atmosphere shading runs from the camera UB fields atmosphereLightDirectionAndIntensity / atmosphereParams packed by WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts (consumed at GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3482-3500). So this renderer is a fully redundant per-frame producer feeding nothing. Per Principle 7 I checked the docstring: it claims 'the GlobeTerrain.wgsl shader reads from' this buffer — that claim is FALSE for current code, so this is stale dead infrastructure rather than live scaffolding. FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:500 still lists it 'WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer — ground-atmosphere fog applied per primitive (SHIPPED)'.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no equivalent standalone renderer; ground atmosphere is integrated into GlobeFS/GlobeVS via shader defines + the czm_atmosphere* auto-uniform suite. The WebGPU equivalent of that integration is WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB's atmosphere fields — which work. This second renderer duplicates the intent without being wired.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either (a) delete WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts + GroundAtmosphere.wgsl + the Globe.js:1172-1179 call + the registration (the real path already covers the feature), or (b) if the intent was per-primitive ground-atmosphere fog distinct from the globe path, wire _webgpuAtmosphereBuffer into a real bind group and document the consumer. Update FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:500 to reflect actual state. The per-frame pack+compare+writeBuffer is wasted CPU/GPU work today.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the full chain. (1) Repo-wide grep: globe._webgpuAtmosphereBuffer is ONLY written (renderer L151 + cesium-js-types.d.ts:986) and cleared (Globe.js:1256) — no createBindGroup / setBindGroup ever references it. (2) GroundAtmosphere.wgsl's computeGroundAtmosphere() is never imported by GlobeTerrain.wgsl (grep shows only the file's own internal defs). (3) The LIVE ground-atmosphere shading at GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3482-3500 uses camera.atmosphereParams / camera.atmosphereLightDirectionAndIntensity (the camera UB packed by WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:539-624) and the inline computeAtmosphereScatteringGround + computeGroundAtmosphereColor functions — NOT the standalone renderer's buffer. (4) WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG Session 65 (Batches 56-72) + SHADER_PAIRS_LOCKSTEP.md:511 confirm the ground-atmosphere math was REWORKED to be inlined in GlobeTerrain.wgsl, superseding the standalone path. (5) The renderer's own docstring (L7-10) claims 'the GlobeTerrain.wgsl shader reads from' this uniform buffer — that claim is FALSE for current code, so this is stale dead infrastructure, not live scaffolding (Principle 7 correctly applied — the docstring's no-op-pending implication doesn't hold). (6) Globe.js:1177-1178 calls update() every frame; packAtmosphereParams + dirty-compare + writeBuffer run for nothing. (7) The orphan state is NOT documented anywhere as superseded — WEBGPU_MIGRATION_STATUS:2158 still says 'Wired (Session 17)' and FEATURE_INVENTORY:500 still says SHIPPED. All claims hold.

allMergedFindings.title: Ground atmosphere dynamicLighting flag drops enableLighting gating and dynamicAtmosphereLightingFromSun, and uses a divergent enum
allMergedFindings.observation: packAtmosphereParams (WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts:86) writes data[13] = globe.dynamicAtmosphereLighting ? 1.0 : 0.0 — a plain boolean. WebGL's canonical mapping DynamicAtmosphereLightingType.fromGlobeFlags (DynamicAtmosphereLightingType.js:42-53) requires `globe.enableLighting && globe.dynamicAtmosphereLighting` (the renderer ignores enableLighting entirely) and then returns SCENE_LIGHT(1) vs SUNLIGHT(2) based on dynamicAtmosphereLightingFromSun (never read here). The WGSL field doc (GroundAtmosphere.wgsl:31) even declares a THIRD divergent meaning: '0=off, 1=sunDirection, 2=viewerDirection'. Three different conventions for the same 3-state value.
