(Compounded by the prior finding: the field is never actually read in the WGSL, so today it's inert — but if the renderer is wired up as-is it will be wrong.)
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL: NONE/SCENE_LIGHT/SUNLIGHT (0/1/2) gated by enableLighting. WebGPU globe path (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:532-541,623) gets this RIGHT — it honors enableLighting and selects sun vs scene light. Only this orphaned renderer gets it wrong.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: If the renderer is kept, replace the boolean with DynamicAtmosphereLightingType.fromGlobeFlags(globe) and reconcile the WGSL field comment to the actual SCENE_LIGHT/SUNLIGHT semantics. If deleted per the prior finding, this is moot.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The factual code claims are all correct: packAtmosphereParams L86 writes data[13] = globe.dynamicAtmosphereLighting ? 1.0 : 0.0 (plain boolean, ignores enableLighting and dynamicAtmosphereLightingFromSun). DynamicAtmosphereLightingType.fromGlobeFlags (L42-53) requires globe.enableLighting && globe.dynamicAtmosphereLighting then selects SUNLIGHT(2) vs SCENE_LIGHT(1) by dynamicAtmosphereLightingFromSun. The WGSL field doc (GroundAtmosphere.wgsl:31) declares a third meaning '0=off, 1=sunDirection, 2=viewerDirection'. The LIVE camera-UB path (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:622-624) gets it RIGHT: dynamicLightingActive = !!tp.dynamicAtmosphereLighting && !!tp.enableLighting, encoded as 2.0/1.0/0.0. HOWEVER: this is a latent bug in DEAD code — per finding #1 the renderer's buffer + GroundAtmosphere.wgsl are never bound/consumed, so data[13] is inert today. It only becomes wrong IF the orphan renderer is ever wired up. The reviewer themselves acknowledged this dependency. Real divergence, but currently harmless; severity dropped from medium to low since it produces no incorrect output in the current code.

allMergedFindings.title: Stale 'resolver NOT invoked for the color draw' comment contradicts actual draw-command behavior (per-frustum UBO IS live)
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js:2589-2591 comment states: 'this resolver is currently NOT invoked for the color draw — the static slot 0 below is what binds — so the encode delivery is still incomplete. See WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG Batch 184.' But resolveFrustumStateBindGroup is installed at sharedDrawArgs.bindGroupResolvers[2] (L2692), and WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:515-518 loops over bindGroupResolvers and calls each non-undefined resolver at draw time (`const resolved = resolver ? resolver() : null; setBindGroup(i, resolved ?? bindGroups[i])`). I verified the producers it reads (uniformState._currentSliceIndex, _logDepthEncodeNearFar) ARE written by WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:304-305 and :194-195. So the resolver IS invoked and the per-slice UBO IS delivered. The comment is stale and actively misleading for the next engineer debugging the documented far-corner recon-precision residual — it points them at a non-bug.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — this is an internal-consistency/doc-accuracy issue in the WebGPU per-frustum classifier plumbing that has no WebGL analog (WebGL classifies per-frustum natively without replay).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Delete or correct the L2589-2591 comment. The real open residual is the depth-reconstruction catastrophic-cancellation near storedDepth≈0.9999997 already tracked as NEW-GROUNDPRIM-CLASSIFIER-RECON-PRECISION — point the comment there instead of at a phantom 'resolver not invoked' problem.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md (NEW-GROUNDPRIM-TEXTURED-MATERIALS, line 896 item (g): 'the resolver is NOT invoked for the color draw (Link 4 unresolved, Batch 184), so the color draw still binds the static slot-0 / u.invProj projection' — marked unresolved)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The reviewer's central claim — that the comment is stale/false because the resolver IS invoked — is itself MISLEADING, and the underlying state is already tracked. I re-read the actual consuming shader: windowToEye() at WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js:892-932. In BOTH the log and non-log branches the eye-space reconstruction unprojects with u.invProj (group 0, L926/L930), NOT the per-slice fstate.invProj (group 2). The fstate (group 2) bind group IS set at draw time (the reviewer is right that WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:515-518 calls resolveFrustumStateBindGroup since it sits at bindGroupResolvers[2], non-undefined), but fstate.invProj is intentionally NOT consumed by the reconstruction — only fstate.encode (log near/far) and fstate.perSlice (slice-discard, L1146-1147) are read. So the substantive claim of the source comment ('the static slot 0 / u.invProj projection is what reconstruction binds; the per-slice encode delivery is still incomplete') is CORRECT and matches DEFERRED_WORK.md:896 (g) verbatim (⬜ unresolved). The comment's phrasing ('resolver currently NOT invoked') is imprecise about the mechanism (the bind group IS set), but its conclusion is accurate and points at a real, documented gap — deleting it as the reviewer recommends would erase an accurate caveat. The reviewer verified the wrong layer (bind-group set) without checking shader consumption. Severity reduced to low.

allMergedFindings.title: GroundPolyline geometricToleranceOverMeter and (acceptable) metersPerPixel are CPU-static approximations of WebGL screen-space builtins
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js:214 hardcodes GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE_OVER_METER = 1.0e-6 and passes it via misc.w. WebGL's PolylineShadowVolumeVS.glsl:117 uses the dynamic czm_geometricToleranceOverMeter (camera/pixel-size-driven) to scale the downward 'bottom' extrusion. The hardcode is steady-state-correct for global views but diverges at extreme near/far zoom, where the bottom skirt can under/over-extrude and produce gaps or z-fighting on terrain at oblique angles. (Separately, the metersPerPixel WGSL reimpl at L369-371 reading proj[0][0]/proj[1][1] is a legitimate and good backend port of the unavailable czm_metersPerPixel builtin — not a defect.) The renderer docstring acknowledges the 1e-6 limitation, so this is documented scaffolding, flagged at low severity for completeness.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL computes both czm_geometricToleranceOverMeter and czm_metersPerPixel dynamically from UniformState each frame; WebGPU statically pins the tolerance and recomputes metersPerPixel in-shader.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Plumb uniformState's dynamic geometricToleranceOverMeter through the UBO (it's already computed for WebGL each frame) to close the oblique-angle extrusion gap. Low priority — affects only extreme-zoom terrain-clamped polylines.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified at source. WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js:214 hardcodes GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE_OVER_METER = 1.0e-6, passed via misc.w (per the renderer's own comment L207-213 acknowledging it as a 'first-cut limitation' vs WebGL's dynamic czm_geometricToleranceOverMeter). The metersPerPixel WGSL reimpl at L369-374 (reading u.proj[0][0]/u.proj[1][1]) is, as the reviewer notes, a legitimate good backend port of the unavailable czm_metersPerPixel builtin — not a defect. The divergence is real (static tolerance vs WebGL's per-frame camera/pixel-driven value) but only bites at extreme near/far zoom on terrain-clamped polylines, and is documented in-code. Low severity confirmed; not a port regression (the renderer is fork-new).

allMergedFindings.title: Depth-sample classifiers discard on exact float equality surfaceDepth == 0.0
allMergedFindings.observation: All three depth-sample fragment shaders (dsColorFS L1103, dsPickFS L1163, dsStencilFS L1180) sky-discard with `if (surfaceDepth == 0.0) { discard; }` after unpackDepth() of an RGBA-packed depth sampled via textureSampleLevel with a LINEAR sampler (materialSampler is linear; depthSampler config not shown here but the pattern reconstructs from a packed-RGBA texture). Exact == 0.0 on a value that is dot(packed, vec4(1,1/255,...)) is fragile if any nearest/linear filtering or precision dither nudges a true-zero (sky) sample to e.g. 1e-9. A small epsilon (surfaceDepth < eps) would be more durable and matches the intent ('no surface wrote depth here').
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's ShadowVolumeAppearance uses the depth-attachment / stencil natively rather than sampling a packed-depth color texture, so it never does this float-equality test. The == 0.0 is a WebGPU-port artifact of the depth-sample (vs depth-attachment) architecture.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Change to `if (surfaceDepth < 1e-7) { discard; }` (or sample with a NEAREST sampler for the depth texture to guarantee unfiltered packed bytes). Verify the depth sampler is nearest — a linear sampler on packed RGBA depth would corrupt unpackDepth() at every tile/object silhouette edge, which would be a more serious bug worth confirming.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified all three FS use the exact-equality discard: dsColorFS L1103, dsPickFS L1163, dsStencilFS L1180 all do 'if (surfaceDepth == 0.0) { discard; }' after unpackDepth() of an RGBA-packed depth sampled via textureSampleLevel. CRITICALLY, the reviewer's flagged 'more serious bug worth confirming' is REAL: the depth sampler (cache.depthSampleSampler, L2452-2458) is created with magFilter:'linear' / minFilter:'linear', and the BGL declares it 'filtering' (L1310) over a texture_2d<f32> globeDepthTex (L797) holding RGBA8-packed depth. Linear interpolation of packed-RGBA bytes does corrupt unpackDepth() at any texel boundary where adjacent depths differ (silhouette edges) and also defeats the == 0.0 sky-discard at sky/surface edges (interpolation nudges a true-zero to ~1e-9). This contrasts with the GlobeDepth depth-copy which intentionally uses magFilter/minFilter 'nearest' (per archive/sandcastle-batch-66 NEW-4-B). It validates (it's an f32 color texture, not a depth-sampleType texture, so no validation error) but is semantically wrong. Practical impact is bounded because screenUV = i.pos.xy/viewport samples at pixel/texel centers for a full-res depth target (linear returns the exact texel for interior pixels), so corruption only manifests at edges / if the depth texture differs in resolution from the viewport. Confirmed-real; an epsilon discard plus a NEAREST sampler would be the durable fix. Low severity given the bounded practical impact, but the linear-sampler concern is the load-bearing part.

allMergedFindings.title: Two ground renderers are ~2850 and ~3200 LOC undecomposed god-files with embedded multi-KB WGSL template strings
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js = 2852 lines, WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js = 3209 lines, WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js = 2873 lines — each ~3x the CLAUDE.md ~1000-line decomposition guideline. Each embeds its full WGSL as a JS template literal interleaved with pipeline/buffer/command/material logic (e.g. the entire GroundPrimitive U-struct + VS + FS + material dispatch is inline from L732-1184). This concentrates the material-resolution, extent-packing, per-frustum-UBO, pick, velocity, and morph concerns into single modules, making the depth-recon-precision residual hard to isolate and the WGSL hard to diff against the GLSL source of truth.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL keeps shader source in dedicated .glsl files (ShadowVolumeAppearanceFS.glsl, PolylineShadowVolumeVS/FS.glsl) separate from the JS Primitive/GroundPrimitive/GroundPolylinePrimitive orchestration. The WebGPU port collapsed that separation into monolithic JS.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Extract the WGSL template builders into companion *.wgsl.js modules (or real .wgsl files run through the existing shader pipeline) and split material resolution (resolveMaterialState/ensureMaterialImage) + per-frustum-UBO management into *Helpers.js, per the file-size rule. Note the CLAUDE.md caveat to not decompose pure math/data classes — this is orchestration code, so it qualifies.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: wc -l verified: WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js = 2852, WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer.js = 3209, WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js = 2873 — each ~3x the CLAUDE.md ~1000-line decomposition guideline. Confirmed each embeds full WGSL as JS template literals interleaved with pipeline/buffer/command/material logic (e.g. the GroundPrimitive U-struct + applyMaterial dispatch inline from ~L732-1184, SHADER_CODE template in GroundPolyline from L216). These are orchestration modules (material resolution, extent packing, per-frustum-UBO, pick, velocity, morph), NOT the pure-math/data classes CLAUDE.md exempts, so the decomposition rule applies. The recommendation (extract *.wgsl.js builders + *Helpers.js) aligns with the file-size rule. Code-quality finding, medium severity confirmed.

allMergedFindings.title: GroundPrimitive Grid material thickness uses a fixed viewport-derived approximation lacking WebGL's per-pixel derivatives
allMergedFindings.observation: applyMaterial Grid branch (WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js:1037-1071) converts line thickness from pixels to cell-fraction via cellFracPerPixel = lineCount / viewportDim, with the code comment explicitly noting 'exact match to WebGL requires per-pixel derivative-based thickness, deferred' and 'Fixed 1/64 approximation works for typical zooms'. The Checkerboard branch (L1016-1035) similarly hardcodes a smoothstep(0.0, 0.03, aaDist) AA width. WebGL's GridMaterial/CheckerboardMaterial use fwidth()/dpdx-style anisotropic AA. Result: grid line widths and checker AA will not track zoom the way WebGL does.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL Grid/Checkerboard materials use screen-space derivatives (fwidth) for distance-stable line thickness and anti-aliasing; WGSL has dpdx/dpdy available but the port chose a viewport-ratio approximation instead.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: WGSL supports dpdx/dpdy/fwidth in fragment shaders — port the derivative-based thickness/AA to match WebGL exactly rather than the viewport-ratio + fixed-constant approximation. Low priority; cosmetic divergence on Grid/Checkerboard ground polygons at non-typical zooms.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified at source. Grid branch (materialType==3u, L1037-1071): cellFracPerPixel = lineCount / max(viewportDim,1.0) (L1060-1061), with the in-code comment L1056-1059 explicitly stating 'Fixed 1/64 approximation works for typical zooms — exact match to WebGL requires per-pixel derivative-based thickness, deferred.' Checkerboard branch (L1016-1035) hardcodes 'smoothstep(0.0, 0.03, aaDist)' AA width (L1033). WebGL Grid/Checkerboard materials use fwidth()/screen-space derivatives for distance-stable thickness/AA. WGSL does support dpdx/dpdy/fwidth in fragment shaders, so the port could match WebGL but chose a viewport-ratio + fixed-constant approximation. Real cosmetic divergence on Grid/Checkerboard ground polygons at non-typical zooms, documented in-code. Low severity confirmed.

allMergedFindings.title: Per-frame ground-atmosphere dirty-compare allocates a fresh 16-float array each frame even when disabled-then-enabled
allMergedFindings.observation: updateWebGPUGroundAtmosphere calls packAtmosphereParams (WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts:131) every frame when enabled, and packAtmosphereParams (L54-91) does `const data = new Float32Array(16)` on every invocation — a per-frame heap allocation purely to feed the dirty-compare loop, then .set() copies it into the cached array. The renderer already keeps cache.data; it could pack directly into a module-scratch Float32Array and compare in place. (Mooted if the renderer is deleted per finding #1, but worth noting as a pattern.)
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGL auto-uniforms are diffed by UniformState without per-frame array allocation. The other WebGPU UB packers in this subsystem (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js scratchRTEUniformData, GroundPrimitive scratch* matrices) correctly use module-scoped scratch buffers; this renderer is the outlier.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Hoist the Float32Array(16) to a module scratch and pack/compare in place, matching the scratch-buffer discipline used elsewhere in the subsystem. Or delete the renderer (finding #1).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified: packAtmosphereParams (WebGPUGroundAtmosphereRenderer.ts:54-91) does 'const data = new Float32Array(16)' at L58 on every call; updateWebGPUGroundAtmosphere calls it at L131 every frame when cache.enabled, then .set()-copies into cache.data for the dirty-compare (L136-145). This is a per-frame heap allocation that could be hoisted to a module scratch and compared in place, matching the scratch-buffer discipline used elsewhere in the subsystem (e.g. WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js scratchRTEUniformData). The pattern observation is correct. HOWEVER it is fully mooted by finding #1: the renderer's output feeds nothing, so the cleaner fix is deletion, not micro-optimizing a dead per-frame producer. Low severity confirmed; real but low-value in isolation.

allMergedFindings.title: TRIANGLE_FAN silently falls back to triangle-list producing wrong topology
allMergedFindings.observation: mapCesiumPrimitiveTypeToWebGPU (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:528-533) maps PrimitiveType.TRIANGLE_FAN to 'triangle-list' because WebGPU has no triangle-fan topology. The comment acknowledges this 'produces wrong topology but no validation error.' Any geometry that genuinely uses TRIANGLE_FAN will render as garbage triangles silently (same failure class as the Session-65 LINES-as-triangles bug this function was created to fix). LINE_LOOP→line-strip (L519-523) has the same silent-wrong-topology risk but is documented as safe because Cesium outline geometries wrap manually.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL2 supports GL_TRIANGLE_FAN natively, so any upstream consumer using it renders correctly there. WebGPU drops it.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either convert TRIANGLE_FAN index/vertex data to triangle-list at geometry-extract time (the comment already suggests this), or emit a one-time console.warn so a TRIANGLE_FAN consumer fails loudly rather than rendering garbage. Mainstream Cesium geometry avoids TRIANGLE_FAN, so low severity, but the silent-wrong path violates the project's 'fail loudly' sentinel guidance.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified mapCesiumPrimitiveTypeToWebGPU (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:528-533) maps PrimitiveType.TRIANGLE_FAN to 'triangle-list' with the comment explicitly acknowledging it 'produces wrong topology but no validation error.' The silent-wrong path does violate the project's 'fail loudly' sentinel guidance, and the reviewer's isPortRegression:true is fair (WebGL2 supports GL_TRIANGLE_FAN natively). MITIGATING: mainstream paths convert TRIANGLE_FAN to triangle indices BEFORE reaching this function — ModelReader.convertTriangleFanToTriangleIndices (ModelReader.js:722-725) for glTF, and GeometryPipeline.js validation requires TRIANGLES/TRIANGLE_STRIP/TRIANGLE_FAN conversion. So raw TRIANGLE_FAN reaching this fallback is an edge case, not a mainstream regression — the reviewer correctly rated it low. The fix (convert at extract time, or emit a one-time console.warn) is sound. Confirmed-real, low severity, isPortRegression.

allMergedFindings.title: Primitive clipping-plane receive is silently a no-op (placeholder effects slot)
allMergedFindings.observation: _getOrCreateSharedPrimitiveEffectsBG (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:774-896) wires shadow-receive, CSM, aerial-LUT fog, and clustered lighting into the per-frame primitive effects bind group, but the comment at L771-773 and L875-876 states clipping planes are NOT threaded through: 'Clipping wiring for primitives is a separate follow-up; this helper leaves the clipping slots on the placeholder so clipping stays no-op.' So a ClippingPlaneCollection applied to an appearance Primitive (Box/Polygon/etc.) has no visual effect on WebGPU. I did not find this specific gap clearly enumerated under the primitive subsystem in the docs I sampled (it may be tracked under a clipping epic, but the primitive-path coupling is worth surfacing).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL primitives honor ClippingPlaneCollection via the appearance shader's czm_clipPlanes path. The WebGPU effects BG declares the clipping slots in its layout but binds placeholder (no-op) data for primitives.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Thread the primitive's/scene's ClippingPlaneCollection into createEffectsBindGroup for the primitive path (the slot already exists in the BGL), or confirm/cross-reference an existing tracked clipping entry and note primitives specifically. Per Principle 9, surface this as the concrete next work item rather than leaving the placeholder silently.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:815 (WGF-1-EXPAND: 'clip-distances only wired in globe; Primitive shaders have struct but no VS output; Models lack clipping plane support entirely'); WGF-1-INTERSECTION (:816)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the gap is real: _getOrCreateSharedPrimitiveEffectsBG (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:774-896) threads shadow/CSM/aerial-LUT/clustered-lighting but NOT clipping — comments at L769-772 ('the primitive pipeline doesn't currently thread a ClippingPlaneCollection reference through to the effects BG ... clipping stays no-op') and L874-875 ('Clipping wiring for primitives is a separate follow-up') confirm it; grep shows clipping is referenced in this file ONLY as the placeholder slot (L769/772/875/1251/1705). So a ClippingPlaneCollection on an appearance Primitive has no visual effect on WebGPU. HOWEVER this IS tracked: FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:815 (WGF-1-EXPAND) explicitly states primitive clipping is incomplete ('Primitive shaders have struct but no VS output'). Note the 2026-04-16 PER_FEATURE review C-P6 'FIXED Batch 12' only corrected the clip-plane eye-space TRANSFORM math, not the data-threading from a primitive's collection through the effects BG — so the no-op the reviewer found is the still-open threading half, consistent with WGF-1-EXPAND. The reviewer's specific call-site detail is useful but the gap is already enumerated. Medium severity retained.

allMergedFindings.title: Billboard eyeOffset is silently dropped on WebGPU (also breaks Label.eyeOffset)
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGL's Billboard supports a per-billboard eyeOffset (Cartesian3, eye-space offset) via a dedicated vertex attribute (BillboardCollection.js:44 EYE_OFFSET_INDEX, :801/:814 writeEyeOffset, :1367 attributeLocations.eyeOffset) and the GLSL shader applies it. The WebGPU instance build (buildInstanceData / buildPickInstanceData) packs posHigh/Low, scale, rotation, pixelOffset, alignedAxis, imageRect, color, miscFlags, perInstanceFlags, 3 NearFarScalars and threePointAttribs — but NEVER eyeOffset. BillboardCollection.wgsl has zero references to eyeOffset (grep confirms absent). Tellingly, computeBoundingVolumeForFeatureRenderer DOES read billboard.eyeOffset for the BV expansion (BillboardCollection.js:2167-2177), so the cull sphere accounts for an offset the shader never applies. Because LabelCollection delegates glyph rendering to the WebGPU billboard path and Label.eyeOffset (Label.js:223/1092/1119) is forwarded to its glyph billboards, Label.eyeOffset is also a no-op on WebGPU. eyeOffset is the documented mechanism for nudging a label/billboard toward the camera to avoid z-fighting and for the classic 'lift label above marker' pattern.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL applies eyeOffset in eye space in the vertex shader after the model-view transform; WebGPU never reads it. Pure dropped feature, not a backend constraint.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add an eyeOffset vec3 to the billboard instance layout (it can ride in the unused .w lanes of an existing vec4 plus one new lane, or extend the stride by one vec4) and apply it in eye space in BillboardCollection.wgsl (and the SDF label shader) after translateRelativeToEye / before projection, mirroring the GLSL term. Pick path needs it too so picks line up with the offset render.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_PER_FEATURE_2026_04_16.md:331-337 (historical only; bundle partially closed, eyeOffset not in live trackers)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified directly. WebGL BillboardCollection.js has a dedicated EYE_OFFSET_INDEX attribute (line 44), writeEyeOffset at 1689-1721, and attributeLocations.eyeOffset at 1367. The WGSL shader BillboardCollection.wgsl has ZERO eyeOffset references (grep confirms). The WebGPU instance builder enumerates the full 44-float layout (posHigh/Low, scale, rotation, pixelOffset, alignedAxis, imageRect, color, miscFlags, perInstanceFlags, 3 NearFarScalars, threePointAttribs) and never packs eyeOffset. computeBoundingVolumeForFeatureRenderer DOES read billboard.eyeOffset for BV expansion (BillboardCollection.js:2167-2177), confirming the cull sphere accounts for an offset the shader never applies — exactly as the finding states. This is a pure dropped feature, not a backend constraint. On tracking: eyeOffset was bundled into the C-P9-COLLECTIONS follow-up in PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_PER_FEATURE_2026_04_16.md (lines 331-337, 636) alongside distanceDisplayCondition/translucencyByDistance/pixelOffsetScaleByDistance/scaleByDistance. The four siblings LANDED in Batches 135/136 (A.14 work — verified present in both JS pack and WGSL), but eyeOffset was left out and is NOT carried in the live DEFERRED_WORK.md or FEATURE_INVENTORY.md (grep returns nothing). So it is an orphaned, still-open parity gap that has fallen out of active tracking now that its bundle-mates were completed. Severity high stands (label-above-marker and z-fight-nudge are common patterns; Label.eyeOffset forwards to glyph billboards so it is also a no-op).

allMergedFindings.title: Billboard + Label rebuild the full instance buffer every frame; Point gates on dirtiness and WebGL only rewrites changed billboards
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1251 calls buildInstanceData(collection) unconditionally every frame — a full O(n) CPU walk that allocates a new Float32Array(length*44) and does a full device.queue.writeBuffer of the entire instance range, even when nothing changed (the grep for needsRebuild/lastLength in the billboard file returns only the function def). WebGPULabelRenderer.js:1012 does the same via buildSDFInstanceData. By contrast WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js:959-965 computes needsRebuild from instanceBuffer presence, _pointPrimitivesToUpdate.length, lastLength change, and definesChanged, and only rebuilds when dirty. WebGL's BillboardCollection only rewrites vertices for billboards in _billboardsToUpdate (the writers loop), not the whole buffer. For a static label-heavy scene (every glyph is a billboard) this is a per-frame full re-encode + full GPU upload + GC churn from the throwaway typed array.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL rewrites only dirty billboards' vertices (sub-range buffer updates keyed by _billboardsToUpdate). WebGPU billboard/label re-encode and re-upload everything every frame.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Port the Point renderer's needsRebuild gate to the billboard and label renderers: keep cache.instanceData + cache.lastLength, skip buildInstanceData/writeBuffer when _billboardsToUpdate is empty and length is unchanged and defines are stable. (The velocity path already needs prevInstanceData stashed, so the typed array can be retained rather than reallocated.) This is a near-mechanical port of an already-proven pattern in the same subsystem.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1251 calls buildInstanceData(collection) unconditionally with no guard; grep for needsRebuild/lastLength/_billboardsToUpdate in the file returns only the buildInstanceData definition — there is no dirtiness gate. buildInstanceData allocates a fresh Float32Array(length*44) every call (line 156) and the code writes the whole instance range. WebGPULabelRenderer.js:1012 calls buildSDFInstanceData unconditionally the same way. By contrast WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js:959-965 computes needsRebuild from instanceBuffer presence, _pointPrimitivesToUpdate.length, lastLength change, and definesChanged. WebGL BillboardCollection.js has the dirty fast path: the else-if(billboardsToUpdateLength > 0) branch at line 782 rewrites only dirty billboards' vertices rather than the whole buffer. The drift is real and the recommended fix (port the Point needsRebuild gate) is a near-mechanical port of an in-subsystem pattern. The 2026-04-16 review flagged 'missing dirty tracking' generically and tracked a TDPC-specific item (H-P9/C-P13) but did NOT track the Billboard/Label rebuild-every-frame issue as a discrete item, and the Point needsRebuild gate that creates this specific drift did not exist at review time. High severity is justified for label-heavy scenes (every glyph is a billboard → per-frame full re-encode + full GPU upload + GC churn).

allMergedFindings.title: Four collection renderers duplicate the entire pipeline-cache / shader-module / placeholder / velocity plumbing with no shared base
allMergedFindings.observation: Billboard, Label, Point and Polyline renderers each independently reimplement: the per-device WebGPUShaderModuleCache WeakMap + getShaderModuleCache (Billboard:692-701, Point/Label/Polyline mirror it), the {descriptor,pipeline,pending} entry Map + tryResolveXPipeline + descriptorToGPU fallback (Billboard:624-686), the _scenePipelineFormatGeneration invalidation block (Billboard:1060-1066, Point:905-911, Label:790-795), the lazy velocity-pipeline cache (Billboard:1107-1135, Label:836-864, Point:898-902), and 1x1 placeholder-texture creation. The prewarm define-set lists and packUniforms RTE blocks are near-copies. Each is a 1000-1700 LOC file (all 5 are at/over the ~1000 LOC decomposition threshold in CLAUDE.md). This is ~3000+ LOC of copy-paste that drifts independently (e.g. Point gained needsRebuild; Billboard/Label did not — see the perf finding).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's collections share Context/ShaderProgram/VertexArray/RenderState abstractions and a common BillboardCollection vertex-array path; the WebGPU port forked each into a standalone module.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Extract a WebGPUCollectionRendererBase (or a set of free helpers in a WebGPUCollectionRendererHelpers.ts) for: shader-module-cache accessor, pipeline-entry resolve + format-generation invalidation, velocity-pipeline resolve, placeholder-texture factory, and the RTE uniform packer. Renderers supply only their instance layout, define-scan, and descriptor builders. This both shrinks the files under 1000 LOC and prevents the kind of per-renderer drift this audit found.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. Each of Billboard (1571 LOC), Label (1212), Point (1381), Polyline (1690), and Cloud (1017) independently declares its own per-device WeakMap shader-module cache (grep confirms _shaderModuleCaches in Billboard:692, _sdfShaderModuleCaches in Label:383, _pointShaderModuleCaches in Point:594, _polylineShaderModuleCaches in Polyline:546 — plus 7 more renderer files repeat the identical WeakMap pattern). All independently reimplement the {descriptor,pipeline,pending} entry Map + tryResolve + the _scenePipelineFormatGeneration invalidation block (Billboard:1060-1066 verified; Polyline:1046 verified) and the lazy velocity-pipeline cache. There is a shared WebGPUCollectionShaders.js for shader SOURCE loading, but no shared WebGPUCollectionRendererBase for the cache/pipeline/velocity/placeholder plumbing. All four/five files are at or over the ~1000 LOC decomposition threshold that CLAUDE.md flags. The finding's claim that the duplication drifts independently is itself evidenced by findings 1 and 2 (Point gained needsRebuild; Billboard/Label did not). This is a legitimate architecture/maintainability finding, not a bug. Medium severity is appropriate for a refactor recommendation.

allMergedFindings.title: Velocity (motion-vector) paths add prevPosHigh+prevPosLow in f32 — RTE-mandate violation behind a 'precision loss acceptable' note that is likely optimistic for static geometry
allMergedFindings.observation: Every collection velocity VS computes the current-frame clip via RTE (mvpRelativeToEye * translateRelativeToEye(...)) but the previous-frame clip via previousViewProjection * vec4(prevPosHigh + prevPosLow, 1.0): BillboardCollection.wgsl:630-631, PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl:326-327, PolylineCollection.wgsl:319-320, WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts WGSL:185. previousViewProjection is a full (non-eye-relative) f32 mat4 and prevPosHigh+prevPosLow collapses the 64-bit emulated position into a single f32 (~7 significant digits) at ~6.3e6 m planet scale — so the low bits are gone. DEFERRED_WORK.md:1189-1192 explicitly calls this an accepted tradeoff ('precision loss at planet scale is acceptable for NDC delta magnitudes'). The concern: for STATIC billboards/labels/points the true velocity is zero, but currentNdc is computed sub-mm-accurately (RTE) while prevNdc carries meter-scale rounding, so curNdc-prevNdc is a nonzero spurious motion vector that TAA will treat as real motion → ghosting/smearing of otherwise-stationary markers. The asymmetry (one side RTE, one side not) is what produces the artifact, not the absolute precision.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL collections have no transform-feedback velocity pass; this is a WebGPU-only TAA feature, so there is no WebGL baseline — but RTE precision is mandatory per CLAUDE.md regardless of backend.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Make the prev-frame projection RTE-symmetric: pass a previousViewProjectionRelativeToEye + previous encodedCamera (or simply reuse the current encodedCamera since the camera-to-prev delta is small) so prev clip is also computed from camera-relative offsets. Alternatively, since static markers dominate, compute prevNdc as currentNdc minus an RTE-space delta. At minimum, re-validate the 'acceptable' claim with a probe at a planet-scale saved view and a static billboard before relying on it; the doc's rationale is asserted, not measured.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The code claims are verified exactly: BillboardCollection.wgsl:630-631 computes prevWorldPos = vec4(prevPosHigh + prevPosLow, 1.0) then prevCenterClip = previousViewProjection * prevWorldPos (full non-eye-relative f32 mat4); PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl:326-327 and PolylineCollection.wgsl:316-320 do the same; the current-frame side uses RTE (mvpRelativeToEye * translateRelativeToEye). The asymmetry is real. HOWEVER, this exact tradeoff is explicitly documented in DEFERRED_WORK.md:1189-1192 ('full mat4 multiply of prevPosHigh + prevPosLow — precision loss at planet scale is acceptable for NDC delta magnitudes') and the shader comment at BillboardCollection.wgsl:624-627 repeats the rationale. So the divergence is a tracked, intentional decision — verdict already-documented. The adversarial nuance the finding adds (that the RTE-vs-non-RTE asymmetry produces spurious nonzero velocity for STATIC markers → TAA ghosting, which the doc's absolute-precision argument does not directly rebut) is a fair point and the recommendation to re-validate with a planet-scale static-marker probe is reasonable. But because the behavior is documented as an accepted tradeoff, this is not a new actionable bug; if pursued it is a refinement of an already-tracked item. Severity reduced to low — it is documented, gated behind TAA-only, and the worst case is sub-pixel jitter on static markers, not broken rendering.

allMergedFindings.title: No error sentinels (buffer-size / null-target / re-entry guards) in any collection renderer despite the CLAUDE.md mandate
allMergedFindings.observation: CLAUDE.md 'Permanent sentinels for new subsystems' requires every new renderer/pipeline subsystem to add a re-entry guard, a null-target guard, and a buffer-size validation. grep for console.error/console.warn/overflow/re-entry in WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js returns nothing but a stray comment. The renderers do device.queue.writeBuffer(...) with requiredSize derived from visibleCount and compare cache.instanceBuffer.size < requiredSize before growing, but there is no permanent console.error sentinel if the upload payload ever exceeds the (possibly stale) GPU buffer, no guard if cache.uniformBuffer/atlasTextureView is null at bind-group build, and no re-entry counter. These are exactly the failure modes (BUG-15 index overflow, BUG-13 null PP views) the rule was written to catch.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — these are WebGPU-runtime safety sentinels with no WebGL analog.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add the three mandated permanent (non-pragma) console.error sentinels per renderer: validate payload byteLength <= GPU buffer size before writeBuffer, null-check the atlas/uniform resources before createBindGroup, and a per-frame re-entry counter. Cheap and aligned with the existing rule.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. grep for console.error/console.warn across WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js, WebGPULabelRenderer.js, WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js, WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js, and WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts returns ZERO matches (the 25 'byteLength/requiredSize' hits are all size-arithmetic, not sentinels). The renderers do compare cache.instanceBuffer.size < requiredSize before growing (Billboard:1257-1260) but emit no permanent console.error if a payload ever exceeds the GPU buffer, no null-guard on atlasTextureView/uniformBuffer before createBindGroup, and no per-frame re-entry counter. CLAUDE.md's 'Permanent sentinels for new subsystems' section says every new renderer/pipeline subsystem SHOULD add a re-entry guard, null-target guard, and buffer-size validation — these are exactly the BUG-15 (index overflow) and BUG-13 (null PP views) failure modes the rule targets. The mandate is a SHOULD (not MUST), so this is a code-quality gap rather than a correctness bug; the fix is cheap and aligned with the documented rule. Medium severity stands.

allMergedFindings.title: updateWebGPUBillboards / updateWebGPUPolylines declared async with no await — caller ignores the returned Promise, swallowing synchronous throws
allMergedFindings.observation: updateWebGPUBillboards (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1006) and updateWebGPUPolylines (WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js:1179) are declared `async` but contain no `await` (grep for await across both files returns nothing). The Point and Label equivalents are plain functions. The FR is registered as { update: updateWebGPUBillboards } and called as fr.update(this, frameState, frameState.commandList) in BillboardCollection.js:713 with no await/.catch. Because there's no real await the body still runs synchronously and pushes commands before returning, so it's not a frame-ordering bug today — but any synchronous throw inside becomes an unhandled rejected Promise that the caller never sees, and the async signature falsely implies the command push could be deferred to a microtask (which would drop the frame). The async keyword is pure liability.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL update() paths are synchronous; the async divergence here is gratuitous and undocumented.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Drop the `async` keyword from both functions to match the Point/Label renderers (the async pipeline resolution already uses the entry.pending + return-null-and-retry-next-frame pattern, so no await is needed). This restores synchronous throw propagation and removes the misleading deferral implication.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. updateWebGPUBillboards is declared async at WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1006 and grep for 'await' in the entire file returns nothing. updateWebGPUPolylines is async at WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js:1179 with zero awaits in the file. The Point (line 859) and Label (line 751) equivalents are plain non-async functions — confirming the gratuitous divergence. The caller at BillboardCollection.js:713 invokes fr.update(this, frameState, frameState.commandList) with no await and no .catch. The finding correctly notes this is not a frame-ordering bug today (no real await means the body still runs synchronously and pushes commands before returning), but the async signature converts any synchronous throw into an unhandled promise rejection the caller never sees, and the signature falsely implies the command push could be deferred to a microtask. The fix (drop async to match Point/Label) is correct since pipeline resolution already uses the entry.pending + return-null-retry pattern, needing no await. Low severity is right — latent liability, not an active failure.

allMergedFindings.title: Billboard color path writes miscFlags.show = 1.0 unconditionally after already culling non-show billboards — the shader's show<0.5 branch is dead
allMergedFindings.observation: buildInstanceData skips billboards with !bb.show || _clusterShow===false (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:164) AND then writes instanceData[offset+20]=1.0 for the show lane unconditionally (line 220). The WGSL reads miscFlags.x and early-returns a degenerate quad when show<0.5 (BillboardCollection.wgsl:246-247, and again at 603-604 for the pick/velocity VS) — but since the JS never emits a show=0 instance, that branch can never be taken on the color path. Either the CPU-side cull or the GPU-side show test is redundant. Not a bug (the result is correct) but it's dead shader code + a wasted attribute lane, and it diverges from WebGL which keeps hidden billboards in the buffer and relies on the GPU show test.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL writes all billboards (including hidden) and discards them in-shader via the show attribute; WebGPU pre-culls on CPU, making the shader branch unreachable. Either approach is fine but doing both is wasteful.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Pick one: keep the CPU pre-cull (cheaper instance count) and drop the show lane + shader branch, OR keep the show lane and stop pre-culling. CPU pre-cull is the better default for sparse-visibility collections; document that the shader show branch is defensive-only.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. buildInstanceData skips !bb.show || _clusterShow===false billboards (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:164) and then writes instanceData[offset+20]=1.0 unconditionally (line 220); the pick path does the same (cull at 314, write 1.0 at 363). The WGSL reads miscFlags.x and early-returns a degenerate quad when show<0.5 (BillboardCollection.wgsl:246-247 color VS, 603-604 velocity VS). Since the JS never emits a show=0 instance, that branch is unreachable on the color and pick paths — confirming the finding. As the finding itself states, this is NOT a bug (output is correct); it is dead shader code + a wasted attribute lane. The framing that it 'diverges from WebGL which keeps hidden billboards in the buffer' is accurate but the finding correctly concedes the CPU pre-cull is a legitimate (arguably better, for sparse visibility) alternative — the waste is doing BOTH. Low severity is correct; this is a minor cleanup, not a correctness issue.

allMergedFindings.title: disableDepthTestDistance forces clipPos.z = 0.0 with no guard for points behind the camera (w <= 0)
allMergedFindings.observation: The recently-fixed disable-depth path sets clipPos.z = 0.0 to force the marker onto the near plane (BillboardCollection.wgsl:357/361/368, PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl:193/197/204 — verified against the git diff). The fix from clipPos.z = clipPos.w to clipPos.z = 0.0 is correct for WebGPU's [0,1] clip-z and matches the on-top intent. However, when a billboard/point is behind the eye (clipPos.w <= 0) the surrounding code still writes z=0 while leaving w negative; after perspective divide the marker can flip to the near plane on the wrong side and the depth override 'rescues' geometry that should be clipped. WebGL's equivalent (gl_Position.z = -gl_Position.w under [-1,1]) has the same theoretical edge but the translucent collections are typically front-facing so it rarely bites. This is a latent edge case worth a w<=0 guard, especially for disableDepthTestDistance=Infinity always-on markers near the antipode.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL sets z to the near value symmetrically; neither backend guards w<=0, but the WebGPU value (0.0) combined with the less-equal compare makes a behind-camera marker more likely to leak onto the near plane than WebGL's setup.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Guard the depth override with a w>0 check (only force z=0 when clipPos.w > 0.0), or clamp z into [0, w] so the perspective divide stays in-range. Low priority but cheap; add a behind-camera billboard to the disableDepthTestDistance probe to confirm.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. The disable-depth path sets clipPos.z = 0.0 unconditionally with no w-guard in both shaders: BillboardCollection.wgsl:357/361/368 and PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl:193/197/204. The accompanying comments confirm this is the recent fix from clipPos.z = clipPos.w to 0.0 (correct for WebGPU's [0,1] clip-z 'on top' = near plane). The latent edge case is real: when clipPos.w <= 0 (point behind the eye), z is forced to 0 while w stays negative, so after perspective divide z=0/negative-w can land the marker on the near plane on the wrong side and the depth override 'rescues' geometry that should have been clipped. The finding's reasoning is sound and it correctly scopes this as a latent edge case (front-facing translucent collections rarely trigger it) most relevant to disableDepthTestDistance=Infinity always-on markers near the antipode. The proposed fix (gate on clipPos.w > 0.0, or clamp z into [0,w]) is correct and cheap. Low severity stands — narrow, rarely-hit edge case, no broad rendering breakage. Note: this is a genuine correctness nuance, not an intentional WebGPU-specific choice — the [0,1] clip-z handling is correct; the missing w<=0 guard is an independent oversight shared with WebGL.

allMergedFindings.title: PickDepth feature-detection picks the WebGL branch on WebGPU → pickPosition/sampleHeight/clampToHeight depth readback never fires
allMergedFindings.observation: PickDepth.update() (PickDepth.js:100-110) branches on `if (defined(context.readPixels)) { updateFramebuffers(...); updateCopyCommands(...); } else { this._asyncDepthTexture = depthTexture; }`. The async branch is the ONLY place `_asyncDepthTexture` is set, and getDepth()'s async readback path (PickDepth.js:148 `if (defined(this._asyncDepthTexture) && !this._pendingReadback)`) is gated on it. But WebGPUContext.readPixels is a real method (WebGPUContext.ts:2533, returns null), so `defined(context.readPixels)` is TRUE on WebGPU → the WebGL framebuffer branch runs and `_asyncDepthTexture` stays undefined. The WebGPU frustum loop explicitly calls `pickDepth.update(context, packedDepthTex)` (WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:643) intending the async path, but update() routes it to the WebGL FramebufferManager/GLSL copy-command path instead. getDepth() then runs the sync branch, context.readPixels returns null, the Batch-48 `defined(pixels)` guard makes it fall through, then the async branch sees `_asyncDepthTexture===undefined` and returns undefined. Net: pickPosition()/pickPositionWorldCoordinates() always return undefined on WebGPU. The Batch 48 commit message even states the author believed 'context.readPixels on WebGPU is a stub that returns undefined' — it is a stub that returns null but is still a DEFINED method, which is exactly why the branch is wrong.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL: context.readPixels returns a populated Uint8Array, update() builds the framebuffer+copy command, getDepth() unpacks RGBA→float synchronously. pickPosition works.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Change the feature-detection from `defined(context.readPixels)` to something that is actually false on WebGPU — e.g. `if (defined(context.readPixels) && !context.isWebGPU)` is the minimal fix but violates the no-isWebGPU-in-Scene principle; better: gate on a capability flag like `context.supportsSyncReadback` (add a getter returning true on WebGL, false on WebGPU) or have WebGPUContext NOT define readPixels (leave it inherited-undefined) so existing `defined()` checks work as the async authors intended. Then verify pickPosition via a Playwright depth-pick probe.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md DP-H45 (partial/stale — assumes async path is reached; this finding shows it never is)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified directly. WebGPUContext.readPixels (WebGPUContext.ts:2533) is a real, defined instance method that returns null. PickDepth.update (PickDepth.js:103) branches on `if (defined(context.readPixels))` — true on WebGPU — so it runs updateFramebuffers/updateCopyCommands (the WebGL path) and the else-branch that sets this._asyncDepthTexture (line 108) is NEVER reached. getDepth (line 125) then takes the sync path; context.readPixels returns null, the `defined(pixels)` guard at line 137 fails through, then line 148 `defined(this._asyncDepthTexture)` is false → returns undefined. The frustum loop (WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:643) calls pickDepth.update(context, packedDepthTex) intending the async path. `git show ef9b9e465f` ('Remove all context.isWebGPU checks from Scene code') is the commit that swapped an isWebGPU check for this broken `defined(readPixels)` feature-detection. No supportsSyncReadback capability exists. Net: pickPositionWorldCoordinates always returns undefined on WebGPU. This is sharper/more severe than the documented DP-H45 (which assumed _asyncDepthTexture IS set by WebGPUGlobeDepth and only off-globe fails, and is marked 'Status unverified'). Confirmed critical.

allMergedFindings.title: readCenterPixel returns only stale prior-frame pixels → pickMetadata and pickVoxelCoordinate broken on WebGPU
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel() (WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:413-423) reads ONLY `this._lastReadPixels` — populated by `_startReadback`'s fire-and-forget `.then()` from a PRIOR pick frame. But pickMetadata (Picking.js:402-471) and pickVoxelCoordinate (Picking.js:343-397) are synchronous, never call end()/_startReadback for the current render, and call readCenterPixel immediately after resolveFramebuffers but BEFORE context.endFrame() (which is what actually submits the pick render's command encoder). So readCenterPixel returns whatever a previous screen-space pick() left in _lastReadPixels — entirely unrelated to the metadata/voxel render just issued — or zeros if no prior pick ran. The metadata render side exists (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:217 selects pickMetadataCommand), so the geometry is rendered into the pick FBO, but the readback never reads it.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL readCenterPixel (PickFramebuffer.js:155-174) calls context.readPixels synchronously on the just-rendered framebuffer and slices the center pixel — correct, current-frame data. pickMetadata/pickVoxelCoordinate work.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Give WebGPUPickFramebuffer a synchronous-after-submit center-pixel readback, OR add async variants pickMetadataAsync/pickVoxelCoordinateAsync in Picking.js that endFrame→copyTextureToBuffer→await mapAsync→read the center pixel (mirroring the endAsync pattern). At minimum add a one-time warning like drillPick has so callers know metadata/voxel pick is unreliable on WebGPU, and track in DEFERRED_WORK.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md DP-H46 (overlaps pickMetadata, but DP-H46's root-cause is now stale; readback-staleness is the real cause)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel (lines 413-423) reads ONLY this._lastReadPixels, which is populated by _startReadback's fire-and-forget .then() from a PRIOR pick frame (or null). pickVoxelCoordinate (Picking.js:390-396) and pickMetadata (Picking.js:452-463) call begin → updateAndExecuteCommands → resolveFramebuffers → readCenterPixel → context.endFrame(); they never call end()/_startReadback/endAsync for the current render, and readCenterPixel runs BEFORE endFrame() submits the pick encoder. So it returns unrelated prior-pick data or zeros. WebGL readCenterPixel (PickFramebuffer.js:155-174) reads current-frame pixels synchronously. The metadata producing path DOES now exist (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:216-219 routes to pickMetadataCommand), making DP-H46's 'read nowhere in a producing path' claim stale — the render happens but the readback never reads it, which is this finding's more accurate diagnosis. High is appropriate.

allMergedFindings.title: Ray picks (pickFromRay/sampleHeight/clampToHeight) call pickFramebuffer.end() synchronously → prior-frame stale results on WebGPU
allMergedFindings.observation: getRayIntersection (PickingRayHelpers.js:195-245) renders the offscreen pick view then calls `view.pickFramebuffer.end(drawingBufferRectangle, 1)[0]` synchronously (line 220). On WebGPU, end() (WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:300-330) returns the PREVIOUS frame's _lastReadPixels by design (async readback). This is the same staleness class the team already identified and worked around for sync drillPick (Picking.js:622-642 emits a oneTimeWarning + added drillPickAsync), but the ray-pick path was left on the sync end(). Additionally, the depth fallback at PickingRayHelpers.js:226-227 calls `pickDepth.getDepth(context, 0, 0)` expecting a synchronous number, but on the intended WebGPU async path getDepth returns a Promise (defined!) — though per the PickDepth feature-detection bug above it actually returns undefined, so position resolution silently never happens. Net: pickFromRay/sampleHeight/clampToHeight return stale objects and no position on WebGPU.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL end() reads current-frame pixels synchronously and getDepth returns a float; ray picks resolve object+position correctly in one frame.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add an async ray-pick path (the offscreen render + endAsync + awaited getDepth) analogous to drillPickAsync, and route sampleHeight/clampToHeight through it on backends without sync readback. Surface a oneTimeWarning on the sync ray-pick path for WebGPU like drillPick does.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md NEW-DRILLPICK-ASYNC (adjacent — fixed sibling drillPick but NOT the ray-pick path this finding targets)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. getRayIntersection (PickingRayHelpers.js:220) calls view.pickFramebuffer.end(drawingBufferRectangle, 1)[0] synchronously; WebGPUPickFramebuffer.end (lines 300-330) returns the PREVIOUS frame's _lastReadPixels by design. The depth fallback (PickingRayHelpers.js:227) calls pickDepth.getDepth(context, 0, 0) expecting a sync number; per finding 1 that returns undefined → `!defined(depth)` continue → no position. pickFromRay/drillPickFromRayHelper/sampleHeight/clampToHeight all funnel through this sync getRayIntersection (no async ray-pick path exists — confirmed grep). drillPick's staleness was fixed via drillPickAsync (DEFERRED_WORK NEW-DRILLPICK-ASYNC, Batch 184) but the ray-pick path was explicitly left on sync end() with no async analog and no oneTimeWarning. Confirmed high.

allMergedFindings.title: endAsync shares _stagingBuffer with _startReadback but ignores _readbackInFlight gate
allMergedFindings.observation: _startReadback (line 429-504) guards against re-encoding a copy to _stagingBuffer while a prior mapAsync is pending via `_readbackInFlight`. But endAsync (line 336-407) encodes copyTextureToBuffer into the SAME `this._stagingBuffer` and awaits mapAsync on it WITHOUT checking or setting `_readbackInFlight`. If a sync pick() (→_startReadback sets _readbackInFlight, leaves buffer mapping-pending/mapped) is followed in the same window by a pickAsync() (→endAsync), the submit will hit 'Buffer used in submit while mapped' / mapAsync on an already-mapped buffer will reject. The single shared mutable staging buffer is the fragile choice.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL PickFramebuffer.endAsync (PickFramebuffer.js:83-118) allocates a FRESH pbo + Sync per call and destroys both in `finally` — concurrent/overlapping async picks are independent and safe.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either make endAsync respect+set _readbackInFlight (await/skip when in-flight), or allocate a per-call staging buffer like the WebGL PBO path. Given pickAsync can be called concurrently (hover + click), per-call buffers are the durable fix.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. _startReadback (lines 429-504) guards re-encoding a copy into _stagingBuffer with _readbackInFlight and sets/clears it. endAsync (lines 336-407) encodes copyTextureToBuffer into the SAME this._stagingBuffer and awaits mapAsync WITHOUT checking or setting _readbackInFlight. Picking.js confirms both paths are reachable on the same FBO: pickAsync calls endAsync (Picking.js:311-312), sync pick calls end()→_startReadback (Picking.js:338). A sync pick() leaving the buffer mapping-pending followed by a pickAsync() in the same window can submit a copy targeting the mapped buffer ('Buffer used in submit while mapped') or double-map. WebGL endAsync (PickFramebuffer.js:83-118) allocates a fresh PBO+Sync per call and frees in finally — independent/safe. The single shared mutable staging buffer is the fragile choice. Requires a specific interleave (hover-sync + click-async), so medium is right.

allMergedFindings.title: Orphaned depth-pick scaffolding: _readableDepthTexture / readableDepthView / readDepthPixelAsync have zero consumers
allMergedFindings.observation: A depth32float `_readableDepthTexture` is allocated on every pick FBO resize (line 240-245) as a RENDER_ATTACHMENT|COPY_SRC target, and getter `readableDepthView` (578) plus `readDepthPixelAsync` (514) implement a full single-pixel depth readback. A repo-wide grep shows ZERO consumers of readableDepthView or readDepthPixelAsync outside this file. The actual pickPosition depth path goes through PickDepth + WebGPUGlobeDepth's packed-color texture instead, so this is a parallel depth-pick mechanism that was scaffolded but never wired. Per CLAUDE.md Principle 7 I checked the module docstring (lines 6-12) — it claims the depth32float target is 'for pickPosition', but pickPosition does not use it. Note: the depth attachment is also never actually attached by the pick render pass (WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts uses pickFBO.depthView = the depth24plus-stencil8, not the readable one), so it is allocated+cleared but never even written.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no equivalent duplicate — PickDepth owns depth readback exclusively.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Do NOT remove yet (scaffolding rule), but add a clear docstring note that this depth32float path is currently inert and that pickPosition routes through PickDepth, OR finish wiring it (attach _readableDepthView in the pick pass descriptor and route pickPosition's depth read through readDepthPixelAsync) to retire the PickDepth.update feature-detection bug above. Track under a DEFERRED_WORK entry so it isn't mistaken for dead code or silently deleted.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. Repo-wide grep shows readableDepthView and readDepthPixelAsync are referenced ONLY inside WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts (definitions at lines 514, 578). The _readableDepthTexture (depth32float, allocated lines 240-245) is never attached by the pick pass: WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:141 attaches pickFBO.depthView (= _depthView = the depth24plus-stencil8 texture, set at line 252/281), not the readable one — so it is allocated+cleared but never even written. The real pickPosition depth path routes through PickDepth + WebGPUGlobeDepth's packed-color texture. This is genuine inert scaffolding. Per CLAUDE.md Principle 7 it should NOT be removed, only documented — the recommendation already says so. Low/code-quality confirmed.

allMergedFindings.title: PickId.normalizedRgba (alpha forced to 1.0) is documented 'for WebGPU' but has no consumers
allMergedFindings.observation: PickId precomputes `normalizedRgba = Float32Array([r,g,b,1.0])` (PickId.js:34-39) documented as the WebGPU encoding. Every actual WebGPU renderer uploads `_pickId.color.{red,green,blue,alpha}` instead (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:1800-1803, WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js:256-259, etc.), which preserves the full 32-bit key including the alpha byte = (key>>24)&0xff. normalizedRgba would have been a latent bug if used (its forced alpha=1.0 would corrupt the round-trip for keys >= 2^24, and break the 'RGB!=0' decode for any future alpha-keyed scheme), but it is simply unused. The WebGPUContext.ts:2539 comment still advertises it as the WebGPU encoding.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGL uses the uint32 key directly. The decode in both backends now reconstructs from RGB(+A) bytes consistently.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either delete normalizedRgba and its mentions (it's genuinely unreferenced and not scaffolding for a tracked feature) or, if kept for a future direct-float-upload path, fix its alpha to (key>>24)/255 so it matches color.alpha and document the intended consumer. Update the WebGPUContext.ts:2539 comment which currently misrepresents it as the live WebGPU encoding.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. PickId.normalizedRgba = Float32Array([r,g,b,1.0]) (PickId.js:39, alpha hardcoded 1.0). Grep shows it is referenced only in docstrings/declarations (PickId.js:7, GraphicsContext.ts:1183, WebGPUContext.ts:2539, PickId.d.ts:25) — never read by a renderer. The actual WebGPU upload uses pickColor.{red,green,blue,alpha} from the full Color (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:1800-1803), preserving the 32-bit key including alpha byte = (key>>24)&0xff. So normalizedRgba is unused dead-ish code whose forced alpha=1.0 would be a latent round-trip bug if ever used. The WebGPUContext.ts:2539 comment misrepresents it as the live WebGPU encoding. Not scaffolding for a tracked feature. Low.

allMergedFindings.title: Pick-pass base-command skip drops translucent OIT pick coverage that WebGL retains
allMergedFindings.observation: executePickBatch (WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:284-316) skips any command for which selectCommandVariant returns it UNCHANGED and which is not a dedicated pick command (pickOnly/_isPickCommand), to avoid the FORK-34 attachment-incompatibility validation error. The comment asserts 'the geometry's real pick command is either its resolved variant or a sibling pickOnly draw'. This holds for renderers that emit a derivedCommands.picking variant or a pickOnly sibling, but any TRANSLUCENT command that lacks a built pick variant (e.g. legacy/agnostic DrawCommands routed through OIT that rely on the base material being drawn into the pick FBO with blending off, the way WebGL does) is silently dropped — it contributes no pick ID. WebGL's performIdPass renders the base command into the pick FBO directly (no attachment validation), so those translucent objects remain pickable there.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL Scene performIdPass executes every pass command (including base translucent draws) into the single-attachment pick FBO; attachment-count is not validated at draw time, so base commands paint pick color and stay pickable.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Audit which translucent/agnostic commands reach the pick pass without a derivedCommands.picking variant; for those, build a pick variant (single-attachment, blend-off) rather than skipping, or down-convert their pipeline to the pick attachment format on the fly. Confirm parity with a translucent-primitive pick probe (e.g. translucent polygon / billboard with alpha).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The webglComparison is factually wrong, which collapses the finding. WebGL's performIdPass (SceneRenderer.js:444-451) calls executeIdCommand per command, and executeIdCommand (SceneRenderer.js:110-135) renders ONLY the derived pick variant: if derivedCommands is undefined → return (nothing); if derivedCommands.picking → execute picking.pickCommand; else if derivedCommands.depth → execute depthOnlyCommand; else → NOTHING. It NEVER paints the base material into the pick FBO. So a translucent command without a pick variant contributes no pick ID on WebGL either — identical to WebGPU's executePickBatch (WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:314 skips !resolvedPickVariant && !isDedicatedPick). selectCommandVariant returns d.picking.pickCommand when a pick variant exists (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts) — same coverage as WebGL. The premise 'WebGL renders base translucent draws into the pick FBO so they stay pickable' does not match the WebGL code. The FORK-34 skip is a correct WebGPU-specific guard that matches WebGL behavior, not a parity regression. (Genuinely-pickable translucent objects DO build a derivedCommands.picking variant via createPickDerivedCommand and render it on both backends.)

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:103 silent return on missing/typeless pick FBO swallows a pick failure
allMergedFindings.observation: executePickPass returns silently (no log) when passState.framebuffer is missing or lacks the _isWebGPUPickFBO discriminator (lines 103-107), and again when device/encoder are absent (110-124). The comment says 'this shouldn\'t happen, but be safe'. Per CLAUDE.md logging rules, a pick pass that no-ops because its FBO wasn\'t published is a real failure the user needs to diagnose (every pick returns undefined) — it should emit a permanent console.error sentinel, not return silently. This is exactly the BUG-12/13 class of null-target failure the project rules call out for permanent sentinels.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL pickBegin always has a valid framebuffer from FramebufferManager; there's no silent-skip equivalent.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add a throttled console.error with the context ID when the pick FBO is missing/untyped or the encoder is null, so a misconfigured pick pass is visible rather than manifesting as universally-undefined picks.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. executePickPass returns silently with no log when passState.framebuffer is missing or lacks _isWebGPUPickFBO (lines 103-107) and again when device/encoder are absent (lines 110-124); the comment says 'this shouldn't happen, but be safe'. Per CLAUDE.md logging rules, a pick pass that no-ops because its FBO wasn't published is a real null-target failure (every pick returns undefined) of the BUG-12/13 class the rules call out for permanent console.error sentinels. The observation is accurate; severity low (diagnostic-quality, not a functional bug on its own). A throttled console.error with context ID is the right fix.

allMergedFindings.title: _pickPositionCache keyed by windowPosition.toString() returns cached value even when underlying pickPosition is broken on WebGPU
allMergedFindings.observation: pickPositionWorldCoordinates caches results keyed by windowPosition.toString() (Picking.js:487-494) and caches `undefined` on miss (line 603). On WebGPU where the depth readback is async, the first call kicks off (or, per the PickDepth bug, fails to kick off) a readback and returns/caches undefined; the cache then short-circuits subsequent same-position calls to undefined until update() flips _pickPositionCacheDirty next frame. Combined with the async depth path returning a Promise that resolves a frame late, the cache can persistently serve undefined for a stationary cursor. This is acceptable for the async-resolves-later design only if the Promise branch (lines 587-594) is actually reached — which it is not, due to the PickDepth _asyncDepthTexture bug. So the cache amplifies that bug into 'pickPosition never resolves for a held cursor'.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL resolves depth synchronously so the cache is populated with the real value on first call; no staleness.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Once the PickDepth async path is fixed, ensure the Promise-returning branch does not write `undefined` into the cache for the in-flight frame (only cache resolved values), so a stationary cursor converges to the real position on the next frame rather than sticking at undefined.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. pickPositionWorldCoordinates caches by windowPosition.toString() (Picking.js:487-494) and writes undefined into the cache on full miss (line 603); on a cache hit it returns the cached value early (line 493). The Promise branch (lines 587-594) only triggers if getDepth returns a thenable — which, per finding 1, it never does on WebGPU (returns undefined), so the sync path runs, finds no depth, and caches undefined. Combined, a stationary cursor sticks at undefined until _pickPositionCacheDirty flips next frame, re-runs, re-caches undefined. The cache amplifies the finding-1 bug rather than causing it; it is a contributing factor and its own caching-of-undefined-in-flight defect (the recommendation to only cache resolved values is correct). Low; mostly subsumed by fixing finding 1.

allMergedFindings.title: CSM receive path drops soft-shadow PCF kernel and normal-shading that WebGL supports
allMergedFindings.observation: sampleOneCascade (ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:107) uses a single textureSampleCompareLevel tap (only the hardware 2x2 bilinear PCF). The CSM receive path ignores effects.shadowSoftShadows entirely — there is no multi-tap PCF kernel and no normal-shading visibility clamp. The WebGL canonical path czm_shadowVisibility (shadowVisibility.glsl:42-59) does a 9-tap PCF cross when USE_SOFT_SHADOWS, and applies USE_NORMAL_SHADING (visibility *= clamp(nDotL/smooth)). The WebGPU single-shadow-map path even keeps a sampleShadowMapPCF 3x3 branch gated on shadowSoftShadows (PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl computeShadowFactor:347-349), so CSM is a regression relative to BOTH the WebGL CSM and the WebGPU single-map path. Result: when a user enables soft shadows, single-map shadows soften but cascaded shadows stay hard-edged with no signal that the setting was ignored.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL czm_shadowVisibility applies a 9-tap PCF kernel (USE_SOFT_SHADOWS) plus normal-shading clamp; WebGPU CSM applies neither, so soft-shadow toggling is a silent no-op for cascades.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add a PCF branch to sampleOneCascade gated on effects.shadowSoftShadows (a 3x3 or 5-tap cross over the cascade layer's texel size, identical structure to sampleShadowMapPCF), and optionally fold the normal-shading clamp into computeShadowFactorCSM. The comparison sampler is already PCF-ready. Track explicitly so the gap isn't mistaken for shipped soft-shadow support.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified in both the canonical helper (ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl sampleOneCascade:107-113, single textureSampleCompareLevel tap, no shadowSoftShadows reference, no normal-shading clamp) AND the production-inlined copy in PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl (sampleOneCascade:253-270, computeShadowFactorCSM:298-307 — neither references effects.shadowSoftShadows nor applies a normal-shading visibility clamp). The WebGL canonical path czm_shadowVisibility (shadowVisibility.glsl:42-59) does a 9-tap PCF cross under USE_SOFT_SHADOWS and czm_private_shadowVisibility:4-11 applies the USE_NORMAL_SHADING clamp. Critically, the WebGPU single-shadow-map path in the SAME file DOES honor the toggle: computeShadowFactor:342-343 branches on effects.shadowSoftShadows>0.5 to call sampleShadowPCF (a 3x3 kernel, lines 210-222). So CSM is a confirmed regression relative to BOTH the WebGL CSM and the WebGPU single-map path — enabling soft shadows softens single-map shadows but is a silent no-op for cascades. The comparison sampler is already PCF-ready, so the fix is the structural addition the finding describes. Note CSM_DESIGN.md:327 lists 'Verify the existing PCF/softShadows path composes with cascade selection' as a Slice 2 task that is demonstrably NOT done, but that line is a planning bullet, not a documented known-gap, so this stays confirmed-real rather than already-documented.

allMergedFindings.title: Clustered-light assign dirty-tracking ignores cluster-bounds changes → stale bins on resize/FOV change
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUClusterAssignRenderer.dispatch (line 324) skips re-dispatch when checksum === _lastLightsChecksum, where the checksum (lines 284-320) is built ONLY from light count + eye-space positions/types. The assignment also depends on the cluster AABBs (bounds), which change on viewport/FOV/near-far changes (WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer dispatches independently on those). The module's own header (lines 13-25) states the assignment depends on cluster bounds. Camera MOTION is covered transitively (lights are CPU-transformed to eye-space, so positions change → checksum changes). But a pure viewport resize or programmatic FOV/near-far change WITHOUT camera or light motion re-dispatches bounds yet SKIPS assign — leaving per-cluster light indices computed against the OLD AABBs. Lights then bin into the wrong clusters until something moves.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL equivalent (clustered lighting is WebGPU-only), but the bug is an internal correctness drift from the documented dependency contract.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Fold a cluster-bounds generation counter (the bounds renderer already tracks (viewport, near, far, projection) dirtiness) into the assign dirty key, or force an assign re-dispatch whenever the bounds renderer re-dispatched this frame. The dispatcher already knows both — pass the bounds-dirty flag into _assign.dispatch.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified WebGPUClusterAssignRenderer.dispatch:324-326 skips re-dispatch when checksum === _lastLightsChecksum, and the checksum (lines 284-321) is built ONLY from clampedCount + per-light posOrDir.xyz + type. The bind group only rebuilds when the clusterAABBs BUFFER identity changes (line 343, _lastClusterAABBs !== clusterAABBs), but the bounds renderer reuses the same storage buffer for its lifetime (its header notes 'same buffer for the life of a ClusterBoundsRenderer instance'), so recomputed AABB CONTENTS in that same buffer never trigger a reassign. WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer's own header (lines 13-23) confirms bounds depend on (viewport, near, far, projection) and re-dispatch on viewport resize / FOV / near-far changes independent of camera motion. The dispatcher (WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.dispatch:236-248) calls _bounds.dispatch then _assign.dispatch every frame, but _assign internally skips on the lights-only checksum. So a pure viewport resize or programmatic FOV/near-far change with no camera or light motion re-dispatches bounds but skips assign, leaving per-cluster light indices computed against stale AABBs. The finding mis-paraphrases the assign-renderer header (the header at lines 22-25 actually says re-dispatch is NOT required and the bounds-change case is 'rare in practice' — it acknowledges the dependency exists but argues it usually coincides with camera motion), but the underlying correctness drift on the no-motion path is real. Medium severity is fair: the documented mitigation ('usually coincides with camera motion') means the window is narrow but genuine (resize-only, programmatic FOV).

allMergedFindings.title: Per-frame dead-write of cull SoA (centerX/Y/Z/radius) arrays in CSM cast cull loop
allMergedFindings.observation: In the per-cascade GPU-cull path, the loop at lines 350-353 writes soa.centerX/centerY/centerZ/radius for every cast command every cascade every frame, but only soa.interleaved (lines 355-358) is ever uploaded (subarray at line 375). The SoA scalar fields are never read anywhere; the comment at lines 316-320 admits they are 'kept alongside for potential future use (debug surface, sphere-sphere narrow-phase) but populated in lockstep.' This is confirmed write-only data (the consumer — interleaved — already exists), not scaffolding awaiting a consumer. For N cast commands × C cascades that is 4N extra typed-array stores per cascade per frame for nothing. At the cull-activation threshold (2400+ commands) this is 4*2400*4 ≈ 38k wasted stores per frame.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGPU-only GPU-cull infrastructure.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Drop the centerX/Y/Z/radius SoA fields and keep only the interleaved pool (rename the struct accordingly), or guard the SoA writes behind a debug pragma. Removing them also shrinks the per-cascade scratch allocation.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts:350-353 writes soa.centerX/centerY/centerZ/radius for every command, while only soa.interleaved (lines 355-358) is uploaded via subarray at line 375. A repo-wide grep confirms host._cascadeCullSoA's scalar fields are never read anywhere — the soa.centerX reads in WebGPUGPUSortKeysDispatcher/WebGPUHiZOcclusionDispatcher/WebGPUSceneRenderer reference a DIFFERENT SoA object (the opaque/sort-keys path), not the CSM cast pass's _cascadeCullSoA. The code comment (lines 316-320) explicitly admits the SoA fields are 'kept alongside for potential future use ... but populated in lockstep.' This is confirmed write-only data, not consumer-pending scaffolding (the consumer — interleaved — already exists). The wasted-store math (4N per cascade per frame, gated at 2400+ commands) is correct. Low severity is appropriate: only active above the cull threshold, and it's pure typed-array stores. Note Principle 7 (don't remove scaffolding) gives mild cover for leaving it, but the finding's recommendation to guard behind a debug pragma rather than delete respects that.

allMergedFindings.title: Per-frame array allocation in clustered-lighting dispatch (_scratchEyeLights.slice)
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.dispatch passes this._scratchEyeLights.slice(0, activeCount) (line 247) to _assign.dispatch every frame clustered lighting is active. The .slice() allocates a fresh array each frame purely to bound the length, defeating the explicitly-pooled _scratchEyeLights (the field's own comment, line 121, says 'reused each dispatch to avoid GC'). The assign renderer only reads lights[0..clampedCount), so the slice is unnecessary — pass the pooled array plus an explicit count.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGPU-only.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Change WebGPUClusterAssignRenderer.dispatch to take (lights, count) or have it read activeCount, and pass the pooled _scratchEyeLights directly. Eliminates one per-frame heap allocation in the render hot path.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.dispatch:247 passes this._scratchEyeLights.slice(0, activeCount) to _assign.dispatch every frame clustered lighting is active (activeCount>0 path). The field comment at line 121 states it is 'reused each dispatch to avoid GC', so the .slice() allocating a fresh array each frame defeats the pooling intent. WebGPUClusterAssignRenderer.dispatch:278 immediately does clampedCount = Math.min(lights.length, CLUSTER_MAX_LIGHTS) and only iterates [0..clampedCount), so passing the pooled array + an explicit count would be equivalent. Real per-frame heap allocation in the render path. Low severity is correct — one small array alloc per frame, only when clustered lighting is active.

allMergedFindings.title: Per-cast-pass Cartesian3 allocations contradict the 'no per-frame allocation' scratch claim
allMergedFindings.observation: renderCSMCastPass allocates `new Cartesian3(cameraPositionWC.x, .y, .z)` on line 243-244 (passed to EncodedCartesian3.fromCartesian) plus two `?? new Cartesian3()` for enc.high/low on lines 241-242, on every cast invocation.
