The module-level _scratchEncodedCamera (line 57) exists specifically to avoid per-frame allocation, and the renderer's own docstring (WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:73-77) claims the scratch avoids per-frame allocation — but the input Cartesian3 wrapper is freshly allocated each call. CSM cast runs once per frame, so this is 1-3 small allocs/frame, minor, but it undercuts the stated zero-alloc contract and is trivially fixable.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGPU-only RTE encode path.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Hold a module-level scratch Cartesian3 for the camera position and set its x/y/z from cameraPositionWC instead of constructing a new one; the enc.high/low fields are already persistent on _scratchEncodedCamera (its .d.ts guarantees them) so the `?? new Cartesian3()` fallbacks can be dropped.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified renderCSMCastPass:243-246 calls EncodedCartesian3.fromCartesian with a freshly-constructed new Cartesian3(cameraPositionWC.x,.y,.z), plus enc.high = enc.high ?? new Cartesian3() and enc.low = enc.low ?? new Cartesian3() at lines 241-242. The module scratch _scratchEncodedCamera (line 57 in CastPass, line 78 in CSMRenderer) and its docstring (CSMRenderer.ts:75-77, 'reused across frames to avoid per-frame allocation in the RTE encode path') claim zero-alloc, but the input Cartesian3 wrapper is allocated each call. CSM cast runs once per frame so this is 1 (steady-state) to 3 (first frame) small allocs/frame — minor, but it does undercut the stated contract and is trivially fixable with a module-level scratch Cartesian3 whose x/y/z are set in place. The ?? new Cartesian3() fallbacks are dead after the first frame (EncodedCartesian3's .d.ts guarantees high/low persist) but harmless. Low severity correct.

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPU CSM hardcodes 4 cascades; WebGL supports numberOfCascades of 1
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUCSMRenderer defaults to and is effectively locked at 4 cascades: the receive shader hardcodes cascadeVP0..3 (ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:25-29), selectCascade has 4 fixed branches (44-49), and CSMParams packs exactly 4 vec4 splits/biases. WebGL's ShadowMap (ShadowMap.js:316,341-343,461-463) explicitly supports numberOfCascades of 1 OR 4. While _cascadeCount is configurable in the constructor, the WGSL receive struct + selectCascade cannot consume anything but 4, so non-4 counts would silently misbehave. This is mostly a non-issue since 4 is the only useful CSM count, but the configurability in the renderer is a false affordance that doesn't reach the shader.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL ShadowMap supports 1 or 4 cascades and adjusts numberOfPasses; WebGPU CSM is shader-locked to 4 despite a configurable _cascadeCount field.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either clamp/assert _cascadeCount to 4 at construction (make the lock explicit) or generalize selectCascade + CSMParams to a runtime cascadeCount loop. The assert is the cheap correct fix.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the WGSL receive struct hardcodes cascadeVP0..3 (ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:26-29 and the inlined copy in PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl:234-240), selectCascade has 4 fixed branches (ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:44-49), CSMParams packs exactly 4 vec4 splits/biases, and getCascadeVP switches on 4 cases. Meanwhile WebGPUCSMRenderer constructor:285 sets this._cascadeCount = config?.cascadeCount ?? DEFAULT_CASCADE_COUNT (4) with NO clamp or assert to 4 — and computeSplits:390-401, the texture array depthOrArrayLayers (line 339), and the cascade loops (315, 348, 451, 511) all honor _cascadeCount. So a config.cascadeCount of e.g. 2 or 1 would allocate a 1-2 layer array and pack 1-2 splits, but the shader's selectCascade would still index up to layer 3 (out of bounds) and read uninitialized cascadeVP2/3. The configurable _cascadeCount is a genuine false affordance that doesn't reach the shader. The finding correctly notes 4 is the only useful CSM count and recommends the cheap fix (assert/clamp to 4). Low severity is right — no current caller passes non-4, but the unguarded config path is a real latent footgun.

allMergedFindings.title: Slice 3/4 CSM features unshipped: altitude-adaptive splits, spot/moon cascades, VSM soft shadows, WebGL CSM parity
allMergedFindings.observation: CSM_DESIGN.md marks Slice 3 (altitude-adaptive splits / orbital-regime single-cascade collapse, moon dual-light cascades, VSM rg32float soft shadows) and Slice 4 (3D-Tiles per-tile cascade culling, snapshot-freeze contract, WebGL CSM parity path, full visual verification) as Pending. Confirmed in code: computeSplits (WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:387-402) uses fixed practical-split lambda with no altitude term, so at orbital altitude cascades waste their budget on empty space (the design doc itself flags this); there is no moon-cascade array; the receive uses depth32float single-tap, no variance texture; and getStatistics exposes no isFreezable contract. WebGL has no CSM-on-WebGPU-parity wiring either. None of this is a regression — it is explicitly-deferred work — but it is the bulk of remaining CSM scope and should remain surfaced as next-work per CLAUDE.md Principle 9.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's integrated CSM has cascade culling and is the canonical reference; WebGPU CSM is at Slice 2 (cast variants + texel snap + receivers) and lacks the orbital/moon/VSM/3D-Tiles-culling features.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Keep Slice 3/4 tracked in CSM_DESIGN.md (it is). The single highest-value next item is altitude-adaptive splits — without it CSM is visibly wasteful at any aerial/orbital Cesium camera, which is the common case. Recommend prioritizing that over VSM.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/CSM_DESIGN.md (Status line 3; Slice 3 row line 16; Slice 4 row line 17; feature-interaction matrix lines 185-191)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified against CSM_DESIGN.md: line 3 states 'Slice 1 SHIPPED. Slices 2-4 pending'; line 16 (Slice 3) lists altitude-adaptive splits, orbital single-cascade collapse above ~500km, moon dual-light cascades, and VSM-style rg32float soft shadows as Pending; line 17 (Slice 4) lists 3D-Tiles per-tile cascade culling, snapshot-freeze contract, WebGL parity path, full visual verification as Pending. The feature-interaction matrix (lines 185-191) reiterates each. Code-side claims also verified: computeSplits:387-402 uses a fixed practical-split lambda with no altitude term (line 189 explicitly flags this wastes budget at orbital altitude); no moon-cascade array exists; receive is depth32float single-tap with no variance texture. This is explicitly-deferred work, correctly tracked — not a regression. Per Principle 9 it should stay surfaced as next-work, which the finding does. Severity none because nothing is broken; it is documented scope.

allMergedFindings.title: Cluster bounds are not re-dispatched per multi-frustum slice — single near/far only
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer's header (lines 25-31) explicitly notes multi-frustum is unhandled: 'each frustum slice has its own (near, far) so the cluster grid would need to be re-bound per slice. Today the renderer only ever runs one set of bounds at a time.' The dispatcher (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2479-2485) computes a single near/far from cam.frustum and dispatches once. Cesium uses multi-frustum splitting for large depth ranges (the very scenes where clustered lighting matters), so the cluster Z-slices only correctly cover ONE frustum's near/far; fragments in other frustum slices get binned with the wrong eye-Z→slice mapping (clusterIndexFor clamps out-of-range Z to the last slice), collapsing many fragments into cluster slice 23 and over/under-including lights. For typical small single-frustum demo scenes this is invisible, which is why the probes pass.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — clustered lighting is WebGPU-only; the gap is internal to the Forward+ design.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either document the single-frustum limitation as a hard constraint on clusteredLightingEnabled (and warn when multi-frustum is active), or extend the dispatcher to re-run bounds+assign per frustum slice with per-slice params. Until then, surface it as a known WIP rather than implying full multi-light support.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer header lines 25-30 explicitly call out the multi-frustum gap: 'each frustum slice has its own (near, far) so the cluster grid would need to be re-bound per slice. Today the renderer only ever runs one set of bounds at a time.' Verified the dispatcher call site WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2474-2491 collapses to a single near/far from cam.frustum (lines 2479-2480) with the comment at 2470-2473 confirming 'Per-frustum-slice cluster bounds are a future optimization.' Cesium does use multi-frustum splitting for large depth ranges, so the cluster Z-slices only correctly cover one frustum's range; sliceZ (ClusterBounds.wgsl:85-91) builds the exponential distribution from that single near/far, and out-of-range eye-Z clamps into the last slice — collapsing far-frustum fragments and mis-binning lights. This is genuine functionality-gap. It IS noted in the bounds renderer's own header as a known limitation, but the finding's value is surfacing it as a hard constraint on clusteredLightingEnabled (warn on multi-frustum) rather than silent. Treating the header comment as informal in-code documentation rather than a tracked migration-doc entry, I leave this confirmed-real at medium; the finding's recommendation (document the constraint + warn, or extend per-slice) is the right next step per Principle 9.

allMergedFindings.title: Cast-pass command resolution leans on broad unknown-cast duck typing without a hard error sentinel on full-skip
allMergedFindings.observation: renderCSMCastPass walks castCommands as `unknown` and silently `continue`s on every unresolved shape (no vertex buffer, null layoutKey, null variant, missing extra binding, unresolved multi-VB slot — lines 422,456,467,470,478,538,593,600). If a whole frame's commands fail resolution (e.g., a layout-key regression), every cascade renders an empty depth map and shadows silently vanish with zero diagnostics. The single-shadow-map path has a one-time warning for unknown layouts; the CSM loop has none. Per CLAUDE.md's 'permanent sentinels' guidance, a no-cast-emitted frame at high command count is exactly the failure mode that should log once.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL ShadowMap derives receive commands deterministically and would not silently emit empty cascades; the WGPU loop's all-skip path is undiagnosable.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Track drawn-vs-skipped counts in the cascade loop and emit a throttled console.warn (pragma-free, since empty shadows is a real bug) when a cascade draws 0 of N>0 commands. Cheap, catches the layout-key regression class.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified renderCSMCastPass walks castIter as untyped commands and silently `continue`s on every unresolved shape: no resolvable VB (line 455), null vb (457), null layoutKey (467), null variant (470), null pipelineEntry (478), missingBinding (538), unresolved multi-VB slot (593), missing modelInstanced VB (600). No drawn-vs-skipped accounting and no warning if a whole cascade emits zero draws from N>0 commands. By contrast the single-shadow-map path documents a sentinel: WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js:111 'Unknown layouts are skipped silently after a one-time warning' with a console.warn at line 620. So the CSM loop is strictly less diagnosable than the path it was forked from. CLAUDE.md's 'permanent sentinels' guidance (null target guard, size validation) and the 'no-cast-emitted at high command count' failure mode squarely match this. A layout-key regression would make cascades render empty depth and shadows vanish with zero console signal. The finding correctly recommends a pragma-free throttled warn (empty shadows is a real bug, not debug noise). Low severity is fair — it's a diagnosability/robustness gap, not an active incorrectness.

allMergedFindings.title: Misleading 'Z grows positive forward' comments in cluster shaders (not a bug, but a maintenance trap)
allMergedFindings.observation: ClusterBounds.wgsl comments (lines 36-40, 88-89) assert 'in Cesium WebGPU eye-space, Z grows positive forward (camera looks toward +Z)'. This contradicts the actual convention documented elsewhere in the same codebase (ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:1467 'looking -Z in EC', :2533 '|positionEC.z| ... looking -Z convention'). The math is self-consistent and correct because sliceZ produces a positive scalar that is converted to NDC and unprojected through the REAL inverseProjection (which yields true Cesium -Z eye space), and the assign/FS sides all use abs() — so there is no runtime bug. But the false convention comment will mislead the next engineer who tries to add an eye-space term (e.g., a CPU-side AABB sanity assert) and assumes +Z forward.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — documentation accuracy issue in WebGPU-only shaders.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Correct the comments to state that the slice scalar is a positive distance, but the resulting eye-space AABBs are in Cesium's -Z-forward convention via inverseProjection. No code change needed.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified ClusterBounds.wgsl comments at lines 37-40 ('in Cesium WebGPU eye-space, Z grows positive forward (camera looks toward +Z)') and lines 88-89 ('Returns eye-space Z (positive forward)'). This contradicts the convention documented elsewhere in the same codebase: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:1467 'looking -Z in EC' and :2533-2534 '|positionEC.z| ... Cesium's looking -Z convention'. The finding correctly assesses this as NOT a runtime bug: sliceZ produces a positive scalar fed through the real inverseProjection (ClusterBounds.wgsl:76-80 unprojectNdcToView), which yields true Cesium -Z eye space, and downstream consumers use the projection consistently. I could not find an abs()-on-Z in ClusterAssign.wgsl (the finding's 'assign/FS sides all use abs()' is slightly imprecise — ClusterAssign processes lights-vs-AABBs by gid and has no per-fragment Z-to-slice mapping), but that does not undercut the core claim: the +Z-forward comment in ClusterBounds.wgsl is factually wrong about the eye-space convention and will mislead the next engineer adding an eye-space term or CPU-side AABB assert. Comment-accuracy issue, low severity, doc-only fix. Confirmed-real as a code-quality finding.

allMergedFindings.title: OIT MRT composite pipeline hardcoded to rgba8unorm — mismatches the actual bgra8unorm/rgba16float scene color, failing pipeline validation
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUOIT._createCompositePipeline() builds the composite render pipeline with `targets: [{ format: "rgba8unorm", ... }]` (WebGPUOIT.ts:295) and the comment 'Will be overridden at draw time if HDR' — but it is NEVER overridden. executeComposite(encoder, targetView, targetFormat) (line 222) receives `targetFormat` and ignores it entirely; it just begins a render pass against `targetView` using the fixed-rgba8unorm pipeline. The caller passes `context._sceneColorFormat` which defaults to `bgra8unorm` (WebGPUContext.ts:389) and becomes `rgba16float` in HDR. WebGPU requires the pipeline color-target format to match the attachment texture format, so the OIT composite render pass fails validation (bgra8unorm != rgba8unorm) every time the MRT OIT path is taken — i.e. whenever isSupported && useOIT && !picking && a translucent command has an _oitPipeline. The net effect is the entire weighted-blended OIT path is non-functional / errors, and translucent geometry either vanishes or falls back inconsistently.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL OIT.js builds its composite command's RenderState/framebuffer against the actual opaque FBO format and works for both float and 8-bit paths; there is no fixed-format pipeline object.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Cache the composite pipeline per target format (or rebuild it in update() using the passed scene color format) and key it on `_sceneColorFormat`. At minimum, thread `targetFormat` into pipeline creation instead of the literal 'rgba8unorm', and rebuild when the format changes (HDR toggle).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Re-read confirms every claim. WebGPUOIT._createCompositePipeline() (WebGPUOIT.ts:295) hardcodes `targets: [{ format: "rgba8unorm", ... }]` with the comment 'Will be overridden at draw time if HDR', but executeComposite(encoder, targetView, targetFormat) (lines 222-254) never uses targetFormat — it begins a render pass against targetView with the fixed pipeline. The caller (WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts:200-208) passes context._sceneColorView + context._sceneColorFormat. _sceneColorFormat is assigned `_sceneFramebuffer.colorFormat` in BOTH WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1093 and WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:193 — i.e. bgra8unorm in SDR, rgba16float in HDR — NEVER rgba8unorm (default WebGPUContext.ts:389 is bgra8unorm). WebGPU requires pipeline color-target format == attachment format, so the composite pass fails validation whenever the MRT OIT path runs. That path IS reachable: WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1060 sets cmd._oitPipeline, and the translucent pass auto-builds _oitPipeline for any opt-in command (TranslucentPass.ts:121-140). NOT documented: FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:592 notes only that dual-source single-pass OIT isn't wired; the format mismatch is unmentioned. Severity critical is justified for the OIT code path, though I note the practical blast radius is narrower than 'entire weighted-blended OIT is non-functional' — it only bites commands that actually populate _oitPipeline (Gaussian splats + explicit opt-ins), not all translucent geometry (which falls back to back-to-front alpha at TranslucentPass.ts:218-228).

allMergedFindings.title: Tonemapper mode mapping reads a non-existent property — user's scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper is always ignored on WebGPU
allMergedFindings.observation: mapTonemapType (WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:174) does `const type = collection._tonemapping?.type ?? collection._tonemappingType;` then switches on numeric 0-4. But `_tonemapping` is a PostProcessStage instance (no `.type` field) and `_tonemappingType` does not exist on the collection (grep confirms neither exists in PostProcessStageCollection.js). The real selector is `_tonemapper`, a STRING enum ('REINHARD','ACES','PBR_NEUTRAL', etc. — Tonemapper.js). So `type` is always undefined and the switch always hits `default → PBR_NEUTRAL`. The user can set scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper = Cesium.Tonemapper.ACES and WebGPU silently keeps PBR_Neutral. Additionally, even if a numeric type were supplied, the case-to-mode mapping is internally inconsistent (the comment claims FILMIC=2/ACES=3 while the WGSL Tonemapping shader uses ACES=1/FILMIC=2).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL swaps the tonemapping shader (createAcesTonemappingStage etc.) based on the string tonemapper value via PostProcessStageCollection.set tonemapper(); the selection is honored.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Read `collection.tonemapper` (the string), map 'REINHARD'/'MODIFIED_REINHARD'/'FILMIC'/'ACES'/'PBR_NEUTRAL' → the TonemapMode constants, and remove the bogus numeric `.type` read. Add a unit test asserting each string maps to the matching WGSL mode.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Core claim verified. mapTonemapType (WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:174-190) reads `collection._tonemapping?.type ?? collection._tonemappingType`. In PostProcessStageCollection.js, `_tonemapping` (lines 46, 359) is a PostProcessStage/Composite instance created by PostProcessStageLibrary.create*TonemappingStage — it has no `.type` field; `_tonemappingType` does not exist anywhere in the file (grep confirms). The real selector is `_tonemapper`, a string enum ('REINHARD'/'ACES'/'PBR_NEUTRAL'/... per Tonemapper.js), exposed via the getter at line 299 and switched on (string) in the setter at lines 320-347. So `type` is always undefined and mapTonemapType always returns TonemapMode.PBR_NEUTRAL (default branch). A user setting scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper = Tonemapper.ACES is silently ignored on WebGPU. The fix (read collection.tonemapper string) is correct. ONE imprecision in the finding's secondary claim: it says the case-to-mode mapping is 'internally inconsistent (comment claims FILMIC=2/ACES=3 while WGSL uses ACES=1/FILMIC=2)'. In fact the switch maps the (hypothetical) CesiumJS numeric `case 2 -> TonemapMode.FILMIC` and `case 3 -> TonemapMode.ACES`, and TonemapMode.FILMIC=2 / TonemapMode.ACES=1 match the WGSL shader exactly — so IF a numeric type were ever supplied the enum resolution would actually be correct. The real and only bug is the always-undefined read. Core finding stands; downgrading from the implied 'two bugs' to one. High severity confirmed (user-facing tonemapper selection broken).

allMergedFindings.title: Bloom uses a different algorithm and mis-maps WebGL's brightness/contrast uniforms onto a luminance threshold
allMergedFindings.observation: The stage collection maps `cache.bloomThreshold = numU(bloom.uniforms.brightness, 0.8)` and feeds it to BrightPass as a luminance `threshold` (WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:223, 313). But in WebGL, bloom's `brightness` uniform default is -0.3 and is an HSB brightness ADD applied in a contrast-bias pre-stage (PostProcessStageLibrary.createBloomStage: contrast=128, brightness=-0.3), NOT a luminance threshold. So a user-set brightness of -0.3 makes the WebGPU bright-pass `threshold` negative → everything passes the bright filter; the WebGL `contrast` (128) is dropped entirely (the WGSL contrast uniform is hardcoded to 1.0 in WebGPUBloomEffect._createUniforms). The two bloom algorithms (WebGPU: max(color - threshold*avgLum,0); WebGL: HSB contrast/brightness bias then blur) produce visibly different glow for the same user uniforms.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL bloom = ContrastBias(contrast, brightness, glowOnly) → GaussianBlur(delta,sigma,stepSize) → composite. The uniforms are contrast/brightness/glowOnly/delta/sigma/stepSize, none of which is a luminance threshold.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either port the WebGL contrast/brightness/HSB bright-pass semantics to the WGSL BrightPass and map all six uniforms, or document the intentional algorithm swap and at least stop feeding `brightness` as `threshold` (it inverts the effect). Map contrast→contrast, glowOnly→glowOnly, delta/sigma/stepSize→blur.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:223+313 map `bloomThreshold/threshold = numU(bloom.uniforms.brightness, 0.8)` and feed it as BrightPass `threshold`. In WebGL (PostProcessStageLibrary.js:388-396), createBloomStage's contrastBias stage defaults `contrast: 128.0, brightness: -0.3`, where brightness is an HSB-brightness ADD in a ContrastBias pre-stage (the JSDoc at lines 376-377 confirms 'converted to HSB then this value is added to the brightness', default -0.3), NOT a luminance threshold. BrightPass.wgsl:43 computes `max(color.rgb - threshold*avgLum, 0)`, so a brightness of -0.3 makes threshold negative -> everything passes the bright filter (inverts the intended gate). WebGL contrast (128) is dropped: WebGPUBloomEffect._createUniforms (line 421) hardcodes the BrightPass contrast component to 1.0. The two algorithms genuinely differ (WGSL: luminance-threshold subtraction; WebGL: HSB contrast/brightness bias then Gaussian blur). High severity appropriate — visible glow differs for identical user uniforms and the default brightness inverts the effect.

allMergedFindings.title: Built-in complex effects (Bloom/AO/DoF/GodRay) allocate 8-bit intermediates even in HDR mode, clamping HDR through the effect
allMergedFindings.observation: addBloom/addAmbientOcclusion/addDepthOfField/addGodRay (WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:710-835) initialize each effect with `canvasFormat` (SDR bgra8unorm), not `_intermediateFormat` (rgba16float in HDR). The effects build ALL their intermediate + output textures in that format (e.g. BloomEffect._createTextures uses `format` for bright/blur/composite; AO output texture uses `format`). When scene.highDynamicRange is on, the ping-pong/scene color is rgba16float but the bloom bright-pass + composite and AO modulate run through 8-bit textures, clamping the HDR scene color to [0,1] before tonemap — defeating bloom's whole purpose (bloom is supposed to capture >1.0 highlights). Notably the USER stage path was explicitly fixed for this (Batch 199 B198-D1 switched addUserWGSLStage to `_intermediateFormat`), but the built-in effects were left on `canvasFormat`.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL bloom/AO run against the HDR scene FBO (FramebufferManager picks the FLOAT pixel datatype when useHdr); the effect chain stays in HDR until the tonemap stage.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Pass `this._intermediateFormat` (not `canvasFormat`) to addBloom/addAmbientOcclusion/addDepthOfField/addGodRay, matching the user-stage fix. The final composite/output of each effect must be HDR-format so tonemap sees real HDR. Add an HDR bloom probe to visual-regression.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. addBloom (WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:703-716), addAmbientOcclusion (722-730), addDepthOfField (804-812), addGodRay (823-836) all call effect.initialize(device, w, h, canvasFormat) — passing the SDR canvasFormat, not _intermediateFormat. BloomEffect._createTextures (WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:336-362) builds bright/blurTemp/blurResult/composite textures in that `format`; AmbientOcclusionEffect._createTextures (line 283) builds _outputTex in `format` too. By contrast addUserWGSLStage (763-786) explicitly overrides to `this._intermediateFormat` (line 783) with a comment citing the Batch 199 B198-D1 HDR-precision fix, and the SDR single-pass stages also use _intermediateFormat (lines 504/561/617). So the built-in effects were demonstrably left on canvasFormat while the user-stage path was fixed — the asymmetry the finding describes is real. In HDR (scene.highDynamicRange) the ping-pong/scene color is rgba16float but bloom bright-pass + composite and AO modulate run through 8-bit, clamping >1.0 highlights before tonemap. High severity justified — defeats bloom's purpose in HDR. (Note: the recommendation must also verify the effects' execute() blends back into the rgba16float chain, but the texture-format defect itself is confirmed.)

allMergedFindings.title: Pipeline.destroy() leaks TAA history textures, ColorGrading UBO, and all user stages on every HDR toggle / recreate
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.destroy() (line 1441-1472) destroys tonemap/fxaa/custom UBOs and bloom/ao/dof/godray/autoExposure, but NEVER touches `_taaEffect` (which owns two full-res history textures — rgba16float in HDR, the largest buffers in the chain, with its own destroy() at WebGPUTAAEffect.ts:702), `_colorGradingStage.uniformBuffer`, or `_userStages` (each owns intermediate textures + a UBO; clearUserWGSLStages() exists but isn't called). WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:393-399 destroys+recreates the whole pipeline on every HDR toggle, so these leak per toggle. The TAA history-texture leak alone is significant on repeated HDR/resolution changes.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL PostProcessStageCollection.destroy() / PostProcessStageTextureCache release all stage framebuffers and textures; no per-toggle leak.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: In destroy(): call this._taaEffect?.destroy(); this.clearUserWGSLStages(); this._colorGradingStage?.uniformBuffer?.destroy(); and null all three. Also null _taaEffect/_colorGradingStage.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.destroy() (lines 1441-1472) destroys tonemap/fxaa/custom UBOs and bloom/ao/dof/godray/autoExposure, but never references _taaEffect, _colorGradingStage, or _userStages — all of which exist as owned resources (declared at lines 231, 223, 236). _taaEffect owns two full-res history textures (rgba16float in HDR) with its own destroy() at WebGPUTAAEffect.ts:702-717. _colorGradingStage is a CompiledStage with a uniformBuffer (lines 562, 578). _userStages each own textures + a UBO and clearUserWGSLStages() exists (793-798) but isn't called from destroy(). WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:389-395 destroys+recreates the whole pipeline whenever `_hdr !== hdr`, so these leak per HDR toggle. The recommended fix (call _taaEffect?.destroy(); clearUserWGSLStages(); _colorGradingStage?.uniformBuffer?.destroy()) is correct. Medium severity appropriate — GPU memory leak proportional to toggle count, largest being the two TAA full-res rgba16float history textures.

allMergedFindings.title: OIT weight function and composite math diverge from WebGL; weight uses window-space z instead of view-space z
allMergedFindings.observation: The WGSL injected weight (WebGPUOIT.ts:417 csm_oitWeight) is `clamp(a * max(1e-2,min(3e3, 10/(1e-5 + pow(z/5,2) + pow(z/200,6)))), 1e-2, 3e2)` — the McGuire Eq.9 form. WebGL's czm_alphaWeight (alphaWeight.glsl) is the Eq.10 form `pow(a+0.01,4) + max(1e-2, min(3e3, 0.003/(1e-5 + pow(abs(z)/200,4))))`. They are different weighting functions, so depth-ordering of overlapping translucent surfaces will look different between backends. Worse, the WGSL passes `param.position.z` (csm_oitOutput call, line 477) which is window-space depth [0,1], whereas the WebGL function reconstructs a linearized z via the viewport transformation before plugging into the weight — so even the same formula would weight differently. The composite math also differs: WGSL composite does `accum.rgb/max(accum.a,eps)` with `alpha = 1 - revealage`, while WebGL MRT composite does `accum.rgb/clamp(revealage,1e-4,5e4)` using `accum.a` as transparency, and additionally forces out.a=1 when opaque != czm_backgroundColor (the background-preservation rule is absent in WGSL).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: See alphaWeight.glsl (Eq.10, view-space z) and CompositeOITFS.glsl (MRT branch divides accum.rgb by revealage, uses accum.a for blend, background-color alpha fix).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Match WebGL: use the Eq.10 weight, feed a linearized view-space z (reconstruct from depth like alphaWeight.glsl does), and port the composite formula including the czm_backgroundColor → alpha=1 rule. This matters for splats + translucent primitives that already route through OIT.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified against the cited shaders. WGSL csm_oitWeight (WebGPUOIT.ts:417-419) is the McGuire Eq.9 form `clamp(a*max(1e-2,min(3e3, 10/(1e-5 + pow(z/5,2) + pow(z/200,6)))), 1e-2, 3e2)`. WebGL czm_alphaWeight (alphaWeight.glsl:4-11) is the Eq.10 form `pow(a+0.01,4) + max(1e-2, min(3e3, 0.003/(1e-5 + pow(abs(z)/200,4))))`, and it reconstructs z from gl_FragCoord.z via czm_viewportTransformation (line 6) — i.e. a linearized/view-space-derived z. The WGSL wrapper (line 477) passes `param.position.z` which in WGSL @builtin(position) is window-space depth in [0,1]. Composite math also differs: WGSL OIT_COMPOSITE (lines 69-75) does `accum.rgb/max(accum.a,eps)` with `alpha = 1 - reveal`, while CompositeOITFS.glsl MRT branch (lines 19-25) does `accum.rgb/clamp(r,1e-4,5e4)` using `accum.a` as transparency, plus the `if (opaque != czm_backgroundColor) out.a = 1.0` rule (lines 27-30) which has no WGSL equivalent. All three divergences confirmed and undocumented (audit FORK_FEATURE_INVENTORY:84 notes only the pick-path gap). Medium severity is fair — affects ordering/appearance of overlapping translucent surfaces + splats routed through OIT, but only on the OIT code path.

allMergedFindings.title: User GLSL post-process stages silently dropped in production builds (warning is pragma-stripped)
allMergedFindings.observation: Custom stages added via scene.postProcessStages.add(...) only run on WebGPU if the user supplies a `wgslFragmentShader` uniform (WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:416). Any standard GLSL PostProcessStage — including the entire PostProcessStageLibrary (BlackAndWhite, Brightness, NightVision, LensFlare, Silhouette, user-added stages) — is counted as glslOnly and dropped. The only signal is a oneTimeWarning wrapped in `//>>includeStart('debug', pragmas.debug)` (lines 465-477), so in a production (non-debug) build the user gets ZERO indication their effect does nothing. This is tracked as NEW-POSTPROCESS-USER-WGSL, but the silent-in-production behavior and the breadth (all library stages) are worse than a typical WIP gap.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL compiles and runs the GLSL fragmentShader for every added stage; the whole PostProcessStageLibrary works.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: (a) Move the warning out of the debug pragma so production users see it (it's a real functionality loss, not a per-frame diagnostic). (b) Longer-term, wire the existing WebGPUShaderTranslator/Naga path to transpile the library's GLSL stages, or ship WGSL equivalents of the PostProcessStageLibrary builtins so the common stages work without user WGSL.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md (NEW-POSTPROCESS-USER-WGSL) — documents the GLSL-drop as by-design, but NOT the pragma-stripped/production-silent warning nor the library-stage breadth
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified, and the distinct contribution (production-silent) is NOT already covered by the tracked entry. The configure loop (WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:396-463) only runs a stage when it carries a string `wgslFragmentShader` uniform (line 417); every other stage increments glslOnlyCount (line 461). The ONLY user signal is oneTimeWarning at lines 466-476, wrapped in `//>>includeStart('debug', pragmas.debug)` ... `//>>includeEnd('debug')` (465/477) — so it is stripped from production (non-debug) builds, leaving zero indication. Per CLAUDE.md's own logging rules, a real functionality loss should NOT be debug-pragma-wrapped (that category is for per-frame diagnostics). DEFERRED_WORK.md (NEW-POSTPROCESS-USER-WGSL, lines 736-769, 2755-2769) documents the GLSL-drop as a by-design limitation and treats the warning as 'the intended surfacing' — but it does NOT note that the surfacing itself vanishes in production, nor the breadth (entire PostProcessStageLibrary: BlackAndWhite/Brightness/NightVision/LensFlare/Silhouette). The finding's actionable item — move the warning out of the debug pragma — is real and untracked. High severity for the silent-loss aspect; the broader 'port the library' work is correctly deferred elsewhere.

allMergedFindings.title: Altitude-gate fade of Bloom + AutoExposure is a gratuitous behavioral divergence from WebGL
allMergedFindings.observation: BloomEffect (applyAltitudeGate, default enableAltitudeGate=true, orbitFloor=0.15) and WebGPUAutoExposure (default enableAltitudeGate=true, orbitFloor=0.75) fade their effect strength toward neutral as the camera rises to orbit. This is a deliberate 'orbit polish' addition with no WebGL equivalent. The result: with the same scene.bloom.enabled=true and the same uniforms, a user comparing WebGL vs WebGPU at orbital altitude sees ~15% bloom on WebGPU vs full bloom on WebGL, and auto-exposure adaptation muted to 25% strength. Per the audit contract this is behavior that diverges from WebGL without being forced by the backend. It may be intentional, but it's on by default and not surfaced through the public API, so it silently breaks backend parity for split-screen / regression comparisons.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL bloom/auto-exposure apply uniformly regardless of camera altitude.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Default enableAltitudeGate to false so WebGPU matches WebGL out of the box, and expose it as an explicit opt-in scene/effect option. If kept on by default, document it in FEATURE_INVENTORY as an intentional WebGPU-only divergence and exclude bloom/exposure from the WebGL-vs-WebGPU visual-regression parity gate.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the code (BloomEffect: enableAltitudeGate default true at WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:155, altitudeGateOrbitFloor default 0.15 at :158; WebGPUAutoExposure: enableAltitudeGate default true at :143, altitudeGateOrbitFloor default 0.75 at :146) — the behavior the finding describes is accurate. HOWEVER this is an explicit, tracked, intentional WebGPU-specific divergence with documented design rationale, NOT an unflagged drift. DEFERRED_WORK.md lines 3221-3232 (NEW-ORBIT-BLOOM-ALTITUDE-GATE, marked RESOLVED Session 65 Batch 22) documents the smoothstep gate, the deliberate 0.15 floor (vs 0.0) to preserve Rayleigh-limb haze, the paired WebGPUAutoExposure.applyAltitudeGate (Batch 39), and the escape hatches (`altitudeGateOrbitFloor: 0` or `enableAltitudeGate: false`). The rationale (bloom-as-camera-lens-effect, real orbital photography) is in CELESTIAL_ATMOSPHERE_DESIGN.md §13.1. So per the audit contract this is an intentional, surfaced divergence. The finding's process recommendation (note it in FEATURE_INVENTORY and exclude bloom/exposure from the parity gate) has merit and isn't yet in FEATURE_INVENTORY, but the divergence itself is documented, so it is not a bug. isPortRegression:false is correct.

allMergedFindings.title: Dead/no-op f16 tonemap error-scope: pushErrorScope/popErrorScope with no work between them never detects a compile failure
allMergedFindings.observation: In _compileStage (lines 1360-1384) the f16 fallback path calls `device.createShaderModule(...)` BEFORE `device.pushErrorScope('validation')`, then immediately `device.popErrorScope().then(...)`. No GPU operation is enqueued between the push and pop, so the error scope captures nothing — a failing f16 shader module or pipeline is created outside the scope and the .then(err) callback never fires. The elaborate comment block (lines 1339-1359) describing 'next-frame recovery' is aspirational; no recovery path actually exists. So the claimed f16→f32 fallback silently does nothing; a bad f16 variant just produces a broken/black tonemap with the real error surfacing only as an uncaught device error elsewhere.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A (f16 is WebGPU-only).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either wrap the createShaderModule + createRenderPipeline calls inside the push/pop scope and actually rebuild with the f32 fallbackWgslCode when err fires, or remove the dead error-scope and the misleading comment and rely on the permanent createShaderModule compilation-info error. Pick the f32 source up front when the device lacks shader-f16.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified, and the finding actually refutes a STALE doc claim. In _compileStage (WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:1360-1384): device.createShaderModule(...) is called at 1360 BEFORE device.pushErrorScope('validation') at 1366, then device.popErrorScope().then(...) at 1367 with NO GPU operation enqueued between push and pop — so the scope captures nothing. The shaderModule and the subsequent createRenderPipeline (line 1417) both use the f16 module synchronously regardless of the (never-firing) callback. The elaborate comment (1339-1359) describes 'next-frame recovery via the renderer's top-level recovery path', but grep finds no such path — the only effect of a failure is a console.error (1376-1381), and the code itself admits 'We can't synchronously rebuild the pipeline from here'. Notably, audits/2026-04-30_FORK_FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:110 and MAINTAINABILITY:67 CLAIM a working 'f16 -> f32 fallback verified at WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:1069-1094' — but lines 1069-1094 are the single-pass-chain assembly (verified by reading them), not a fallback, and the actual f16 error-scope at 1360-1384 is the dead one. So the finding correctly identifies that the documented auto-fallback does not exist. Low severity is fair (f16 is opt-in and the permanent createShaderModule compilation-info error still surfaces), but the misleading comment + false audit claim warrant the fix.

allMergedFindings.title: OIT pipeline cache key keyed on shaderCode.length is collision-prone
allMergedFindings.observation: createOITPipeline caches by `${shaderCode.length}_${fragEntry}_${config.label ?? ''}` (WebGPUOIT.ts:511) and the shader module cache uses the same key. Two distinct shaders with the same character length, same entry point, and same/empty label collide and reuse the wrong injected OIT module/pipeline. label is often the owner constructor name ('auto' or e.g. 'Primitive'), which is NOT unique per shader variant, so collisions are realistic for different geometry of the same primitive class. The result is a wrong-shader translucent draw with no error.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL OIT derives shader variants from the actual ShaderProgram cache keyed on full source + defines, so no length-collision risk.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Key the cache on a hash of the full oitCode (or the input shaderCode) plus entry + a stable per-command pipeline signature, not shaderCode.length. A cheap FNV/DJB2 hash of the source string is sufficient and removes the collision class.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. createOITPipeline (WebGPUOIT.ts:511) builds `cacheKey = `${shaderCode.length}_${fragEntry}_${config.label ?? ''}`` and uses the SAME key for both _oitPipelineCache (512) and _oitShaderCache (519/525). Two distinct shaders with identical character length, same fragment entry, and same/empty label collide and reuse the wrong injected OIT module/pipeline with no error. The label is frequently non-unique: the translucent-pass auto-build path (WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts:126) passes `cmd.owner?.constructor?.name ?? 'auto'`, i.e. a class name shared by all instances of that primitive class. So two different-geometry-but-same-class commands whose generated WGSL happens to match in length would collide. Realistic, silent, wrong-shader translucent draw. The recommended FNV/DJB2 hash of the full source fixes the collision class. Low severity is appropriate — requires a length+entry+label collision to trigger, so it is a latent correctness hazard rather than a guaranteed failure.

allMergedFindings.title: Camera jitter accumulates unboundedly on a stable frustum (never restored)
allMergedFindings.observation: Scene.js:5230-5234 applies jitter with `const proj = cam.frustum.projectionMatrix; proj[8] += jitter.x; proj[9] += jitter.y;` and there is no un-jitter/restore anywhere (grep for proj[8]/proj[9]/-=jitter finds only the += sites). PerspectiveFrustum.projectionMatrix (Core/PerspectiveFrustum.js:259-262) calls update(this), which early-returns at line 395-397 when fov/aspectRatio/near/far/xOffset/yOffset are unchanged, returning the SAME Matrix4 object that was mutated last frame. So whenever the frustum params are stable (a still camera, or a slow orbit that doesn't change fov/near/far — the exact case TAA targets), proj[8]/[9] receive a fresh `+= jitter` every frame on top of the prior accumulated value. The offsets do not cancel (IGN is not zero-mean over short windows), so the projection's row-2 entries drift, shearing geometry progressively off-center. The TAA shader's unjitter only subtracts the single-frame jitterOffset (TAA.wgsl:337), so it cannot compensate for the accumulated render skew, and snapshot/freeze mode (5219-5221 zeroes taa.jitterX but leaves proj[8]/[9] at their accumulated value) cannot recover the drift either — directly contradicting the design's 'frozen scene shows zero accumulation drift over 600 frames' acceptance criterion.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no TAA jitter path, so there is no direct counterpart. A correct implementation must either snapshot the unjittered projection and restore it after the frame, or set the absolute jitter (write a clean projection then apply offset), not accumulate with +=.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Do not mutate the cached frustum matrix in place with +=. Either (a) recompute/clone the clean projection each frame and set proj[8]=baseValue+jitter.x absolutely, or (b) cache the previous jitter and apply (newJitter - prevJitter) as the delta, restoring (-prevJitter) at frame end. Add a spec that renders N stable-frustum frames and asserts proj[8]/[9] stay bounded.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified in full. Scene.js:5230-5234 does `const proj = cam.frustum.projectionMatrix; proj[8] += jitter.x; proj[9] += jitter.y;` and grep across Source/ confirms the ONLY proj[8]/proj[9] mutation sites are these two `+=` lines (the WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:935-937 hits are matrix-vector reads, not jitter restores). PerspectiveFrustum.projectionMatrix (Core/PerspectiveFrustum.js:259-262) calls update(), which early-returns (line 395-397) when fov/aspectRatio/near/far/xOffset/yOffset are unchanged. The off-center frustum it delegates to (PerspectiveOffCenterFrustum.update, lines 465-474) ALSO early-returns when left/right/top/bottom/near/far are unchanged, so Matrix4.computePerspectiveOffCenter is NOT re-run and the getter returns the same cached `_perspectiveMatrix` object (line 430). Therefore on a stable frustum the identical Matrix4 receives a fresh `+= jitter` every frame with no clean rebaseline. IGN jitter (computeJitter: (hx-0.5) is not zero-mean over short windows) accumulates, drifting row-2 entries. TAA.wgsl:337 unjitters only the single-frame jitterOffset and snapshot-freeze (5219-5221) zeroes taa.jitterX but leaves proj[8]/[9] accumulated — directly contradicting TAA_DESIGN.md:218 acceptance criterion 'frozen scene shows zero accumulation drift over 600 frames.' Genuine, actionable bug. High severity stands.

allMergedFindings.title: Per-model previous-frame clip position is computed in single-precision world space (RTE violation)
allMergedFindings.observation: ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:808-814 computes `worldPosPrevious = material.previousModelMatrix * vec4<f32>(prevPositionMC,1.0)` then `output.previousClipPos = camera.previousViewProjection * worldPosPrevious`, while the current-frame term uses the RTE path `camera.mvpRelativeToEye * vec4(rte,1.0)`. WebGPUModelRenderer.js:312 sources `camera.previousViewProjection` from `uniformState.previousViewProjection` — the FULL (non-RTE) previous view-projection. So the previous-frame screen position is reconstructed via full single-precision world coordinates at Earth scale (~6.37e6 m), where FP32 ULP is ~0.76 m. computeMotionVectorScreenSpace (1110-1115) then subtracts curNdc (RTE-precise) from prevNdc (world-precise), so the velocity carries the prev term's multi-pixel FP32 quantization noise. The VS comment at 807 explicitly accepts this: 'RTE is a current-frame optimization that the prev-frame matmul doesn't share.' TAA_DESIGN.md's 'Slice 1 shipped — RTE motion-vector math' section warns this exact world-space reconstruction 'loses precision at the world-space reconstruction step — motion-vector error becomes multi-pixel during orbital fly-to.'
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL TAA path exists. But CLAUDE.md's mandatory RTE rule applies to all rendering paths: 'NEVER multiply mvp * vec4(position,1.0)'. The depth-reprojection path in TAA.wgsl already demonstrates the correct RTE-relative approach (cameraDelta in eye space); the per-model path should mirror it.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Compute the previous clip in eye-relative space: pack previousViewProjectionRelativeToEye (already on UniformState) and a previousModelMatrixRelativeToEye, and form prevPositionRTE before the matmul, matching the current-frame RTE path. This is the same fix the design doc prescribes for Slice 1.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:808-814: current-frame velocity uses RTE (`camera.mvpRelativeToEye * vec4(rte,1.0)`) but previous uses full world space (`material.previousModelMatrix * vec4(prevPositionMC,1.0)` -> `camera.previousViewProjection * worldPosPrevious`). VS comment at 804-807 explicitly accepts this ('RTE is a current-frame optimization that the prev-frame matmul doesn't share'). WebGPUModelRenderer.js:312-314 packs `uniformState.previousViewProjection` (the FULL non-RTE matrix). TAA_DESIGN.md:75 warns this exact world-space reconstruction 'loses precision... motion-vector error becomes multi-pixel during orbital fly-to,' and lines 171-172 + 102 prescribe the RTE prev-frame fix (`prevWorldRTE = (positionHigh - prevCamH) + (positionLow - prevCamL); prevClip = prevViewProjection * vec4(prevWorldRTE,1.0)`) with `previousEncodedCameraHigh/Low`. So the divergence is real and the doc itself names the prescribed fix. Severity adjusted to medium: AUDIT_2026_05_02.md:226 documents the IDENTICAL non-RTE prev pattern for Voxel (`prevClip = prevVP x modelMatrix x modelPos`) and calls it 'correct TAA reprojection for the dominant case' — i.e. this is a recognized, accepted approximation whose error only manifests as multi-pixel velocity noise during fast orbital fly-to (transient, masked by the disocclusion clamp), not a render-breaking defect. Real but not high.

allMergedFindings.title: Shared CameraUniforms chunk is missing the DP-H41 previousViewProjection tail; field is dead in Globe/Primitive shaders
allMergedFindings.observation: CLAUDE.md DP-H41 states 'Every renderer's CameraUniforms struct MUST carry previousViewProjection: mat4x4<f32> at the tail.' The canonical shared chunk chunks/structs/CameraUniforms.wgsl (the #import source of truth) does NOT contain previousViewProjection at all — it ends at modelViewProjectionRelativeToEye (offset 304). The field instead lives only in hand-copied per-shader CameraUniforms structs (PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl:57, GlobeTerrain.wgsl:91, ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:85). Worse, grep confirms previousViewProjection is only actually CONSUMED in ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:812 — in PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl and GlobeTerrain.wgsl it is a declared-but-never-read struct field (the globe/primitive motion vectors come exclusively from TAA.wgsl depth reprojection, the intended Option C). So the field is a 64-byte-per-frame UBO upload of dead data in those shaders, and the per-struct duplication invites layout drift between copies.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGL-side has no equivalent struct. This is purely a WGSL contract/consistency issue.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either (a) add previousViewProjection to the canonical chunk and route the per-shader structs through the #import so the contract is centrally enforced, or (b) explicitly document that Globe/Primitive use depth-reprojection only and DROP the unread field from those structs to reclaim the UBO tail. Pick one; the current state is the worst of both — duplicated AND partially dead.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified all three claims. (1) The canonical shared chunk chunks/structs/CameraUniforms.wgsl ends at modelViewProjectionRelativeToEye (offset 304, total 368 bytes) with NO previousViewProjection — violating CLAUDE.md DP-H41 ('Every renderer's CameraUniforms struct MUST carry previousViewProjection at the tail'). (2) The field is hand-copied into per-shader inline structs: PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl:57, GlobeTerrain.wgsl:91, ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:85 — these shaders define their own `struct CameraUniforms` rather than #import-ing the chunk (the chunk IS imported by CsmBuiltins.js but lacks the field). (3) `camera.previousViewProjection` is CONSUMED only in ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:812; in PrimitivePhongColor and GlobeTerrain it appears only in the struct declaration + a comment, never read — confirmed dead-but-declared (those paths use TAA.wgsl depth reprojection, Option C). So the state is genuinely 'duplicated AND partially dead.' Real architecture/consistency issue. Medium is appropriate (no runtime breakage; 64-byte dead UBO tail + layout-drift risk across hand-copied structs).

allMergedFindings.title: TAA runs pre-tonemap on linear/HDR color, contradicting the design's post-tonemap SDR requirement for variance clamping
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:1038-1067 executes _taaEffect.execute() on `currentView` BEFORE the tonemap/colorGrading/FXAA single-pass chain (pushed at 1069-1092), and the comment at 1042 explicitly states 'TAA always operated on the pre-tonemap, linear/HDR currentView.' But TAA_DESIGN.md §'Frame pipeline order' (lines 143-151) and §'HDR pipeline interaction' (line 211) both state TAA must run AFTER tonemapping/color-grading so its history accumulates perceptually-uniform SDR values, and that 'if the HDR pipeline fix lands (promoting ping-pong to rgba16float), TAA must move to before tonemapping AND the variance clamp thresholds must be retuned for the wider value range.' TAA.wgsl's clamp uses a fixed Reinhard tonemapWeight (78-84) and a tonemap-space 3x3 AABB tuned for SDR; on raw HDR (values >>1), the Reinhard compression and the AABB bounds behave very differently, weakening the disocclusion clamp and risking ghosting/fireflies — the opposite of TAA's purpose.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL TAA. The concern is internal consistency between the shipped pipeline order and the documented design intent + the clamp's numeric tuning.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Decide deliberately: if TAA stays pre-tonemap (HDR), retune the variance clamp for linear HDR and update TAA_DESIGN.md to match; if it should be SDR, move the execute() call after the tonemap/colorGrading stages. The current code silently diverges from its own design doc.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The code-vs-design divergence is real. WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:1047-1067 runs `_taaEffect.execute()` BEFORE the tonemap/colorGrading single-pass chain (pushed 1071-1085); the comment at 1038-1046 confirms 'TAA always operated on the pre-tonemap, linear/HDR currentView.' TAA_DESIGN.md:142-151 + 211 say TAA should run AFTER tonemap/colorGrading in the SDR case and only move before tonemap in HDR mode (rgba16float) WITH the variance clamp retuned. I confirmed `_intermediateFormat` is bgra8unorm (SDR) by default, rgba16float only in HDR mode (lines 348). The clamp uses a fixed Reinhard tonemapWeight (TAA.wgsl:78-84) and was NOT retuned. So the divergence (SDR-mode design says post-tonemap; code is pre-tonemap; HDR-mode clamp un-retuned) is genuine. Severity kept medium but note the finding overstates impact: Reinhard `c/(1+luminance)` is specifically a firefly-suppression operator that DOES compress HDR (so the clamp doesn't 'behave very differently' to the point of failing) — the actionable core is the documented code/doc inconsistency + un-retuned clamp, not a guaranteed ghosting regression.

allMergedFindings.title: Edge emitter uses single-precision model-space position + non-RTE MVP (precision loss at planetary scale)
allMergedFindings.observation: The EDGE_EMITTER_WGSL vertex shader (WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:39-170) declares `CameraUniforms { modelViewProjection: mat4x4<f32>, modelView: mat4x4<f32> }` and computes `posClip = camera.modelViewProjection * vec4<f32>(input.position, 1.0)` with `position: vec3<f32>` (line 119, attribute at 634). Edge geometry positions are stored as raw model-space FP32 (extractEdgeGeometry pushes positionData directly, 482-499). For a 3D Tile / glTF model anchored anywhere on the globe, an MVP*vec4(pos,1) with single-precision pos quantizes to ~sub-meter at best and jitters the rasterized edge lines — the very RTE failure mode CLAUDE.md forbids ('NEVER multiply mvp * vec4(position,1.0)', 'NEVER use a single position: vec3<f32> in vertex buffers'). WebGL's EdgeVisibilityStageVS.glsl, by contrast, runs through Cesium's standard czm_modelViewProjection with high/low position handling.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's EdgeVisibilityPipelineStage emits edges through the model's normal RTE-aware position pipeline (high/low split), so edges stay locked to geometry at planetary scale. The WebGPU emitter drops that, producing edge shimmer/offset on globe-anchored tilesets.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Feed positionHigh/positionLow into the edge emitter and use an RTE MVP (mvpRelativeToEye + translateRelativeToEye), matching every other WebGPU primary pass. The CPU extractEdgeGeometry already has the source positions to split.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The code facts are verified: WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:39-42 declares `CameraUniforms { modelViewProjection, modelView }`, line 58 `position: vec3<f32>` (attr float32x3 at line 634), line 119 `posClip = camera.modelViewProjection * vec4(input.position,1.0)`. WebGPUModelRenderer.js:3456-3459 EXPLICITLY admits 'Standard RTE isn't applied... Future: switch to RTE when an edge-enabled model gets used at planet-scale distances.' So a real, self-acknowledged precision gap exists relative to the WebGPU main-model path which uses true per-vertex RTE high/low. HOWEVER the finding's WebGL comparison and isPortRegression:true are FALSE: I read EdgeVisibilityStageVS.glsl — WebGL's edge stage uses `czm_modelViewProjection * vec4(v_positionMC,1.0)` (lines 51,54,72) and `gl_Position` from GeometryStageVS which is `czm_projection * (modelView * vec4(positionMC,1.0))` (GeometryStageVS.glsl:8,15) — NOT a per-vertex high/low split. Both backends compute a model-relative MVP in FP64 on CPU (Matrix4 is FP64) and apply it to single-precision model-space positions in-shader. The WebGPU emitter's `mvp = us.viewProjection * modelMatrix` (WebGPUModelRenderer.js:3465) is the same precision regime as WebGL's czm_modelViewProjection. So this is NOT a port regression vs WebGL's edge stage; it is a divergence only from WebGPU's own RTE main-model path. Downgraded to low: equivalent to WebGL edge precision; matters only for very-large-extent models far from camera, already flagged as future work in-code.

allMergedFindings.title: extractEdgeGeometry is O(triangles) per frame with string-keyed edge map and unbounded JS arrays — no caching shown
allMergedFindings.observation: extractEdgeGeometry (291-526) builds a `Map<string,number[]>` keyed by template-literal strings `${a},${b}` for every triangle edge (registerEdge, 366-377) and a second `Set<string>` of `${small},${big}` for dedupe (385-414), plus `verts: number[]` / `idx: number[]` growable arrays that are then copied into typed arrays (519-523). String key construction + Map/Set churn for every edge of every triangle is a large per-extraction allocation/GC cost on dense meshes. The function takes raw primitive/positionData and returns fresh buffers; nothing in the signature memoizes by primitive identity, so if a caller invokes this per-frame (vs once at load), it re-CPU-builds the entire edge topology each frame.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's EdgeVisibilityPipelineStage builds edge geometry once at primitive load into a vertex buffer and reuses it. The WebGPU emitter's CPU build must be load-time-cached the same way; if it already is (createEdgePrimitiveResources uploads once), the string-keyed Map is still avoidable with integer keys (a*N+b).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Confirm extractEdgeGeometry is called once per primitive at load (not per frame); regardless, replace string keys with numeric edge keys (smaller*vertexCount+bigger in a Map<number,...> or a typed hash) to cut allocation. Pre-size verts/idx from edgeCount estimate to avoid array doubling.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The string-keyed Map/Set + growable arrays are real (WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:326 `Map<string,number[]>`, 367 `${a},${b}` key, 385/413 `Set<string>`, 383-384 growable `verts`/`idx`). BUT the finding's central worry ('if a caller invokes this per-frame') is NOT realized: WebGPUModelRenderer.js:3397 guards extraction with `if (!defined(primCache.edgeResources))` and line 3448 sets a `false` sentinel to avoid re-extracting null-edge primitives — so extractEdgeGeometry runs ONCE per primitive at load, GPU buffers are reused thereafter (createEdgePrimitiveResources). The finding itself hedges this. So there is NO per-frame CPU rebuild; the only residual is a one-time load allocation cost where integer edge keys (a*N+b) would be cheaper than template-literal strings. Real but minor (load-time micro-optimization, not a per-frame GC hot path). Downgraded to low.

allMergedFindings.title: Design-doc-promised TAA debug snapshot (taaStats / framesSinceJump / lastJitter) is never wired
allMergedFindings.observation: TAA_DESIGN.md acceptance criteria (line 219) require 'scene.getDebugSnapshot().renderer.taaStats reports historyPing/Pong validity, lastJitter, and framesSinceJump.' WebGPUTAAEffect.getStatistics() (687-700) returns only enabled/frameCounter/blendWeight/jitterX/jitterY/historyIndex — no framesSinceJump (teleport-recovery counter) and no ping/pong validity. There is also no plumb of a `taaStats` key into getDebugSnapshot (the teleport-invalidation logic in Scene.js:5266-5281 computes isTeleport but never records frames-since-teleport for diagnostics). This makes the TAA history-validity / teleport behavior unobservable from the documented debug surface, which Principle 8 (Playwright verification) and the debugging-guide tooling rely on.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — TAA is WebGPU-only. This is an unmet acceptance criterion of the feature's own design doc.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Extend getStatistics with framesSinceJump (track a counter reset when updateMotionVectorParams receives valid=false) and history-slot validity, and surface them under renderer.taaStats in getDebugSnapshot.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUTAAEffect.getStatistics() (687-700) returns only enabled/frameCounter/blendWeight/jitterX/jitterY/historyIndex — no framesSinceJump and no ping/pong validity. Grep for `taaStats`, `framesSinceJump`, `historyPing`/`historyPong`, `lastJitter` across packages/engine/Source returns ZERO hits, so getDebugSnapshot has no `renderer.taaStats` key and the teleport-recovery counter (computed implicitly via isTeleport in Scene.js:5266-5281) is never recorded for diagnostics. TAA_DESIGN.md:219 lists this as an explicit acceptance criterion. Genuine unmet-acceptance-criterion functionality gap. Low severity correct (debug-surface observability only, no rendering impact).

allMergedFindings.title: Disocclusion depth-test threshold uses eyePosCurr.z absolute floor of 1.0m — scale-fragile at altitude
allMergedFindings.observation: TAA.wgsl:290-292 sets `disocclusionThreshold = abs(eyePosCurr.z) * 0.001` then rejects when `depthDelta > max(disocclusionThreshold, 1.0)`. The 0.1% relative term scales with eye-space depth, which is reasonable, but the hard `max(..., 1.0)` meter floor means at near distances (eyePosCurr.z under ~1000 m, e.g. street-level / model inspection) the relative term is below 1 m and the constant floor dominates — a fixed 1 m tolerance is far too coarse for a model viewed at 10-50 m, letting genuinely disoccluded fragments pass the depth gate and ghost (the normal-divergence gate at 313-322 only fires when a real G-buffer normal is present, which excludes globe/billboards/sky). Conversely the same 1.0 floor is negligible at orbital scale. A single magic constant can't serve both regimes.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL TAA. This is a tuning-durability concern in the new shader; the threshold should be derived from a pixel-scale or near-plane-relative quantity, not a raw meter constant.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Replace the 1.0 m floor with a near-plane-relative or projected-pixel-size-relative floor (e.g. a fraction of the per-pixel eye-space footprint), so the disocclusion test holds across the full altitude range Cesium spans.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. TAA.wgsl:290-291: `disocclusionThreshold = abs(eyePosCurr.z) * 0.001; if (depthDelta > max(disocclusionThreshold, 1.0))`. The hard 1.0m floor dominates the 0.1%-relative term whenever |eyePosCurr.z| < ~1000m (street-level / model inspection), giving a coarse fixed 1m depth tolerance that lets near-field disoccluded fragments pass the gate. The normal-divergence backstop at 313-322 only fires when a real G-buffer normal is present (`length(nCenter) >= 0.1 && length(nPrev) >= 0.1`), which by the sentinel comment (303-306) excludes sky/billboards/labels/lines — so those classes have only the depth gate. The single meter constant genuinely can't serve both near-field and orbital regimes. Real tuning-durability concern. Low severity correct (manifests as occasional ghosting in a narrow near-field regime, not a hard failure).

allMergedFindings.title: Edge emitter single-target fallback silently drops id + packed-depth outputs (feature-ID edge gating cannot work without MRT FBO)
allMergedFindings.observation: ensureEdgeEmitterPipeline builds two pipelines: an MRT 3-target variant and pipelineSingleTarget (688-700) whose comment (681-687) states the FS's id + packed-depth writes 'get dropped silently' when the edge MRT FBO isn't allocated. The FS unconditionally writes @location(0/1/2) (FragmentOutput, 172-176), relying on WebGPU silently discarding writes to absent attachments. That's valid WebGPU, but it means whenever a scene draws edges without _enableEdgeVisibility (the common path), the feature-ID and packed-depth channels — which per-feature edge gating (C-R8-EDGE-FEATURE-ID) and depth-aware compositing depend on — produce nothing. Combined with the module docstring noting per-feature gating is 'still deferred' pending C-R8-EDGE-INLINE, the net is that edge feature-ID gating is plumbed end-to-end (vertex attr, FS pack, id FBO) but functionally inert. This is acceptable scaffolding per Principle 7, but it is not clearly surfaced as a tracked gap in the audited code path.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL EdgeVisibilityPipelineStage supports per-feature edge gating via the inline per-fragment featureId at draw time. WebGPU's post-process consumer can't see the model fragment's featureId, so the parity item is genuinely blocked on C-R8-EDGE-INLINE.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Leave the scaffolding (correct per Principle 7) but ensure C-R8-EDGE-FEATURE-ID / C-R8-EDGE-INLINE is an explicit tracked WIP entry in DEFERRED_WORK.md / FEATURE_INVENTORY §C so the inert id/depth plumbing isn't mistaken for working parity.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the facts: pipelineSingleTarget (688-700) targets only `[{format: colorFormat}]`; the FS unconditionally writes @location(0/1/2) (172-176) relying on WebGPU silently discarding writes to absent attachments — valid WebGPU. The comment (681-687) and module docstring (26-30) explicitly state per-feature edge gating is 'Still deferred (C-R8-EDGE-FEATURE-ID)' pending C-R8-EDGE-INLINE because a post-process consumer can't see the model fragment's featureId. This is exactly the deliberate scaffolding Principle 7 protects — the id/depth plumbing (vertex attr slot 6, FS pack, MRT pipeline) is pre-allocated for follow-up inline detection. The finding's own verdict is 'acceptable scaffolding.' The only residual ask is documentation tracking: I confirmed FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:639 lists 'WebGPU Edge Visibility / Edge Feature ID ... per-edge feature picking (SHIPPED)' which is arguably over-claiming since gating is inert — but the code behavior itself is correct intentional WebGPU design, not a bug. Reclassified from functionality-gap to intentional-webgpu-specific; the actionable item is an inventory-accuracy nit (the SHIPPED tag should be WIP/SCAFFOLDED for the gating sub-feature), not a code defect. Severity low.

allMergedFindings.title: TAA params bind group is recreated every frame instead of cached
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUTAAEffect.execute() calls this._device.createBindGroup({...}) every frame (584-596) with the seven entries (source, history read, depth, sampler, params buffer, motion, gBuffer). Source/historyRead/depth/motion/gBuffer views genuinely change frame-to-frame (ping-pong + per-frame textures), so a fully static cache isn't possible — but the sampler and params-buffer bindings are invariant, and the history read/write views only rotate between two fixed values. A per-frame createBindGroup is a known WebGPU hot-path cost the project's own bind-group cache (referenced in CLAUDE.md performance subsystem) is designed to avoid.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A (WebGL has no bind groups). Compare against the project's WebGPUBindGroupCache pattern used elsewhere — TAA bypasses it.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Cache two bind groups (one per ping-pong phase) keyed on (sourceView, depthView, motionView, gBufferView); only rebuild when a contributing view changes (resize / new velocity texture). For typical steady-state frames the source/depth views are stable, so this eliminates almost all per-frame bind-group creation.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. WebGPUTAAEffect.execute() calls `this._device.createBindGroup({...})` every frame (584-596) with 7 entries (source, historyRead, depth, sampler, paramsBuffer, motion, gBuffer). Source/historyRead/historyWrite/depth/motion/gBuffer views legitimately rotate (ping-pong + per-frame textures), so a fully-static cache isn't possible, but sampler+paramsBuffer are invariant and the history views rotate between two fixed slots — so a 2-entry phase cache keyed on (sourceView, depthView, motionView, gBufferView) would eliminate most per-frame allocation. CLAUDE.md's performance subsystem references a bind-group cache pattern (WebGPUBindGroupCache) that this path bypasses. Real but genuinely low: one createBindGroup/frame is a small, known WebGPU cost and TAA runs at most once per frame (not per draw). Low severity correct.

allMergedFindings.title: Globe pass builds and discards a render bundle every frame instead of caching via WebGPURenderBundleManager
allMergedFindings.observation: executeGlobeDispatch (WebGPUSceneRendererGlobePass.ts:89-141) creates a fresh GPURenderBundleEncoder, replays every globe draw command into it (`cmd.execute(bundleEncoder, ...)` loop at lines 124-132), finishes the bundle (line 135), executes it once (line 136), and then drops it on the floor — the local `bundle` is never stored. The next frame re-encodes the entire globe command list into a brand-new bundle. The whole value proposition of render bundles (`encode once, replay many` — see WebGPURenderBundleManager docstring lines 8-12: '50-80% CPU reduction... encoded once, then replayed each frame') is lost. The fully-built WebGPURenderBundleManager.getOrCreate() cache (with keys, versioning, eviction, snapshot-freeze) exists and is wired into the context, but the globe pass bypasses it entirely. So the most command-heavy pass in the engine pays the per-frame encode cost AND the bundle-build overhead with zero amortization benefit — strictly worse than just calling executeBatch directly.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no render-bundle concept; this is WebGPU-new infra. The intent (per the manager docstring and WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:470-479 bundle fast-path) was to cache bundles keyed by tile/pass so static terrain replays without re-recording. WebGL can't do this, so it's a WebGPU-only win that's currently not being realized.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Route the globe bundle through context.renderBundleManager.getOrCreate(key, descriptor, recordCallback) keyed on a per-frustum + command-structure signature (e.g. tile-set version + pass + format hash), with invalidation on tile add/remove (the SceneRendererEnsureResources already calls renderBundleManager.invalidateAll on resize). If per-frame command-list churn makes caching unsound for the globe, then the bundle path is net-negative and should be removed in favor of plain executeBatch — building-and-discarding a bundle every frame is strictly more CPU than not bundling at all.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified against WebGPUSceneRendererGlobePass.ts:108-138. executeGlobeDispatch creates a fresh GPURenderBundleEncoder, replays every command (cmd.execute loop 124-132), calls bundleEncoder.finish() (135), executes once (136), and the local `bundle` is never stored — re-encoded every frame. By direct contrast, the Environment/moon site (WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js:994-1006) DOES use bundleMgr.getOrCreate()/invalidate() with a per-moon cache key, proving the globe pass is the inconsistent one. The fully-built WebGPURenderBundleManager.getOrCreate() cache exists and is bypassed. Crucially, this is NOT documented as a known limitation: FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:660 lists globe terrain as a SHIPPED bundle site, and FUTURE_RESEARCH_2026_05_01.md:301/318 describe it as a working bundle site whose 'CPU recording cost' win was 'big' — the docs assume amortization that the code never achieves. So a build-and-discard pays encode cost AND bundle-build overhead with zero replay benefit, plausibly net-negative vs plain executeBatch. The reviewer's recommendation (route through getOrCreate keyed on tile-set/pass/format, or drop the bundle path) is actionable. One nuance: bundles are only attempted above renderBundleThreshold (default 8) so the cost only applies on command-heavy frustums, but those are exactly the heavy frames. Severity high is justified for the most command-heavy pass.

allMergedFindings.title: GPU sort-keys + bitonic-sort + readback runs every frame on dense scenes but the sorted result is never consumed
allMergedFindings.observation: When command count for a frustum exceeds GPU_SORT_KEYS_THRESHOLD_HI=6000 (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:949), gpuSortActive turns on automatically (no opt-in flag) and _dispatchGPUSortKeys runs each frame: it uploads 6 SOA storage buffers, dispatches keygen (dispatcher.dispatch), then chains runBitonicSort (O(log^2 N) compute passes — ~28 dispatches at N=65536, each a separate beginComputePass/writeBuffer per WebGPUGPUSortKeysDispatcher.ts:470-489), prepareIndicesReadback (copyBufferToBuffer), and an async readSortedIndices map. The readback result lands in `this._lastSortedIndices` (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:3914). But `_lastSortedIndices` is WRITTEN ONLY — grep across the file shows it is never read (occurrences only at the field decl 971, the docstring 965, and the write 3914). No consumer reorders the command list from it. The field docstring (lines 964-967) asserts 'consumers reorder their command list using this on the NEXT frame' — that consumer does not exist. So at exactly the scene scale where it is most expensive (>6000 cmds), the engine burns a full keygen + multi-pass bitonic sort + GPU->CPU readback every frame for zero functional effect.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL sorts opaque commands front-to-back and translucent back-to-front on the CPU in RenderScheduler. The dispatcher's own docstring (lines 31-37) concedes the JS comparator is faster than the GPU path for <50K commands because the encode->submit->readback round trip dominates — yet the activation gate fires at 6000, well inside that range. The WebGPU path therefore both (a) does redundant work the CPU sort already does and (b) discards it.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Either wire `_lastSortedIndices` into the frustum command dispatch (apply the 1-frame-stale permutation to the command order before executeCommands, matching the cull-readback model) and gate it behind a real feature flag with a benchmark proving net win above the threshold — or disable gpuSortActive by default and treat the dispatcher as explicitly-deferred scaffolding (it is tagged 'infrastructure — consumer integration is a separate step' at lines 33-37, so the auto-activation at 6000 contradicts its own deferred status). Per Principle 9, surface the missing consumer as the concrete next work item rather than leaving the discard in place.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: The code claim is fully verified: grep shows _lastSortedIndices in WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts only at the docstring (965), field decl (971), a comment (3897), and the write (3914) inside the readback .then() — never read. gpuSortActive auto-activates at count>=GPU_SORT_KEYS_THRESHOLD_HI=6000 via _updateActivationGate (1783-1788) with no opt-in flag, and _dispatchGPUSortKeys (3771+) chains keygen + runBitonicSort + prepareIndicesReadback + async readSortedIndices each frame. HOWEVER this is explicitly and thoroughly tracked in migration_doc/DEFERRED_WORK.md as 'NEW-GPU-SORT-PIPELINE-PHASE-3 — RenderScheduler consumer integration for sorted-indices readback' (lines 259-308), which states verbatim: 'The _lastSortedIndices field is populated each frame the sort fires, but never read.' It even names the two fix paths (CPU reorder / indirect-draw) and the latency contract. Also surfaced in audits/2026-04-30_ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE.md:153 ('GPU sort keys ... dispatchers exist; consumers absent'). The one sharper sub-point the reviewer adds — that the 6000 gate fires inside the <50K range where the doc itself concedes the JS comparator wins, so it's net-negative work in the 6K-50K band — is a legitimate critique of the activation threshold not just the missing consumer, but the core symptom is documented. Severity drops to medium since it's tracked and the work-burn only occurs at >6000 commands, an uncommon density.

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUBindGroupCache has no eviction or size cap despite docstring claiming lazy eviction — unbounded growth risk
allMergedFindings.observation: The module docstring (line 24) states 'When any input changes (typical after a texture resize), the cache produces a new bind group and evicts the stale one lazily.' There is no lazy eviction: getOrCreate (lines 134-175) only ever does `_map.set(key, bg)` on a miss; the sole removal path is invalidateAll() (lines 183-186) which clears everything. There is no maxSize, no LRU, no per-key eviction. For consumers whose input resource identities legitimately rotate across frames without a resize event — e.g. effects that composite from different source views per frustum/per ping-pong target, or split-screen where two scenes alternate inputs — every distinct (layout, resource-identity) tuple accretes a permanent entry. The _idMap is a WeakMap so collected resources free their IDs, but the bind groups themselves stay pinned in the strong `_map` keyed by the stale string. Unlike the render/compute pipeline caches (which have DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE=1024 + LRU touch/evict) and the storage pool (maxTotal=64) and resource manager (maxUniformPoolSize=100), this cache is the only unbounded one in the subsystem.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has no bind-group object; this is WebGPU-new. The analogous WebGPURenderPipelineCache in the same subsystem implements a proper LRU (lines 309-335), so the unbounded design here is an inconsistency within the fork's own perf infra, not a backend constraint.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add a maxSize (insertion-order LRU like WebGPURenderPipelineCache.touch/evictIfNeeded, ~256 is ample for effect graphs) and evict on insertion, OR fix the docstring to state there is no eviction and document the contract that callers MUST invalidateAll whenever the input graph changes. The first is safer for long-running kiosk sessions (the exact workload the docstring at lines 13-17 cites as the motivation).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified against WebGPUBindGroupCache.ts in full. The module docstring line 24 states 'the cache produces a new bind group and evicts the stale one lazily' — this is factually false. getOrCreate (134-175) only ever does _map.set(key, bg) on a miss; the only removal path is invalidateAll() (183-186) which clears the entire Map. There is no maxSize, no LRU, no per-key eviction — confirmed there is no _maxSize field and no eviction method. The _idMap is a WeakMap (103) so collected GPU resources free their numeric IDs, but the bind groups themselves stay pinned in the strong _map keyed by the now-stale string key.
