allMergedFindings.title: Device-loss recovery is robust and SceneRenderer resources are correctly invalidated (confirming, no defect)
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery.ts:154-385; WebGPUDeviceInvalidationBus.ts:55-67; WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:109-120
allMergedFindings.observation: Recovery correctly distinguishes intentional 'destroyed' (FATAL, no recovery) from transient loss, tracks in-flight recovery so destroy() can abort/await (no half-recovered-orphan-device), routes pool-managed devices through WebGPUDevicePool.recoverDevice to dedup concurrent multi-context recoveries with direct-requestDevice fallback, re-inits limits/canvas/textures/caches and re-arms the lost handler on the new device. The invalidation bus catches per-subscriber throws and logs with context id. Critically, the SceneRenderer DOES drop its GPU resources on loss: EnsureResources.ts:114-120 subscribes once to context.onDeviceInvalidated and nulls _sceneFramebuffer/_edgeFramebuffer/_translucentTileClassification/_oit/_globeDepth/etc so the next frame rebuilds against the new device. WebGL has no recovery path at all, so this is strictly additive.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL Context.js has no device-loss recovery; this entire subsystem is a NEW fork addition with no WebGL counterpart to drift from.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: No action. The exponential-backoff cap at maxAttempts=3 and pool dedup are sound. Optionally surface a user-facing event when state→FATAL so apps can show a reload prompt (minor enhancement).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the load-bearing half of the claim: WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:114-124 subscribes ONCE (guarded by !host._deviceInvalidationUnsub) to context.onDeviceInvalidated and nulls _sceneFramebuffer/_edgeFramebuffer/_translucentTileClassification/_oit/_globeDepth/_depthPlane/_postProcess/debug overlays so the next frame's _ensureResources rebuilds against the new device — exactly as claimed, and the correct behavior for surviving transient device loss. This is a POSITIVE no-defect note; the broader recovery-state-machine claims (intentional-destroyed vs transient, pool dedup, exponential backoff cap) are consistent with the cited files and this entire subsystem is a NEW fork addition with no WebGL counterpart to drift from. Severity none — no action required. The optional enhancement (user-facing FATAL event) is a reasonable nice-to-have, not a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: Hysteresis-gated GPU culling / HiZ / GPU-sort with per-frustum state is a WebGPU-only win worth back-porting consideration
allMergedFindings.evidence: WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1724-1792,3274-4094
allMergedFindings.observation: _executeOpaquePass (1675-1894) and the cull cluster (3274-4094) implement threshold-gated, per-frustum, hysteresis-stabilized activation of GPU frustum culling, HiZ occlusion, and GPU sort-keys for very large opaque batches (>~2400 commands), with gpuCullingHint = auto/always/never honored and pick passes excluded so render/pick filter sets never diverge. This is genuinely new capability not present in WebGL2.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL2 does CPU culling only (Scene.updateFrameState) and cannot do HiZ/GPU-sort without compute. A partial back-port (GPU sort-keys via transform-feedback, coarse occlusion via a CPU HiZ readback) is feasible but high-effort and arguably not worth it given the fork targets WebGPU for new perf features. The activation-gate/hysteresis LOGIC itself (the Map-keyed per-frustum state machine) is backend-agnostic and could be lifted to a shared helper if a WebGL GPU-sort path is ever added.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Leave WebGL as-is for now (compute-dependent), but extract the activation-gate state machine (_updateActivationGate + per-frustum Maps) into a backend-neutral helper so a future WebGL path could reuse the hysteresis logic. Low priority.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified the subsystem exists: _executeOpaquePass (1675) gates GPU cull/HiZ/GPU-sort via _updateActivationGate (1771-1792 calls, gate at 3559) with per-frustum culler selection (gpuCullCommands picks context.getGPUCullerForOpaqueFrustum(fIdx) at 3298-3299 — Batch 220 multi-frustum cull-results), and pick passes are excluded so render/pick filter sets don't diverge. This is genuinely WebGPU-only capability (HiZ occlusion + GPU sort-keys require compute, which WebGL2 lacks). It is NOT a defect — it is a correct WebGPU-specific feature, so the verdict is intentional-webgpu-specific with severity none. The backport recommendation is appropriately scoped as low-priority/speculative; the only backend-agnostic piece (the activation-gate hysteresis state machine) could be lifted to a shared helper if a WebGL GPU-sort path ever lands, but that's a future nicety, not actionable now.

allMergedFindings.title: Soft type leaks: Scene JSDoc annotates params as WebGPUContext
allMergedFindings.observation: GBufferFramebuffer.js:81 and OcclusionCulling.js:181 name the concrete WebGPUContext type in scene-layer JSDoc. No runtime import (not a hard violation) but documents a WebGPU-specific contract in backend-agnostic code and can mislead readers.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Type params as {GraphicsContext} since both backends satisfy them.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Re-read both cited sites. GBufferFramebuffer.js:81 does use `@param {WebGPUContext} context` as the JSDoc type — accurate. BUT OcclusionCulling.js:181 actually reads `@param {object} context The WebGPUContext (or GraphicsContext).` — the TYPE is `{object}`, and the prose even qualifies with '(or GraphicsContext)'. So the finding's claim that line 181 'names the concrete WebGPUContext type in scene-layer JSDoc' is factually wrong for that file. More fundamentally, the finding's premise that these are 'backend-agnostic code' is false. Both files explicitly declare themselves WebGPU-only in their module docstrings: GBufferFramebuffer.js:16-20 says 'this class is now WebGPU-specific (it builds a GPUTexture against context.device)... deferred lighting is a WebGPU-only path. The WebGL backend never instantiates this class'; OcclusionCulling.js:12-13 says '**WebGPU only** — requires compute shaders, storage buffers, and texture_storage_2d. No WebGL equivalent exists.' Caller verification confirms it: GBufferFramebuffer is only constructed/updated from WebGPUSceneFBTargetHelpers.ts and WebGPUContext.ts (WebGPU renderer code), and it directly dereferences context.device. The `@param {WebGPUContext}` annotation therefore correctly documents the actual runtime contract — it is not a 'leak' into agnostic code and is not misleading; it is precise. The recommendation to retype as {GraphicsContext} would make the JSDoc LESS accurate (the methods call WebGPU-only members). These files living under Scene/ is an organizational artifact, not an agnosticism violation (CLAUDE.md §2 prohibits Scene code importing from Renderer/WebGPU/ and branching on isWebGPU — neither file does that). No actionable defect.

allMergedFindings.title: Capability-getter migration is the correct durable pattern; codify it
allMergedFindings.observation: GraphicsContext.ts:736/749/762/927 define capability getters (requiresVertexTypedArrayRetention, supportsLegacySunBloom, supportsStereoViewport, requiresSceneRenderer) with WebGL-safe defaults overridden in WebGPUContext; consumers branch via ===true/!==false (FramebufferOrchestrator.js:51,115,134; GltfLoader.js:1383; Scene.js:2372). Cleanly replaced raw isWebGPU branching; behavior identical to pre-migration WebGL. Positive pattern.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Document the getter-per-capability convention in CLAUDE.md as the canonical replacement for isWebGPU branches; name getters by capability not backend; apply to ViewportQuad and isWebGPUDrawCommand.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/audits/2026-04-30_MAINTAINABILITY_SURVIVABILITY.md (residual isWebGPU branch count only, not the getter pattern itself)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: All cited code verified accurately. GraphicsContext.ts defines requiresVertexTypedArrayRetention (line 736, default false), supportsLegacySunBloom (line 749, default true), supportsStereoViewport (line 762, default true), requiresSceneRenderer (line 927, default false) — each with WebGL-safe defaults, AUDIT_2026_05_02 JSDoc markers, and documented WebGPU overrides. Consumer branching confirmed at FramebufferOrchestrator.js:51 (`context?.supportsLegacySunBloom !== false`), :115 and :134 (`context.requiresSceneRenderer === true`), with inline comments explicitly noting the 2026-05-02 switch from isWebGPU to the capability getter per CLAUDE.md §2. This is a genuine positive pattern, correctly identified. On the documentation status: the 2026-04-30 MAINTAINABILITY audit (line 162) already tracks '15 real branches across 11 files' of residual `if (context.isWebGPU)` in Source/Scene/ — the surface the recommendation's 'apply to ViewportQuad' targets (verified ViewportQuad.js:144 still has a raw `if (context.isWebGPU)`). However, the capability-getter convention itself is NOT yet codified in CLAUDE.md (§2 line 22 only states getters MAY be used to query type, not the getter-per-capability replacement pattern), and grep of DEFERRED_WORK.md / the audit trio for the getter names returns no hits — these getters postdate the 2026-04-30 audit. So the actionable substance (document the convention in CLAUDE.md; migrate remaining branches like ViewportQuad and isWebGPUDrawCommand) is a legitimate, undocumented backport/convention item. Severity correctly low — this is a quality/codification suggestion, not a defect; the existing code is already correct and behavior-preserving.

allMergedFindings.title: Globe surface renderer allocates 3-4 GPUBindGroups per tile per frame (no cache)
allMergedFindings.observation: Inside the per-tile draw loop, every tile unconditionally builds bindGroup0 via device.createBindGroup (camera+tile UB, WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:877), bindGroup1 via _createTextureBindGroup (17 entries — 16 imagery views + sampler, :1348), and bindGroup2 via _createWaterOceanBindGroup (:901). None are cached. For a typical ~200-tile globe frame at 60 Hz that is ~600-800 fresh GPUBindGroup driver objects per second, each carrying ~150-300 bytes of driver state reclaimed only on GC. The bound resources (imagery texture views, sampler, water/ocean placeholders) are stable across frames for a given tile+imagery revision; only the camera/tile UB ring-offset changes frame to frame. The UB ring allocator (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts) was explicitly built to avoid per-tile buffer creation, but the bind groups that reference those buffers reintroduce per-tile churn by binding {buffer, offset, size} explicitly instead of using a dynamic-offset BGL (hasDynamicOffset:true) which would let ONE cached bind group be reused via setBindGroup(i, bg, [offset]). bindGroup1/bindGroup2 reference only stable resources and could be cached per (tile, imageryRevision) with zero steady-state allocation.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's GlobeSurfaceTile path reuses a persistent uniform map object and binds imagery to texture units without allocating any per-frame GPU-side objects — texture units and the uniform map are mutated in place. There is no per-tile per-frame driver-object allocation equivalent in the WebGL globe path.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Cache bindGroup1 (texture set) and bindGroup2 (water/ocean) per-tile keyed on the imagery texture-view identities + revision, invalidating on imagery change. For bindGroup0, switch group(0) to a dynamic-offset BGL (hasDynamicOffset:true on both UB bindings) so a single bind group is created once and reused with the ring-allocator's per-frame offset passed to setBindGroup. CesiumDebug.cpuPassCost should show the globe pass CPU time drop; add a getStats() counter as WebGPUBindGroupCache already has.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified directly. In the per-tile render method (one tile per call, confirmed by signature at :550+ taking tile/surfaceTile/mesh), the per-pass loop at :715 unconditionally builds bindGroup0 via device.createBindGroup (:877-897), bindGroup1 via _createTextureBindGroup which itself ends in a 17-entry device.createBindGroup (:1348-1369), and bindGroup2 via _createWaterOceanBindGroup (:901). None route through WebGPUBindGroupCache.getOrCreate (grep confirms no cache import use at these sites; only texture/buffer helpers are cached). The bound texture VIEWS are cached (getOrCreateImageryTextureHelper) but the bind groups referencing them are rebuilt every call. The camera/tile UBs come from a ring allocator (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB returns {buffer,offset,size}, :20/:101), so the buffer itself is not re-created — only the bind group is churned because bindGroup0 binds explicit offsets. The ~600-800 driver-objects/sec estimate is order-of-magnitude reasonable for ~200 tiles. The 2026-04-30 audit (line 131) only claims the EFFECTS BG and post-process hot paths are deduplicated, NOT the globe texture/camera bind groups — so this is not the same item marked fixed at audit line 94. Genuine, actionable regression vs WebGL's in-place uniform-map/texture-unit model.

allMergedFindings.title: Billboard renderer rebuilds entire instance array + re-uploads all instances every frame (no dirty tracking)
allMergedFindings.observation: updateWebGPUBillboards unconditionally calls buildInstanceData(collection) every frame (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1251), which allocates a fresh new Float32Array(length * FLOATS_PER_INSTANCE) (:156) and loops over ALL billboards re-encoding RTE positions, then writeBuffer's the full range to the GPU (:1327-1333). There is no collection._dirty / _billboardsToUpdate short-circuit — a static 10k-placemark collection that never changes still pays a full 10k-element CPU rebuild + full GPU re-upload every frame, plus the GC pressure of a new typed array each frame. The TAA velocity path doubles this (a second prev-instance buffer rebuild + writeBuffer, :1318). The Label and Point collection renderers share this pattern.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: BillboardCollection.update() (BillboardCollection.js:738-801) tracks _billboardsToUpdate / _billboardsToUpdateIndex and only invokes the relevant attribute writers for billboards that are actually dirty, writing just the changed vertex-buffer sub-regions via the VertexArrayFacade. A static collection settles to zero per-frame write work after the first frame. The WebGPU port dropped this dirty-region optimization entirely.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Mirror WebGL's dirty tracking: keep the CPU instance Float32Array resident on the cache (rebuild only on collection revision/length change), and writeBuffer only the dirty instance sub-ranges (or the whole buffer only when revision changed). Gate buildInstanceData behind a collection revision/dirty check the same way the point-cloud path gates its rebuild on 'revision change'. This is the single biggest collections-path regression for large static datasets.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. buildInstanceData (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:153) allocates a fresh new Float32Array(length*FLOATS_PER_INSTANCE) at :156 and loops ALL billboards re-encoding RTE positions every call. It is invoked unconditionally at :1251 inside updateWebGPUBillboards with no _dirty/revision/_billboardsToUpdate short-circuit (grep for those symbols in the file returns ZERO hits). The full instance buffer is device.queue.writeBuffer'd unconditionally at :1327-1333; the TAA prev-instance buffer adds a second full write at :1318-1324. The WebGL comparison is accurate: BillboardCollection.js DOES carry _billboardsToUpdate/_billboardsToUpdateIndex (:153,:596,:608,:738) and writes only dirty sub-regions via _vaf.subCommit(bb._index,1) (:862). Corroborated by DEFERRED_WORK.md:1100-1101 which notes the POINT renderer gates its prev-buffer write on a needsRebuild flag 'so static point collections don't re-upload for nothing' — confirming the billboard path lacks the equivalent gate the point path has. The driver-object bindGroup itself IS cached (:1237), but the CPU rebuild + full GPU upload are not. Genuine port regression for large static collections.

allMergedFindings.title: createEffectsBindGroup runs full per-tile on the globe path instead of being frame-memoized like the primitive path
allMergedFindings.observation: When shadows/clipping/CSM/atmosphere-LUT are active, the globe renderer calls createEffectsBindGroup per tile (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1022, inside the per-tile loop). Even though all tiles share one cache entry (identical resource graph + content key), every call still: zero-fills and repacks the 480-byte _scratchEffectsData (WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js:1041-1282), runs ~20 _idFor WeakMap lookups, concatenates two long template-literal cache keys (resKey ~20 ids + contentKey, :1366-1404), and unconditionally issues device.queue.writeBuffer of identical 480 bytes to the same cached buffer (:1466). The author comment at :1461 dismisses the redundant writeBuffer, but at 200 tiles that is 200 identical 480-byte uploads + 200 key reconstructions per frame. The primitive path already solved this with a per-frame memo (_primitiveEffectsBGFrameNumber / _primitiveEffectsBGToggleHash, WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:848-895) that returns the cached BG without re-entering the factory — the globe path lacks the equivalent guard.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL computes shadow/clipping uniforms once per collection per frame and binds them via the shared uniform map for all tiles; it does not repack a per-tile uniform staging buffer or re-issue an identical UBO upload per tile.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Apply the primitive path's frame-number+toggle-hash memo to the globe call site: compute the effects BG once per frame (the inputs — shadowMap, clippingPlanes, csm, LUT views, world camera — are frame-constant for the globe) and reuse the handle for all tiles. At minimum, skip the writeBuffer on cache hit when the content key is unchanged since the last write this frame.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/audits/2026-04-30_ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE.md (line 94 documents the Batch-55 BG-object fix; the residual repack/writeBuffer this finding targets is NOT covered)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. The globe renderer calls createEffectsBindGroup directly per tile at WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1022 when shadows/clip/CSM/atmosphere-LUT is active. Inside createEffectsBindGroup the 480-byte _scratchEffectsData (EFFECTS_UNIFORM_SIZE=480, :198) is .fill(0)'d and repacked every call (:1041-1042), the resKey is rebuilt from ~20 _idFor WeakMap lookups concatenated into a template literal (:1366-1377) plus a contentKey (:1398-1402), and on cache HIT device.queue.writeBuffer of the identical 480 bytes is issued unconditionally (:1466, comment at :1461 explicitly dismisses it). The primitive path DOES have the frame-memo the finding describes: _primitiveEffectsBGFrameNumber + _primitiveEffectsBGToggleHash early-return at WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:848-854, returning the cached BG without re-entering the factory. The globe call site has no equivalent guard. IMPORTANT: the 2026-04-30 audit line 94 marks the per-tile createBuffer+createBindGroup as FIXED (Batch 55 tuple cache) — but that fix only eliminated DRIVER-OBJECT allocation, not the residual per-tile repack + key reconstruction + redundant writeBuffer this finding targets. So the residual is real and undocumented; the BG-object allocation it would also reduce is already cached. Severity medium is fair (CPU repack + redundant upload, not driver-object churn).

allMergedFindings.title: GPU culler reallocates bounding-sphere Float32Array every frustum every frame
allMergedFindings.observation: The GPU frustum-cull path allocates const sphereData = new Float32Array(count * 4) per call (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:3305, and again in the translucent variant at :3484) plus a small new Float32Array(24) plane buffer (:3325, :3500). For dense scenes (thousands of cullable commands) this is a multi-KB typed-array allocation per frustum per frame fed straight into culler.uploadBoundingSpheres — pure GC churn since the data is immediately copied to a GPU staging buffer. The plane array is a fixed 24 floats and is trivially poolable.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL does CPU-side frustum culling per command without staging a packed sphere array to the GPU at all (CullingVolume.computeVisibility on each BoundingSphere), so there is no equivalent per-frame typed-array allocation. The GPU-cull approach itself is a fork addition; the allocation is the avoidable part.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Hold a reusable scratch Float32Array on the SceneRenderer (or on the per-frustum culler), grown via a capacity check (if (cap < count*4) realloc) and subarray'd to count*4 for upload — the same grow-on-demand pattern already used elsewhere in the file (e.g., :3682 centerX/Y/Z caps). Make planeData a fixed module-scope scratch since it is always 24 floats.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified at both sites. Opaque path: const sphereData = new Float32Array(count*4) at WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:3305 and const planeData = new Float32Array(24) at :3325, both fresh per call, fed straight to culler.uploadBoundingSpheres/uploadFrustumPlanes (:3335-3336). Translucent variant: identical new Float32Array(count*4) at :3484 and new Float32Array(24) at :3500. For dense scenes this is multi-KB GC churn per frustum per frame. The grow-on-demand scratch pattern is genuinely used elsewhere in the same file (the finding cites the centerX/Y/Z caps), so the recommendation is consistent with local conventions. planeData is trivially a fixed 24-float module scratch. WebGL does CPU-side per-command culling without staging a packed sphere array, so there is no equivalent allocation — accurate. Real, low-risk fix.

allMergedFindings.title: Effects BGL collection cache rebuilds long string keys + 20 WeakMap lookups per call on the hot path
allMergedFindings.observation: createEffectsBindGroup builds its cache key by concatenating ~20 _idFor() WeakMap lookups into a multi-segment template literal for resKey (:1366-1377) plus a second contentKey template literal (:1398-1402), producing a fresh string per call. WebGPUBindGroupCache.getOrCreate has the same shape — it builds a keyParts string array and joins it (WebGPUBindGroupCache.ts:140-160) on every lookup. String-key maps are correct but allocate a string (and for getOrCreate, an array) on every hit, defeating part of the point of caching the GPU object. On the globe path this fires 200×/frame.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: N/A — WebGL has no bind-group concept; this is WebGPU-specific cache machinery. The concern is that the cache's own key construction is itself a per-frame allocation.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: For the hot effects/globe path, prefer a nested-Map or numeric-composite key over string concatenation, or (better) hoist the lookup out of the per-tile loop entirely via frame memoization (see the createEffectsBindGroup finding). For WebGPUBindGroupCache, consider a 2-level Map keyed on layout-id then a numeric fold of entry ids to avoid the per-call string array+join.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. createEffectsBindGroup builds resKey from ~20 _idFor() WeakMap lookups into a multi-segment template literal (WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js:1366-1377) plus a second contentKey template literal (:1398-1402), allocating fresh strings per call including on cache hits. WebGPUBindGroupCache.getOrCreate has the same shape: it builds a keyParts string[] array and .join('|')s it on every call before the map lookup (:140-160), so a hit still allocates an array + a string. The claim that this 'defeats part of the point of caching the GPU object' is fair — the string-key construction is a per-frame allocation on the hot path. On the globe path the effects key reconstruction fires per tile (200x/frame). This overlaps heavily with finding #3 (the right fix — frame-memoizing the globe call — eliminates both), so it is somewhat a duplicate framing, but the underlying observation about both string-keyed caches is factually correct. Severity medium for the allocation cost; not a correctness issue.

allMergedFindings.title: sortGaussianSplatsBackToFront allocates a full command slice array every frame
allMergedFindings.observation: sortGaussianSplatsBackToFront does const slice = commands.slice(0, count) (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:380) every frame before mergeSort, allocating a new array of length count each frame for splat ordering. For large splat scenes (tens of thousands of splat commands) this is a sizeable per-frame array allocation feeding a back-to-front sort that already runs every frame.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Cesium's WebGL splat/translucent sort operates on the existing command list in place where possible; the extra defensive slice() copy is a port artifact.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Reuse a persistent scratch array grown on demand (length = count) instead of slice() each frame, or sort the command array region in place if the merge sort can target a stable scratch buffer held on the renderer.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/audits/2026-04-30_ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE.md line 98 (documents the same mergeSort(slice) per-frame allocation class; cites the per-frustum sort sites, not the splat site specifically)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. sortGaussianSplatsBackToFront does const slice = commands.slice(0, count) at WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:380 every call, mergeSorts it, then copies back into commands[i] (:382-384). For large splat scenes this is a per-frame array allocation. The 2026-04-30 audit line 98 ALREADY documents the structurally-identical pattern: 'mergeSort(commands.slice(0, count)) per pass per frustum allocates one transient array per sort — small, but per-frame. Could be hoisted into a reusable buffer.' The audit cites the per-pass/per-frustum sort sites (:279,:299) rather than this splat-specific :380 site, but it is the same allocation pattern and same recommended fix (reusable scratch). Confirmed real and low severity, and the general class is already noted in the audit even though this exact call site is not enumerated.

allMergedFindings.title: Globe bindGroup0 binds explicit UB offsets instead of dynamic-offset BGL — blocks bind-group reuse
allMergedFindings.observation: The camera/tile UBs are suballocated from a per-frame ring allocator (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts) — good. But bindGroup0 binds them with explicit per-call {buffer, offset, size} (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:880-895), so a NEW bind group must be created whenever the ring offset changes (every tile). Had group(0)'s BGL been declared with hasDynamicOffset:true on both UBO bindings, a SINGLE bind group could be created once per ring buffer and reused for all tiles by passing the per-tile offsets as the dynamicOffsets arg to setBindGroup. WebGPUDrawCommand.execute() currently calls setBindGroup(i, bg) with no dynamic-offset arg (WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:518), so this would need a small DrawCommand extension to carry dynamicOffsets.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: This is the WebGPU-idiomatic equivalent of WebGL's glBindBufferRange / persistent uniform map — WebGL never recreates binding objects when only the buffer offset changes. The dynamic-offset path is how WebGPU achieves the same zero-allocation rebind.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Add a hasDynamicOffset:true variant of the group(0) BGL for the globe tile path, create one bind group per ring buffer, and thread a dynamicOffsets array through WebGPUDrawCommand (a new optional field consumed in execute()'s setBindGroup loop). This is also reusable for any other ring-allocated UB path (collections, primitives).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. The camera/tile UBs are ring-allocated (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB returns {buffer,offset,size}, :20/:101), but bindGroup0 binds them with explicit per-call {buffer, offset, size} entries (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:880-895), so a new bind group must be created whenever the ring offset changes (every tile) — this is the mechanistic root of finding #1's per-tile bindGroup0 churn. A hasDynamicOffset:true BGL would let one bind group be reused with the offset passed via setBindGroup's dynamicOffsets arg. Confirmed that WebGPUDrawCommand.execute() calls passEncoder.setBindGroup(i, resolved ?? this.bindGroups[i]) at :518 with NO dynamicOffsets argument, so the proposed reuse genuinely needs a DrawCommand extension to thread dynamicOffsets — the finding's implementation note is accurate. NOTE: DEFERRED_WORK.md:949-950 discusses dynamic UBO offsets but in a DIFFERENT context (the GroundPrimitive classifier's per-slice frustum-state UBO), not the globe surface bindGroup0 reuse path — so this specific improvement is not the documented one. Real missed-improvement; severity medium (it is the enabler for the high-severity finding #1).

allMergedFindings.title: WebGPUBindGroupCache dedup architecture is sound but adoption is partial across per-frame paths
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUBindGroupCache (with getStats hit/miss telemetry) is a clean, durable abstraction for identity-based bind-group dedup, and the effects-BG + post-process effects paths use the equivalent. But the highest-volume per-frame bind-group producers — the globe texture/camera bind groups and the collection renderers' per-frame createBindGroup calls (WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1238, and grep shows 255 createBindGroup/createView call sites across 60 files) — do not route through any cache. The infrastructure to fix the top findings already exists; it is an adoption gap, not a missing-tool gap.

allMergedFindings.recommendation: Adopt WebGPUBindGroupCache (or per-owner equivalents) in the globe texture-bind-group path and the collection renderers, and surface their getStats() hitRate via CesiumDebug (PerformanceManager already aggregates the effects-BG stats). A 0% hit rate flag would have caught these regressions automatically.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/audits/2026-04-30_ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE.md (lines 111, 131 corroborate partial cache adoption as a general theme)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified as an accurate architecture-level observation. But the highest-volume producers do not route through it: the globe bindGroup0/1/2 use device.createBindGroup directly (:877,:1348,:1647 — confirmed no getOrCreate at those sites), and the billboard renderer's bindGroup is cached only via a hand-rolled cache.bindGroup field (:1237) rather than the central cache. The 2026-04-30 audit corroborates partial adoption: line 131 lists only post-process effects + globe-terrain-EFFECTS + auto-exposure as deduplicated, and line 111 notes only 6 of ~44 files prewarm the pipeline cache. allMergedFindings.title: Per-frame writeBuffer churn in collection renderers uploads full buffers where dirty-region would suffice
allMergedFindings.observation: Beyond the billboard full-rebuild finding, the collection renderers issue full-buffer device.queue.writeBuffer uploads every frame (billboard instance buffer at WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1327, prev-instance velocity buffer at :1318, uniform buffer at :1150). With WebGPU's unordered-write queue semantics, uploading the entire instance buffer every frame (rather than dirty sub-ranges) is both bandwidth waste and serializes against the same buffer's prior-frame read if the buffer isn't double-buffered. The 2026-04-30 audit line 182 flagged writeBuffer cadence generically for Polyline/Model/BufferPrimitive but did not include Billboard or frame the fix as dirty-region uploads.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL's VertexArrayFacade.subCommit writes only the dirty vertex-buffer byte ranges computed from _billboardsToUpdate, so a partially-changed collection uploads only the changed billboards' bytes rather than the whole buffer.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Track the dirty instance index range (min/max changed) per frame and writeBuffer only that byte sub-range; full upload only when the collection length/revision changes. Combine with the dirty-tracking fix from the billboard-rebuild finding. Measurable via CesiumDebug.gpuPassCost on the collections pass and a writeBuffer-bytes counter.
allMergedFindings.documentedIn: migration_doc/audits/2026-04-30_ARCHITECTURE_PERFORMANCE.md lines 96, 182 (documents writeBuffer cadence for Polyline/Model/BufferPrimitive only; Billboard and the dirty-region framing are NOT covered)
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified. The billboard renderer issues full-buffer device.queue.writeBuffer uploads every frame: full instance buffer at WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:1327-1333, full prev-instance velocity buffer at :1318-1324, and the uniform buffer at :1150-1156. None upload dirty sub-ranges. WebGL's VertexArrayFacade.subCommit writes only the changed vertex-buffer byte ranges (BillboardCollection.js:862), so a partially-changed collection uploads only changed billboards' bytes — accurate comparison. The finding correctly notes the 2026-04-30 audit (line 96 and line 182) flagged writeBuffer cadence generically for Polyline/Model/BufferPrimitive but did NOT include Billboard and did not frame the fix as dirty-region uploads — I verified line 182 lists exactly 'Polyline, Model, BufferPrimitive' and omits Billboard. So this is a real gap-extension of a partially-documented item, specific to the collection (Billboard) path. This overlaps with finding #2 (the dirty-tracking fix subsumes the dirty-region upload), so it is partly a different facet of the same regression rather than fully independent. Severity medium is appropriate.

allMergedFindings.title: Volumetric fog (froxel-grid) is high-value but the hardest backport — needs a 3D-texture froxel grid WebGL2 lacks cheap write paths for
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUVolumetricFogRenderer.ts:1-51 runs three compute passes (density injection, light scattering, front-to-back ray-march integration) into a 160x90x128 rgba16float 3D texture, then a fullscreen composite samples the integrated volume by (screen UV, linearized depth). This is genuinely WebGPU-only and one of the most visually impactful fork additions. WebGL2 has no compute and no storage-image writes, but it DOES support 3D textures (texImage3D) as render targets via layered FBO attachments. The froxel passes would have to be re-expressed as: render-to-3D-texture-slice loop (one draw per Z-slice, or layered rendering with gl_Layer in a geometry-shader-less workaround using instanced draws), which is a known but awkward WebGL2 technique. The composite pass ports trivially (it is already just a fullscreen GLSL fragment shader sampling a sampler3D).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: No WebGL volumetric fog exists; WebGL Fog.js is a simple per-fragment exponential fog. The capability gap is real and large.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Treat as a MEDIUM-value / HIGH-effort backport. Feasible via render-to-3D-texture slice loop (or a 2D-atlas-of-slices flattening to dodge layered-FBO quirks) + the existing fullscreen composite ported to GLSL. Effort ~1-2 weeks. Lower priority than the post-process effects below because the slice-loop rewrite is substantial and the froxel passes are the only part that doesn't port mechanically.

FEATURE_INVENTORY line 527/552 confirms SHIPPED, default-off. This is a correct, deliberate WebGPU-only feature (compute + storage-image writes), not a port regression or bug — isPortRegression is correctly false. The backport-feasibility analysis is technically accurate (WebGL2 has no compute, would need render-to-3D-slice loop) but it is advisory scoping, not an actionable defect. Severity medium is for the work item, not a bug; downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: God rays, SSR, and TAA are the cleanest high-value post-process backports — all are screen-space fragment passes WebGL2 runs natively
allMergedFindings.observation: All three are post-process stages with zero compute dependency. God rays (WebGPUGodRayEffect.ts:29-54) is a radial-blur-toward-sun-UV fragment shader + composite — a textbook WebGL2 PostProcessStage. SSR (WebGPUSSREffect.ts:1-50) ray-marches against the depth buffer in a fragment shader; its only extra input is an optional normal G-buffer, which WebGL2 can produce identically (the fork already reconstructs normals from depth — GBufferNormalsFromDepth.wgsl — and the WebGL AO stage AmbientOcclusionGenerate.glsl:26 already does depth-derivative normal reconstruction). TAA (WebGPUTAAEffect.ts:36-49) is sub-pixel jitter + history ping-pong + neighborhood-clamp reprojection using a CPU-precomputed inverseVP UBO — every input is available in WebGL2 (camera jitter is a projection-matrix tweak, history is a ping-pong FBO, the reprojection math is identical). The Cesium PostProcessStage framework already supports multi-pass stages with ping-pong (PostProcessStageTextureCache).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has none of god rays / SSR / TAA. SunPostProcess exists but is a different (geometry-based) sun flare, not screen-space god rays.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: HIGHEST-value backport cluster. Port each as a GLSL PostProcessStage: translate the WGSL fragment bodies to GLSL (the math is backend-neutral), wire jitter into Camera for TAA, and reuse the existing PostProcessStageCollection plumbing. Effort ~2-4 days each. The GraphicsContext/PostProcessStage abstraction makes this clean — no renderer-specific coupling. Start with god rays (simplest), then SSR, then TAA (needs the camera-jitter + motion-vector hook).

FEATURE_INVENTORY 565-567/644-646 confirms all three SHIPPED as WebGPU post-process effects. SSR is explicitly 'gated on FEAT-GAP-01 normal G-buffer for full fidelity', and GBufferNormalsFromDepth.wgsl confirms the normal-reconstruction technique the finding cites. These are correct WebGPU-only additions; the backport recommendation is sound advisory scoping, not a bug. isPortRegression correctly false. High severity reflects backport value, not a defect — downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: GPU radix/bitonic sort is the single most defensible compute backport — but WebGL2 has no clean path, so the value is capped
allMergedFindings.observation: Both backends currently sort Gaussian splats on the CPU via a WASM TaskProcessor (GaussianSplatSorter.js:11-25 is worker-based, backend-agnostic). The WebGPU bitonic sort (PointCloudSort.wgsl, BitonicSortU64.wgsl) is EXPERIMENTAL (useGPUSort flag default false per inventory §B.4) and GPUSortKeys is SCAFFOLDED — even on WebGPU the JS comparator wins below ~50K commands (WebGPUGPUSortKeysDispatcher.ts:29-37 says so explicitly). A WebGL2 backport would require expressing a bitonic network as ping-pong fragment passes over a data texture (a classic but slow GPGPU technique — O(log^2 n) fullscreen passes with heavy texture-fetch overhead and no storage buffers). For 64-bit keys (BitonicSortU64) the packing into RGBA8/float textures is painful.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL sorts on CPU/worker (same GaussianSplatSorter). There is no WebGL GPU sort.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: LOW-priority backport. The WebGPU version isn't even the live path yet, and the WebGL2 fragment-shader bitonic sort is typically slower than the existing WASM worker sort for Cesium's scales. Recommend NOT backporting; instead, if sorting is a bottleneck on WebGL, invest in the shared WASM sorter both backends already use. Flag this in the inventory so a future session doesn't speculatively port it.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified GaussianSplatSorter.js is WASM/worker-based and backend-agnostic (TaskProcessor + wasm_splats_bg.wasm, lines 11-25). FEATURE_INVENTORY confirms PointCloudSort.wgsl EXPERIMENTAL (useGPUSort default false, line 548) and GPUSortKeys SCAFFOLDED (line 550/665). The finding's recommendation NOT to backport is well-supported. Correct WebGPU-future scoping, not a defect. Downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: Forward+ clustered lighting is high-value and mostly backportable, but the cluster-assign compute pass needs a WebGL2 fragment-pass rewrite
allMergedFindings.observation: Clustered lighting (16x9x24 grid) gives WebGPU multi-light point/spot/directional shading beyond the single sun, consumed by Model PBR + all 19 Lit material shaders. The per-cluster light-list build (ClusterAssign.wgsl) is a compute pass writing variable-length per-cluster index lists into storage buffers — the part WebGL2 can't do directly. BUT: WebGL2 Forward+ is a well-trodden path. The cluster AABB build and light-assign can run as a fragment pass writing into a 2D-flattened cluster-index texture (each texel = a cluster, RGBA channels pack light indices, capped per cluster). The consumer side (the FS that reads the cluster and loops its lights) ports near-directly to GLSL because evalClusteredLights is already a backend-neutral algorithm. The dispatcher's 'always-bind-something' pattern (WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.ts:30-49) maps onto WebGL uniform/UBO defaults cleanly.

allMergedFindings.recommendation: MEDIUM-value backport. Feasible via classic WebGL2 Forward+ (clustered light culling into a UBO/texture via a fragment or CPU pass, then per-fragment cluster lookup). The consumer shaders are the easy 80%. Effort ~1 week. Worth doing if multi-light scenes matter on WebGL; the abstraction is clean because the FS chunk is already backend-neutral math.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.ts docstring (lines 1-49): 16x9x24 cluster grid, ClusterBounds + ClusterAssign compute passes producing storage buffers consumed at @group(4), and the 'always-bind-something' placeholder-buffer pattern at lines 30-49 exactly as described (skips compute when disabled, sets activeLightCount.x=0). This is a correct WebGPU compute feature; the backport analysis (consumer FS is backend-neutral, cluster-assign needs a WebGL2 Forward+ fragment rewrite) is accurate advisory scoping. Not a bug; isPortRegression correctly false. Downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: Procedural volumetric clouds are high-value and 100% backportable — it's a pure fullscreen ray-march fragment shader
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer (Schneider-style HG dual-lobe + Beer-Powder + 3D FBM density + light-ray march, per inventory §B.3 line 528) is a fullscreen ray-march. Ray-marching FBM noise is a fragment-shader workload with no storage-buffer or compute dependency — it is exactly the kind of thing WebGL2 fragment shaders do well (the existing CloudCollection/CloudNoiseFS already does 3D-noise SDF billboard clouds in GLSL). The only WebGPU-specific input is a precomputed 3D noise texture, which WebGL2 supports (sampler3D / texImage3D).
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has CloudCollection (billboard SDF clouds) but no volumetric raymarched sky clouds. Gap is real but the existing GLSL 3D-noise infrastructure de-risks the port.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: MEDIUM-value, LOW-effort backport. Translate the WGSL raymarch FS to GLSL, supply the 3D noise via sampler3D, wire as an environmental-effect fragment pass. Effort ~3-5 days. Default-off like WebGPU so no perf regression for non-users.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts exists; FEATURE_INVENTORY line 528 confirms Schneider-style HG dual-lobe + Beer-Powder + 3D FBM + light-ray march, SHIPPED default-off. Correct WebGPU-only feature with sound backport-feasibility scoping; not a defect. Downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: IBL prefilter + atmosphere LUT compute passes are backportable via the existing ComputeEngine fragment-to-texture path
allMergedFindings.observation: Renderer/ComputeEngine.js is the existing WebGL2 'compute via fragment shader to a texture' engine (it renders a viewport quad into an output texture for ComputeCommands). The WebGPU IBL prefilter (RadiancePrefilter/IrradianceConvolution), BRDF LUT (BrdfLutGenerate), and atmosphere transmittance/scattering LUT (AtmosphereLUT) are all one-time or low-frequency passes that write a texture from a texture — the canonical ComputeEngine use case. WebGL Cesium already generates a BRDF LUT and IBL via ConvolveSpecularMap/ComputeIrradiance/ComputeRadianceMap (FEATURE_INVENTORY A.14), so the BRDF/IBL parts are largely PRESENT on WebGL. The atmosphere precomputed-LUT (transmittance + multi-scatter) is the genuinely WebGPU-only piece worth porting.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has runtime IBL (ConvolveSpecularMap/ComputeIrradiance/ComputeRadianceMap) and BrdfLutGenerator already; it does NOT have the precomputed atmosphere transmittance/scattering LUT (it ray-marches per-fragment in GroundAtmosphere/SkyAtmosphere).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: MEDIUM-value, LOW-effort for the atmosphere LUT specifically. Port AtmosphereLUT.wgsl to a GLSL ComputeCommand fragment pass writing a transmittance + scattering texture, then sample it in the existing GroundAtmosphere/SkyAtmosphere GLSL FS instead of ray-marching. This is a clean perf win for WebGL atmosphere. The BRDF/IBL convolution is already covered on WebGL — do not duplicate.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified ComputeEngine.js IS the WebGL2 'compute via fullscreen fragment pass to a texture' engine (ViewportQuadVS rendered into a Framebuffer for ComputeCommands, lines 8-50). The finding's nuanced correction is accurate: it acknowledges WebGL already has runtime IBL (ConvolveSpecularMap/ComputeIrradiance/ComputeRadianceMap) and BRDF LUT, and isolates the genuinely WebGPU-only piece (precomputed atmosphere transmittance/scattering LUT) as the real backport target. This is correct advisory scoping that avoids duplicating existing WebGL functionality. Not a defect. Downgraded to none.

allMergedFindings.title: GPU compute LOD / frustum-cull / Hi-Z occlusion should NOT be backported — they are SCAFFOLDED, the live path is WASM/JS, and WebGL2 has no clean indirect-draw target
allMergedFindings.observation: Per inventory §B.4/§B.8, FrustumCull.wgsl / HiZPyramid.wgsl / OcclusionTest.wgsl / WebGPUGPUCuller / WebGPUHiZOcclusionDispatcher are all SCAFFOLDED with WASM/JS culling as the active path on BOTH backends. The whole point of GPU culling is to feed an indirect-draw buffer with the compute-produced visible count/offset — WebGL2 has no indirect draw and no compute, so the GPU-cull payoff (avoiding the CPU readback) is structurally unavailable. The Hi-Z pyramid build (mip-reduction of depth) IS expressible as fragment mip passes, but without indirect draw the occlusion result still has to round-trip to the CPU, which defeats the purpose.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL and WebGPU both cull on CPU (WASM/JS) today. No regression and no backport gap — the shared culling path is already backend-agnostic.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: DO NOT backport. The WebGPU versions aren't the live path even on WebGPU, and the indirect-draw dependency makes a WebGL2 GPU-cull a net loss. Note in the inventory that this trio is intentionally WebGPU-future, not a parity gap, so a future audit doesn't mis-scope it.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: FEATURE_INVENTORY confirms the exact status: FrustumCull.wgsl SCAFFOLDED 'WASM/JS culling active' (line 545), HiZPyramid SCAFFOLDED (546), OcclusionTest SCAFFOLDED (547), WebGPUGPUCuller/WebGPUHiZOcclusionDispatcher SCAFFOLDED 'JS/WASM cull active' (663-664). The finding's DO-NOT-backport recommendation (indirect-draw dependency unavailable in WebGL2, so GPU-cull is a net loss) is well-supported. Correct WebGPU-future scoping; not a parity gap or defect. Downgraded to none.

allMergedFindings.title: Timestamp GPU pass-profiling has a real but degraded WebGL2 path via EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2
allMergedFindings.observation: WebGPUTimestampProfiler (timestampWrites on each pass, async readback N frames later) gives per-pass GPU timing exposed via CesiumDebug.gpuPassCost(). WebGL2 has EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 (beginQuery/endQuery TIME_ELAPSED) which can bracket a pass and read elapsed-ns asynchronously — functionally equivalent for per-pass timing, though support is spottier (often disabled in Chrome for fingerprinting) and it can't do the fine-grained timestampWrites boundaries. The CPU-side profiler (WebGPUCpuPassProfiler, R-7a) is fully backend-agnostic and could be shared as-is.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL currently has FrameRateMonitor/PerformanceDisplay (frame-level) but no per-pass GPU timing. EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 would close the per-pass gap where the extension is available.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: LOW-value, LOW-effort. Add a WebGL EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 profiler behind the same CesiumDebug.gpuPassCost() surface, with graceful no-op when the extension is unavailable. Bigger win: lift WebGPUCpuPassProfiler to a backend-neutral location so both backends share CPU pass timing immediately (no extension needed).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts and WebGPUCpuPassProfiler.ts both exist. The EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 claim is a standard WebGL2 extension fact and the finding correctly notes its spotty availability. The recommendation (add an EXT profiler behind CesiumDebug.gpuPassCost, and lift the backend-agnostic CPU profiler to a shared location) is reasonable advisory tooling work, not a bug. Low severity is appropriate for the work item; downgraded to none as a defect.

allMergedFindings.title: Render bundles, decoupled-lookback scan, and subgroup utils are intrinsically non-backportable — no WebGL2 primitive exists
allMergedFindings.observation: Three capabilities have NO WebGL2 equivalent: (1) Render bundles (WebGPURenderBundleManager — record-once/replay-many command lists for 50-80% CPU reduction on static terrain) rely on the WebGPU command-recording model; WebGL2 has no command-buffer replay API. The nearest WebGL analog is VAO + minimizing state changes, which Cesium already does. (2) Decoupled-lookback scan (DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl, Merrill-Garland) needs storage buffers + atomics + cross-workgroup lookback — none in WebGL2. (3) Subgroup ops (WebGPUSubgroupUtils.ts:1-31) have no WebGL primitive at all.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has none of these and cannot. They are legitimately WebGPU-exclusive by hardware/API capability, not by missing effort.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: DO NOT attempt to backport. Document in FEATURE_INVENTORY §D that these are permanently WebGPU-only by API constraint, so future audits don't flag them as parity gaps. The CPU-reduction goal of render bundles is partly achievable on WebGL via the existing VAO/state-sort path — keep investing there instead.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: All three files exist. WebGPUSubgroupUtils.ts docstring (lines 1-31) confirms it requires the 'subgroups' feature (Chrome 132+ origin trial) — no WebGL primitive. FEATURE_INVENTORY line 445/660 confirms WebGPURenderBundleManager SHIPPED (record/replay, 3 active sites). DecoupledLookbackScan needs storage buffers + atomics + cross-workgroup lookback (none in WebGL2). The finding's conclusion that these are permanently WebGPU-only by API/hardware constraint is correct, and the recommendation to document this so future audits don't mis-flag them as parity gaps is sound. Not a defect. Downgraded to none.

allMergedFindings.title: OIT-MRT, AutoExposure, and AO are already present on WebGL — they are NOT backport candidates and the inventory should not imply they are
allMergedFindings.observation: Three items that look like WebGPU-only additions in §B already exist on WebGL: (1) OIT — Scene/OIT.js:24-35 implements the SAME McGuire-Bavoil weighted-blended MRT OIT (with drawBuffers MRT + multipass fallback) that WebGPUOIT.ts:8-17 implements; this is parity, not a WebGPU-only feature. allMergedFindings.webglComparison: WebGL has OIT, AutoExposure, and HBAO already. Only the GTAO refinement and the (unwired) dual-source OIT are WebGPU-differentiated.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: Correct the framing: these are not backport candidates. The only genuine post-process backport deltas vs WebGL are god rays / SSR / TAA / volumetric fog / procedural clouds (above) and the GTAO refinement (low-value). Update §B tags so a future audit doesn't double-count parity features as fork-exclusive.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: This finding makes verifiable claims about existing code, and all check out.
