allMergedFindings.title: Viewer.js carries genuine WebGPU async-init hook but is ALSO wholesale converted to class, bloating an otherwise-targeted change
allMergedFindings.evidence: Viewer.js 1324/1214. Justified hooks: `const needsAsync = contextOptions.renderer === 'webgpu'` with a WebGPU loading-overlay path and a createViewerAsync wrapper (8 webgpu refs). BUT also `-function Viewer` -> `+class Viewer { constructor }` (line 17->23), relocating the entire body — pickEntity call sites moved from ~line 1355 to ~731. LoadingOverlay.js is a NEW 226-line file (first added in commit 39f5341e64) — legitimately supports the async WebGPU device-init overlay.
allMergedFindings.observation: Category (a) WEBGPU-HOOK (the async path + LoadingOverlay — justified) entangled with (b) class conversion + (d) full body re-indent. The justified change is maybe ~80 lines; the class conversion is responsible for the bulk of the 1324-line diff.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Upstream Viewer.js is `function Viewer` with prototype methods; constructor is synchronous (no async device init needed for WebGL). The WebGPU async path is a real backend requirement — WebGPU device acquisition is async.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: keep-justified for the async path + LoadingOverlay; but the class conversion should have been a separate consideration. Going forward, isolate the WebGPU async hook so a Viewer.js modernization revert wouldn't drop the createViewerAsync logic. LoadingOverlay.js: keep-justified (clean new file).
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified, with one symbol-name correction. The justified WebGPU hook is real: `const needsAsync = contextOptions.renderer === 'webgpu'` with a LoadingOverlay async path (Viewer.js has 8 webgpu refs). LoadingOverlay.js is genuinely a NEW 226-line file (did not exist at merge-base; first added in a stash-WIP commit) that legitimately supports async WebGPU device init—WebGL context creation is sync, WebGPU adapter/device acquisition is async, so this is a real backend requirement. The class conversion is also confirmed (`function Viewer` :396 -> `class Viewer` :397). CORRECTION: the async wrapper is the static method `Viewer.createAsync` (line 2046), NOT `createViewerAsync` as the finding names it—the mechanism is real but the cited symbol is wrong. The finding's thesis (justified ~80-line hook entangled with a full class conversion that dominates the 1324-line diff) holds. Severity medium is appropriate; the justified piece should be kept (see finding 8), the class conversion is the gratuitous part.

allMergedFindings.title: Viewer.js is the ONLY assigned file upstream also modified — active merge-conflict surface in pickEntity + zoomTo JSDoc
allMergedFindings.evidence: git diff 0becdbfc17..upstream/main shows upstream added Cesium3DTileVectorFeature to the import + pickEntity instanceof check, and extended zoomTo/flyTo JSDoc with BufferPrimitiveCollection. Our drift relocated pickEntity call sites (lines 1355->731) and rewrote the surrounding module to a class. The other 5 assigned files (Animation/Timeline/3 inspectors) had ZERO upstream changes in-window.
allMergedFindings.observation: Category cross-cut: our (b) class conversion overlaps upstream's (c) behavioral pickEntity change in the same file. Not a textual conflict in the exact same lines today, but the 100%-reorganized file makes git's 3-way merge fragile — the pickEntity hunk context lines no longer match.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Upstream's pickEntity change (vector feature picking) is a real bug/feature we will WANT to absorb. Our rewrite makes absorbing it manual.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: minimize-diff on Viewer.js to lower the conflict surface, OR plan a manual reconciliation of upstream's pickEntity/Cesium3DTileVectorFeature change at next sync. Track that upstream pickEntity change as a must-port item.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Core claim verified but specific mechanics overstated. Upstream/main vs merge-base touched ONLY Viewer.js among the 6 assigned files (the other 5 had zero upstream changes in-window). Upstream's Viewer.js diff (7+/3-) adds a `Cesium3DTileVectorFeature` import + a `picked instanceof Cesium3DTileVectorFeature` check in the pickEntity helper, plus zoomTo/flyTo JSDoc extended with `BufferPrimitiveCollection`. This is a real feature the fork will want to absorb, so tracking it as a must-port item is correct. HOWEVER the finding's specific relocation claim is misleading: it cites 'pickEntity call sites moved from ~1355 to ~731', but those are diff-hunk line numbers for the constructor's screenSpaceEventHandler call sites, not file lines. The `pickEntity` HELPER function that upstream actually modifies is a module-level function that stayed at file line 104->105—barely moved by the class conversion. So upstream's pickEntity hunk lands in a region our drift left nearly intact; the textual-conflict risk is lower than 'the file is 100% reorganized' implies (the import-block churn is the more real conflict point). Verdict stays confirmed-real because the headline (only upstream-touched assigned file, must-port pickEntity/vector-feature change, class conversion raises merge friction) is accurate; severity medium retained.

allMergedFindings.title: 94% of drifted widgets (34/36) modernized with no WebGPU rationale — systemic codemod scope-creep across the widgets package
allMergedFindings.evidence: Scripted check over all 36 drifted widget .js files: 34 have 0 webgpu/getFeatureRenderer/rendererType/isWebGPU refs in added lines; only Viewer.js (8) and LoadingOverlay.js (2) have any. It maximizes future upstream-sync pain across ~34 files for zero functional benefit, and (per the Animation.js near-miss) carries real regression risk on string-continuation / childNodes-sensitive code.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Upstream maintains all of these as prototype-function modules and continues to evolve them; every one of these 34 files becomes a guaranteed conflict the next time upstream touches it.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: revert-to-upstream for the modernization-only files (everything except Viewer.js + LoadingOverlay.js). Adopt a strict policy: modernize a widget ONLY in the same commit that adds a real WebGPU hook or fixes a real bug there. The current blanket sweep contradicts CLAUDE.md's own 'never modernize a file you're not otherwise touching' rule.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified by scripted enumeration. Exactly 36 widget .js files drifted vs merge-base; only 2 (Viewer.js with 8 refs, LoadingOverlay.js with 2 refs) have any webgpu/getFeatureRenderer/rendererType/isWebGPU references in their ADDED lines. The other 34 (BaseLayerPicker, Geocoder, SceneModePicker, ProjectionPicker, InfoBox, SelectionIndicator, etc.) have zero. allMergedFindings.title: Modernization sweep added new JSDoc/comment blocks, violating CLAUDE.md 'Do NOT add new JSDoc' rule
allMergedFindings.evidence: Whitespace-stripped diff of Cesium3DTilesInspectorViewModel shows the codemod reflowed/relocated JSDoc blocks around the new method members (e.g. togglePickTileset/toggleInspector/toggleTileset getters wrapped with /** ... */). 'Toggles the pick tileset mode' did exist upstream (count=1), so it's reflow not net-new in that case, but the class conversion reshuffles comment placement throughout.
allMergedFindings.observation: Category (d) REFORMAT-NOISE. CLAUDE.md Comment rules: 'Do NOT add new JSDoc that didn't exist in the original' and 'Preserve ALL existing JSDoc when modernizing.' The codemod's comment relocation muddies which JSDoc is original vs fork-added and adds noise to the diff.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Upstream's JSDoc sits on prototype-assigned getters via Object.defineProperties; placement is stable.
allMergedFindings.recommendation: minimize-diff. If modernization is reverted (recommended above) this is moot. If kept, ensure no net-new JSDoc was introduced and comment placement matches upstream intent.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Partially verified; downgraded in force. In Cesium3DTilesInspectorViewModel the `/**` block count went 74->77 (net +3), confirming the codemod did not merely reflow but introduced new JSDoc blocks. allMergedFindings.title: createViewerAsync + LoadingOverlay is the correct pattern for WebGPU async init — keep as the model for justified widget drift
allMergedFindings.evidence: Viewer.js adds `const needsAsync = contextOptions.renderer === 'webgpu'; if (!needsAsync) return new Viewer(...)` then an async path with a LoadingOverlay during device acquisition. LoadingOverlay.js is a clean new 226-line module. This is a real backend requirement (WebGPU adapter/device requests are async, WebGL context creation is sync).
allMergedFindings.observation: Category (a) WEBGPU-HOOK — the one clearly justified piece of widget drift in the whole bucket. It is implemented as a reusable helper + new file rather than an inline hack, matching CLAUDE.md's 'real reusable artifact, not inline shortcut' guidance.
allMergedFindings.webglComparison: Upstream Viewer construction is synchronous; no async overlay exists because WebGL needs none. This is additive, not a behavioral change to the WebGL path (WebGL still returns `new Viewer(...)` synchronously).
allMergedFindings.recommendation: keep-justified. Use this as the template for any future widget drift: isolate the WebGPU-specific code behind a renderer check and a co-located helper/file, and do NOT bundle a package-wide modernization sweep with it.
allMergedFindings.verifyReasoning: Verified as a correct, necessary WebGPU-specific addition, not drift to be reverted. Viewer.createAsync (line 2046) gates on `contextOptions.renderer === 'webgpu'`, returns `new Viewer(...)` synchronously for the WebGL path (no behavioral change to WebGL), and only takes the async LoadingOverlay path for WebGPU—because WebGPU adapter/device acquisition is genuinely async while WebGL context creation is sync. LoadingOverlay.js is a clean co-located new 226-line module, matching CLAUDE.md's 'real reusable artifact, not inline shortcut' guidance. This pattern is also referenced in migration_doc/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md (the cross-backend runner flips `new Cesium.Viewer(` -> `await Cesium.Viewer.createAsync(` for WebGPU). Note: the finding names it 'createViewerAsync' but the actual symbol is the static `Viewer.createAsync`—cosmetic naming error only. This is the one clearly justified piece of widget drift; keep-justified. Severity low (it is a positive/keep recommendation, not a defect).
